title: Texas Tech coach Joey McGuire: We'll definitely look at adding a player cut by an NFL team
summary: "I know this: I get to keep my job if I win, and so I'm gonna constantly look at how we can be better as a team, and be better roster-wise," McGuire said.
full_text: ''' The Big Ten and SEC have passed rules saying players who have been under contract with NFL teams are not eligible to play in either conference . But the Big 12 has no such rule, and Texas Tech coach Joey McGuire says he'll look into adding a player who was in an NFL training camp but didn't make the final roster. "We've been monitoring, for the last week or so, how we can add, if possible, somebody to make this team better," McGuire said. "We haven't called any NFL coaches. We haven't scouted any NFL players, that I think some teams have done, but we're definitely gonna look." Two players who were cut by NFL teams this month, tight end Dae'Quan Wright and defensive tackle Zxavian Harris, had agreed to play for LSU this season, reuniting them with coach Lane Kiffin, who coached them both at Ole Miss last year. The new SEC rule would seem to preclude them from going to LSU, but wouldn't preclude Texas Tech from adding them — unless the Big 12 adopts the same rule. McGuire said he's unsure whether the Big 12 will do that. "You know what's coming next: Those players are gonna sue the conference. So what do you do? I was checking with our guys today, what's the Big 12 gonna do? It's going to be interesting," McGuire said. NCAA teams are allowed to have up to 105 players on their rosters. McGuire said he currently has one roster spot available and won't kick anyone off the team to make room for a new player, so Texas Tech would only add one former NFL player to the team. "If we add anybody, it'd be one," McGuire said. "We're not gonna have to ask anybody to leave or anything like that. We have a spot, and if we can find the right guy to make this team better, we'll use it." Texas Tech has already become a symbol for the chaos that pervades college football, after the school backed quarterback Brendan Sorsby's attempt to get his NCAA eligibility back after a gambling suspension. Sorsby ultimately gave up his NCAA eligibility, was denied in his attempt to enter the NFL supplemental draft, and will not play football at any level this season while awaiting the 2027 NFL draft. McGuire is unapologetic about Texas Tech's ambitions to acquire talented players any way it can. "I know this: I get to keep my job if I win, and so I'm gonna constantly look at how we can be better as a team, and be better roster-wise," McGuire said. Given McGuire's comments, it should come as no surprise if some player who was in an NFL training camp this summer is playing for Texas Tech this fall.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Dave Canales: Bryce Young is our franchise QB right now, contract is up to front office
summary: Young is eligible for a second contract but does not yet have one.
full_text: Bryce Young is the Panthers' franchise quarterback right now. Whether he will remain the Panthers' franchise quarterback for years to come depends on whether he and the team agree to a long-term contract extension. So far, that hasn't happened. In an interview with Stephen A. Smith , Panthers head coach Dave Canales was asked this question about Young: "Is he your franchise quarterback?" Canales answered, "He is right now." Canales then went on to praise the way Young has developed, from a first overall pick who looked like he was in over his head as a rookie in 2023, to a struggling quarterback who got benched two games into his second season in 2024, to a player who led his team to the playoffs in 2025. "He's our guy. He's our guy, and I love the trajectory that he's on," Canales said of Young. "And not just the stuff that he's growing in, from just an operational standpoint, moving the offense, finding chemistry and all that, but it's also just the critical moments. It's those games, it's the close games, it's the one-score game at the end. Whether we're up or down, I love having Bryce out there. I love that he stays cool, calm and collected and aggressive, and he attacks at the right time. So, all those things are pointing in the right direction." So why is Young only the franchise quarterback "right now"? Why haven't the Panthers committed to him with a long-term contract extension? Canales isn't the person to answer those questions. Panthers General Manager Dan Morgan and Executive VP of Football Operations Brandt Tilis will handle negotiations on a second contract for Young. "I'll just let the rest of the stuff just sort itself out, with all the conversations with his whole group and party and our front office here with Dan and Brandt working that part out," Canales said. "But for me, especially now not calling plays, I get to just enjoy this road, help him improve on a daily basis." The Panthers picked up Young's fifth-year option, which means he is under contract through 2027, with a guaranteed salary of $25.9 million next season. But a true commitment to Young from the Panthers would mean a second contract guaranteeing him a lot more than $25.9 million, for a lot longer than the next two years. Right now, Young doesn't have that.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Commanders sell gear with abandoned name, logo at team store
summary: The Commanders' former name and logo are gone.
full_text: The Commanders' former name and logo are gone. Unless they aren't. As explained by Eric Flack of WUSA, the Commanders are selling in their team store gear containing both the name and the logo . The Commanders have insisted that the name and the logo are gone for good. They told Flack that they're using both on a limited basis in order to preserve their trademark rights. And they stress that none of it means they'll be going back to either. Still, it feels as if the Commanders are periodically dipping a toe a little deeper into the water regarding the possibility of bringing back both. Or maybe they've decided to pander, just a bit, to fans who want the old name and logo to return. Without researching the niceties of copyright law, it seems possible to shelve trademarks indefinitely without making it open season on the protected name and logo. And if they're truly never going back to the name and the logo, why do they care about preserving the trademark rights? That fact alone suggests they're reserving the right to bring both back — at the right time.
author: Mike Florio

title: Giants trade OG Joshua Ezeudu to the Chiefs
summary: The Giants traded offensive guard Joshua Ezeudu to the Chiefs on Tuesday night, Mike Garafolo of NFL Media reports.
full_text: The Giants traded offensive guard Joshua Ezeudu to the Chiefs on Tuesday night, Mike Garafolo of NFL Media reports. New York will get a 2028 seventh-rounder in return. Ezeudu, 26, was listed on the team's depth chart as the backup to Jermaine Eluemunor at right tackle, but coach John Harbaugh had said Ezeudu would train in multiple spots. The Giants selected Ezeudu in the third round of the 2022 draft. A calf injury sidelined Ezeudu for all of 2025, but he has appeared in 33 games, with 10 starts. The Chiefs wanted depth in the interior of their offensive line, especially at right guard behind Trey Smith.
author: Charean Williams

title: Kyle Shanahan: Jed York's arrest "has no effect on us"
summary: Shanahan insists owners legal issue won't be a distraction.
full_text: It's been a bizarre couple of months for the 49ers, with the most bizarre development happening on Monday, when team owner Jed York pleaded no contest to a pair of charges arising from an effort to solicit prostitution. Coach Kyle Shanahan was asked about the situation by reporters on Tuesday. "I got to talk to Jed the last two days and today," Shanahan said. "Obviously, it's a very tough situation. I mean, views for the organization going forward is the same as usual. There won't be any difference in that, but I know it's extremely fresh. I think it's a very, very personal situation. I’ve got a lot of respect for Jed. I got a lot of respect for Danielle [York]. Their family does mean a lot to me. So, with it being this personal, I'm trying as hard as I can to keep it that way.” Shanahan added that the situation is "irrelevant" to players, especially since York has been living in Ohio and absent from training camp. "From a football standpoint, it has no effect on us," Shanahan said. "As far as what we do day-to-day, what we talk about. It hasn’t been mentioned in a meeting today, it doesn't have to do with what happens on the field. Everything outside of there, I think you guys can judge that better than me.” He insists that the York arrest won't be a distraction. "Well, the one thing that went on yesterday, I don't think pertained to our players much," Shanahan said. "And if you guys talk about me getting in a car accident, I think that's kind of a joke that people think that's a distraction to our team. So, I think it's been training camp as usual.” Right, but it's one thing for an absentee owner to get arrested. It surely was a distraction, and a disruption, for the 49ers to not have Shanahan at full capacity in the early stages of training camp. As to York, the fact that Shanahan was asked several questions about it on Tuesday necessarily makes it a distraction. Even if there's no reason to believe it will be a disruption.
author: Mike Florio

title: Christian Gonzalez: Contract talks are "frustrating"
summary: As the regular season approaches, the Patriots and cornerback Christian Gonzalez still don't have a new contract in place.
full_text: As the regular season approaches, the Patriots and cornerback Christian Gonzalez still don't have a new contract in place. And Gonzalez is feeling the burden of the negotiations. " I mean, it’s frustrating ," Gonzalez told reporters on Tuesday, via Michael Hurley of NBC Sports Boston. "But I mean it's -- I'm focused on the season. I'm focused on here now and doing what I gotta do, and I'm out here to compete and get better." Gonzalez also sidestepped the chatter that his recent absence from practice related to his contract talks, which will only reinforce the perception that it was contract related. "Yeah, you know, I'm not going to get into that," Gonzalez said. "I'm out here now, so it is what it is. . . . Everything we do is speculating, at the end of the day. I could say something and then it's still gonna be speculated, so I mean, it is what it is." Gonzalez didn't get into the specifics as to what he wants in a new deal. "There's certain things that go into a contract that my team knows what we want, so it kind of depends how you put it," Gonzalez said. The reality is that the contract signed 10 days ago by Seahawks cornerback Devon Witherspoon, which pushed the new-money bar for the position to $33 million per year, should provide the template for Gonzalez's deal. The fact that the Gonzalez deal still isn't done shows that it's not nearly that simple. Either way, Gonzalez is under contract for two more years. And the real question is whether Gonzalez, who is back at practice, will step away again as Week 1 approaches. And, frankly, he should. Tuesday's news regarding CTE underscores the risks of playing football at a high level. All players should do whatever they can to get whatever they deserve. If they don't get it, they shouldn't play.
author: Mike Florio

title: SEC, Big 10 block return of NFL players to member schools
summary: The chaos in college football is only getting more chaotic.
full_text: The chaos in college football is only getting more chaotic. With the courts opening the door for players from the high school class of 2022 to return for a fifth year of college football, the two most powerful college-football conferences have slammed the door on players who have signed NFL contracts. First on Tuesday, it was the Big Ten. "The Big Ten Conference announced Tuesday the unanimous adoption of a conference rule to prohibit football players who have signed a professional contract, were on a professional roster at any point or declared for the NFL Draft as an underclassman without withdrawing, from maintaining eligibility for athletic competition at a conference institution," the conference announced. "The conference continues to evaluate potential rules restricting professional athletes in other sports from conference competition." Later in the day, the SEC followed suit. "An SEC institution is not permitted to have an athlete on its roster who has: (1) previously declared for the NFL, NBA, or WNBA raft, and did not appropriately withdraw; (2) signed a contract with an NFL (or other professional football league), NBA/G-League, or WNBA (or affiliate) team; or (3) been listed on an NFL (or other professional football league), NBA/G-League, or WNBA (or affiliate) roster. The Commissioner is authorized to enforce this expectation with penalties against member institutions." The SEC's move could set up a showdown with LSU, which intends to add former Browns tight end Dae'Quan Wright to the roster. It also arguably defies the injunction granting another year of eligibility to Wright and other athletes, setting the stage for further litigation. However it goes, the conferences are obviously seizing on a widely-unpopular development in college sports in an effort to create sufficient political momentum to persuade Congress to pass the Protect College Sports Act — which will directly give college programs an antitrust exemption and indirectly pick the pockets, and reduce the freedoms, of college players. Good luck getting anyone connected to the college football money machine to admit this objective. It's all about screaming that the sky is falling, without giving serious consideration to the impacts of the effort to get the federal government to solve the problem that decades of a corrupt system created.
author: Mike Florio

title: With Aaron Donald undecided, Rams prepping for 53-player rosters with and without him
summary: The Rams open the season in 16 days, and defensive tackle Aaron Donald still has not reached a decision about his return.
full_text: The Rams open the season in 16 days, and defensive tackle Aaron Donald still has not reached a decision about his return. Will he or won't he? Time is running out. Coach Sean McVay, who has said he didn't want to place a deadline on Donald, said the team has plans for a final 53-player roster with Donald and one without Donald. “If he decides he wants to be able to do it, then the next conversations are: What is your ramp-up ?” McVay said Tuesday, via Benjamin Royer of the ocregister.com. “What does it look like to approach whenever that would be the first time that we think we make the most sense for him to impact and make a positive change with us? “We’ve had to have a lot of fluidity and flexibility, and that’s what I’ve had to learn over 10 years. But I think what’s good is the thing that has served us well – and it’s really the truth – is let’s just stay one day at a time.” The three-time Defensive Player of the Year began considering a comeback after the Rams traded for two-time Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett. Donald has not played in the NFL since 2023.
author: Charean Williams

title: J.J. McCarthy, Carson Wentz split second-team reps on Tuesday
summary: If McCarthy slips to No. 3, he could be gone by Sunday's roster cuts.
full_text: After losing the starting quarterback job to Kyler Murray, J.J. McCarthy could be losing the backup spot, too. Via Kevin Seifert of ESPN, McCarthy and Carson Wentz split second-team reps during an 80-minute practice on Tuesday. McCarthy, who fell to No. 2 in the days before the preseason opener, has not performed well in a pair of exhibition games. He continues to have accuracy issues, and he continues to overuse his fastball when making throws. Wentz was a capable backup in 2025 for the Vikings, despite not signing until late August. With a full offseason, training camp, and preseason in the system, Wentz would be in even better position to fill in for Murray, if necessary. With Max Brosmer also on the roster, McCarthy could be in danger of not being on the roster by Sunday, when the rosters reduce to 53. The Vikings undoubtedly would try to trade him, since the balance of his 2026 pay ($1.075 million) and all of his 2027 compensation ($3.775 million) are fully guaranteed. The Vikings may have to pay a significant chunk of the money in order to facilitate a deal. Ultimately, the Vikings may have to simply waive McCarthy. However it plays out, it's not looking good for McCarthy in Minnesota. It will be interesting to see whether and to what extent McCarthy plays in the preseason finale against the Broncos.
author: Mike Florio

title: Dae'Quan Wright clears waivers, paving way to join LSU
summary: Dae'Quan Wright is going back to school.
full_text: Dae'Quan Wright is going back to school. The former Browns tight end cleared waivers on Tuesday, via Adam Schefter of ESPN. Wright now has a clear path to return to college football. He plans to play for LSU. If Wright had been claimed, he would have been unable to play college football. The standard NFL contract, which would have been absorbed by the team claiming it, prevents a player from playing football for anyone else. The move raises future questions. What if an NFL team offers him a roster spot during the 2026 season, while he's playing for LSU? Can he be signed after the 2026 LSU season ends? Will he have to re-enter the draft in 2027, or does he remain a free agent? The questions are unprecedented, because the situation is. And if the NFL doesn't already have rules to cover this situation, it needs to figure something out.
author: Mike Florio

title: Myles Garrett remains out of Rams' practice
summary: Rams pass rusher Myles Garrett remained out of practice Tuesday, the 12th practice he has missed with minor knee swelling.
full_text: Rams pass rusher Myles Garrett remained out of practice Tuesday, the 12th practice he has missed with minor knee swelling. Yet, Rams coach Sean McVay continues to downplay the two-time Defensive Player of the Year's absence. “The goal is, what can we do to be able to get him ready to roll for Australia?” McVay said, via Benjamin Royer of the ocregister.com. Garrett played all 17 games each of the past two seasons with the Browns, and he has missed only four games over the past six seasons. Garrett, who the Rams acquired in a blockbuster offseason trade with the Browns, set the NFL's single-season sacks record with 23 last season. He has 125.5 sacks in his nine NFL seasons. Wide receiver Puka Nacua (hip flexor) and offensive lineman Keagen Trost (hamstring) also did not practice on Tuesday. Tight end Terrance Ferguson worked on the side with an athletic trainer, and offensive lineman Alaric Jackson missed practice for a personal matter that McVay said is "nothing to worry about."
author: Charean Williams

title: Texans to sign DE Derek Parish
summary: The Texans lost defensive end Dylan Horton to a torn Achilles this week and they made a move to help fill in for him on Tuesday.
full_text: The Texans lost defensive end Dylan Horton to a torn Achilles this week and they made a move to help fill in for him on Tuesday. Adam Schefter of ESPN reports that they are signing Derek Parish to their 90-man roster. The NFL's daily transaction report doesn't have word about that move, but does show that Horton and linebacker Marte Mapu have been placed on injured reserve. Parish was a 2023 seventh-round pick of the Jaguars, but never played in any games for the team. He played for Toronto in the CFL and then moved on to the UFL's DC Defenders this spring. Parish had 23 tackles, four tackles for loss, three sacks and a forced fumble for the Defenders.
author: Josh Alper

title: Commanders sign OT D.J. Humphries to a one-year deal
summary: The Commanders signed offensive tackle D.J.
full_text: The Commanders signed offensive tackle D.J. Humphries to a one-year deal, according to multiple reports. Humphries worked out for the team earlier in the day. The Commanders needed help at the position with starting left tackle Laremy Tunsil out with a torn triceps. Humphries, 32, appeared in eight games for the Rams last season, with one start, and he has started 101 career games. The Cardinals drafted him in the first round in 2015. He made two starts for the Chiefs in 2024.
author: Charean Williams

title: Dolphins claim WR Ryan Miller off waivers
summary: The Dolphins added a wide receiver to the roster on Tuesday.
full_text: '' The Dolphins added a wide receiver to the roster on Tuesday. They announced that they have claimed Ryan Miller off of waivers. The Giants waived Miller on Monday. Miller's time with the Giants ended without him appearing in any regular season games. He was claimed off of waivers from the Bucs last December and re-signed with the team in April. Miller had 14 receptions for 162 yards and three touchdowns in 25 games with the Bucs over three seasons. The Dolphins created room for Miller in Miami by waiving wide receiver Tahj Washington. The 2024 Dolphins seventh-round pick had three catches for 37 yards last season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Seahawks place S Bud Clark, OL Mason Richman on IR
summary: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said on Sunday that safety Bud Clark and offensive lineman Mason Richman would miss extended time after suffering injuries in Seattle's preseason game against the Titans.
full_text: ' Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said on Sunday that safety Bud Clark and offensive lineman Mason Richman would miss extended time after suffering injuries in Seattle's preseason game against the Titans. We learned just how much time they'll miss on Tuesday. Clark and Richman were both placed on injured reserve, which means they'll be ineligible to return to action during the regular season. Clark was a second-round pick this year and he broke his ankle on Sunday night. Richman was a 2025 seventh-round pick and he went down with an undisclosed lower body injury. The Seahawks signed offensive tackle Derrick Graham, safety Tysheem Johnson and running back Justin Jones in other moves.
author: Josh Alper

title: Lions place LB Damone Clark on IR, sign C Gus Hartwig
summary: The Lions placed veteran linebacker Damone Clark on injured reserve on Tuesday, the team announced.
full_text: The Lions placed veteran linebacker Damone Clark on injured reserve on Tuesday, the team announced. Clark had an undisclosed injury early in training camp that will keep him out for the season. The Lions signed Clark as depth at the position behind Derrick Barnes and Malcolm Rodriguez, but Clark's injury prompted the team to sign veteran Devin White. In a corresponding move, the Lions signed center Gus Hartwig. Hartwig went undrafted in 2025, signing with the Jets. He spent his rookie season on injured reserve with a leg injury. The Jets waived him after the offseason program. Center Cade Mays is out with a wrist injury and backup Michael Niese injured his leg in Saturday's preseason game. The Lions might be without safety Thomas Harper in the preseason finale against the Colts as he deals with an ankle injury.
author: Charean Williams

title: Sam LaPorta returned to practice on Tuesday
summary: The Lions got one of their key offensive players back on the field on Tuesday.
full_text: ''' The Lions got one of their key offensive players back on the field on Tuesday. Via Dave Birkett of the Detroit Free Press , tight end Sam LaPorta returned to practice after missing less than a week with a hip injury. Head coach Dan Campbell had said that he wasn’t sure if LaPorta’s injury would linger into the regular season. But LaPorta took part in individual and team drills on Tuesday. LaPorta caught 40 passes for 489 yards with three touchdowns in 2025. He missed much of the season due to a back injury. Additionally, guard Ben Bartch returned to practice after missing last week and linebacker Trevor Nowaske exited practice early with an apparent knee injury.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Vikings WR Jeshaun Jones suspended three games
summary: Wide receiver Jeshaun Jones will find out whether he makes the cut to 53 players in Minnesota later this week, but he won't be playing in any of the team's first three games either way.
full_text: Wide receiver Jeshaun Jones will find out whether he makes the cut to 53 players in Minnesota later this week, but he won't be playing in any of the team's first three games either way. The NFL announced that Jones has been suspended for three games on Tuesday. The ban comes as a result of a violation of the league's substance abuse policy. Jones signed with the Vikings after going undrafted in 2024 and he has spent the last two seasons on the team's practice squad. He was elevated to play in Week 18 last season and returned two punts for five yards. Jones will be able to practice this week and play in the preseason finale before his suspension takes effect. The Vikings will set their initial 53-man roster by Sunday afternoon.
author: Josh Alper

title: Patrick Mahomes plans to "go out there and be myself" Week One
summary: Mahomes expects to play against the Broncos in the Monday Night Football opener.
full_text: Patrick Mahomes expects to play when the Chiefs take the field for the first Monday Night Football game of the season, September 14 against the Broncos. Mahomes noted that he was told when he tore his ACL last year that it would be a nine-month recovery, and the Chiefs' opener is nine months to the day since he suffered the injury. "It's nine months," Mahomes said, via ESPN. "It's the amount of time [doctors] said from the beginning, that if I did everything the right way, I would be ready to play Week One. I'm someone that, if you put [a goal] out in front of me, I want to go out and get it and maximize every single opportunity, every rep in the weight room, every hour that I can spend in the building to get my body right. This has always been the plan. From the day I got the surgery, as quick as I did, to hopefully the first game of the year, the plan will go accordingly, and I’ll be able to go out there and be myself ." Mahomes hasn't been playing in the preseason, but the games have been getting his competitive juices flowing. He said he was pumped up by Chiefs kicker Harrison Butker hitting a 69-yard field goal in a preseason game. "I just love football," Mahomes said. "It's such a cool sport. It takes everybody. Him hitting that field goal, I was as excited, I think, as he was, seeing your teammates succeed. I want to have fun and just enjoy being out there on the field again. I was pretty excited about that." Chiefs fans will be excited to see Mahomes step onto the field at Arrowhead Stadium in Week One.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Under "Joe" alias, Jed York allegedly contacted prostitution ad multiple times
summary: More details inevitably will emerge regarding 49ers owner Jed York's recent arrest, and lickety-split no-contest plea, in Ohio.
full_text: More details inevitably will emerge regarding 49ers owner Jed York's recent arrest, and lickety-split no-contest plea, in Ohio. None will make things better. If anything, extra facts will make it all look worse. Case in point: Per the California Post , York pinged a dummy ad for a prostitution service multiple times before arranging a Sunday-morning dalliance. The first attempt happened the prior day. He reportedly used an alias: Joe. “York messaged the female and advised that his name was Joe and that he would like to visit the female,” detectives wrote in an official document, per the Post. Later on Saturday, York “advised that he was just checking in, and was seeing if the female was available." After receiving no reply, York tried again at 9:11 a.m. ET on Sunday morning. Per the official report, York “asked if the female was free, and that he would love to come see her." He said he was driving from Boardman to East Palestine, and he asked the woman to “shoot him an address.” He then reportedly asked for the charge for one hour. York was told the price was $160, with a $20 surcharge for unprotected sex. He agreed to pay $160, and he said he was on his way to a fictitious lot number at the trailer park. (The owner of the trailer park has claimed that addresses in the park were not used for the sting operation; this new information obviously contradicts that.) The arrest happened at the trailer park at 9:35 a.m. ET. York had $160 in cash, and a test text message confirmed that his iPhone was the one used to arrange the encounter. He was driving an AVIS rental car. York has said nothing since the arrest and plea to misdemeanor charges of disorderly conduct and possession of criminal tools. He received a sentence of two days in jail and a $1,150 fine. The NFL is reviewing the case under the Personal Conduct Policy. The league's owners are due to meet in Atlanta on Wednesday.
author: Mike Florio

title: Commanders release OL Foster Sarell
summary: The Commanders have let go of an offensive lineman.
full_text: The Commanders have let go of an offensive lineman. Washington announced on Tuesday that the club has released offensive tackle Foster Sarell. Sarell, 27, joined the Commanders in March for his second stint with the club. He previously as with Washington for the offseason program and training camp last year before he did not make the 53-man roster. Sarell has also spent time with the Ravens, Giants, and Chargers. But he’s only appeared in games with Los Angeles, making 41 appearances with four starts over the last four seasons.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Kellen Moore confirms RB Ty Chandler has season-ending knee injury
summary: Saints running back Ty Chandler will miss the entire season with a knee injury, coach Kellen Moore confirmed Tuesday.
full_text: Saints running back Ty Chandler will miss the entire season with a knee injury, coach Kellen Moore confirmed Tuesday. Chandler was injured during the preseason game against the Rams. With Alvin Kamara sidelined with an MCL sprain and Devin Neal dealing with a hamstring injury, the Saints traded for running back Zamir White this week. Chandler spent the past four seasons with the Vikings but played only three games last season. The Saints placed Chandler and tight end Moliki Matavao on season-ending injured reserve Tuesday. Moore offered better news about wide receiver Chris Olave, who left practice early after a hard landing on a deep pass. Moore said Olave is "all good."
author: Charean Williams

title: Bears RT Darnell Wright left practice with possible elbow injury
summary: Bears right tackle Darnell Wright's health is a concern after his early departure from practice on Tuesday.
full_text: ''' Bears right tackle Darnell Wright's health is a concern after his early departure from practice on Tuesday. Per reporters at the team's practice, Wright had his right elbow checked out by members of the team's medical staff before exiting for the rest of the session. Wright tore the UCL in the same elbow last year, but played through the injury with a brace on his arm. Wright played well enough to land a second-team All-Pro spot at the end of the year, so the Bears will be hoping that nothing that happened on Tuesday will keep him off the field come the regular season. Reporters also noted the departures of defensive tackle Gervon Dexter and defensive back Dontae Manning during practice.
author: Josh Alper

title: Ja'Marr Chase says he's "fine" after hyperextending his knee
summary: Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase gave the team a scare at practice on Tuesday, but it looks like that's all it was.
full_text: '' Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase gave the team a scare at practice on Tuesday, but it looks like that's all it was. Chase landed awkwardly while trying to catch a pass and limped off the field without assistance from the medical staff. Chase spoke to trainers, but never left the field and he gave a positive update on how he's feeling during a radio interview after practice. Chase said on 1530 ESPN that he felt he could have returned to practice, but the team "pulled me" out of caution. “A little hyperextension , but other than that I’m fine,” Chase said. The Bengals' caution could extend to limiting Chase's practice time in the coming days, but it does not sound like there should be much reason to worry about his availablity for the start of the regular season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Bucs sign rookie WR Matthew Henry
summary: The Buccaneers signed rookie wide receiver Matthew Henry on Tuesday, the team announced.
full_text: The Buccaneers signed rookie wide receiver Matthew Henry on Tuesday, the team announced. In a corresponding move, the Bucs placed rookie defensive lineman Deshawn McKnight on injured reserve. McKnight injured a hamstring in the team's preseason win over the Chiefs on Saturday night. Henry finished his collegiate tenure last year at Western Kentucky after previous stops at Western Illinois and Livingstone College. He started all 13 games for the Hilltoppers in 2025, hauling in 55 passes for 888 yards and six touchdowns. He was named to the All-Conference USA second team. After going undrafted in April, he participated in rookie minicamps with the Titans and 49ers. The Bucs need help at the position to get through the final week of the preseason. Wideouts Emeka Egbuka (toe), Jalen McMillan (knee) and Tez Johnson (groin) all have missed practice time this week.
author: Charean Williams

title: Patriots don't view Week 1 as a deadline for a Christian Gonzalez deal
summary: Cornerback Christian Gonzalez returned to the practice field on Monday, but there hasn't been any sign that a contract extension with the team is imminent.
full_text: Cornerback Christian Gonzalez returned to the practice field on Monday, but there hasn't been any sign that a contract extension with the team is imminent. Gonzalez had not practiced for a couple of weeks due to what the team said was an injury, but others wondered if the ongoing negotiations on an extension played a role in the decision. At a Tuesday press conference, Patriots executive vice president of player personnel Eliot Wolf said there's "nothing new" to report on the contract front and that the two sides are "continuing to work with his representation to find a resolution that works for everyone." Wolf also said that neither side has set Week 1 of the regular season as a deadline to wrap up an agreement, but declined to say if he's confident that they'll come to an agreement. "I’m confident we’re continuing to work on it, and we’re positive that we’re making momentum," Wolf said, via a transcript from the team. The agreement that Devon Witherspoon reached with the Seahawks earlier this month was seen as a potential stepping stone toward a deal between the Patriots and Gonzalez, but it hasn't played out that way and the clock is ticking for something to get done before the two corners are on opposite sides of the field on September 9.
author: Josh Alper

title: Broncos agree to terms with OLB Ron Stone, cut WR Hakeem Butler
summary: The Broncos agreed to terms with outside linebacker Ron Stone Jr., Parker Gabriel of The Denver Post reports.
full_text: The Broncos agreed to terms with outside linebacker Ron Stone Jr., Parker Gabriel of The Denver Post reports. In a corresponding move, the Broncos released wide receiver Hakeem Butler. Both Stone and Butler played in the UFL this spring. With the Columbus Aviators, Stone recorded 5.5 sacks and five tackles for loss. In the spring of 2025, he played for the Michigan Panthers and totaled 3.5 sacks and four tackles for loss. Stone, 26, signed with the Raiders as an undrafted free agent in 2024. Las Vegas waived him with an injury designation at the roster cutdowns.
author: Charean Williams

title: Klint Kubiak: Ashton Jeanty is on the mend
summary: The Raiders HC did not say much about Jeanty's injury after the RB exited Sunday's practice early.
full_text: ' The injury to Ashton Jeanty was apparently not as serious as initially feared, as it was reported that he was diagnosed with a sprained ankle after going down during practice over the weekend. In his Tuesday press conference, head coach Klint Kubiak declined to give any specifics about Jeanty or the nature of his injury, saying simply that Jeanty is " on the mend ." When asked as a follow up if there has been discussion about Jeanty possibly starting the season on injured reserve, Kubiak again said only that Jeanty is "on the mend." He did, however, give a clue that Jeanty's injury is not too serious when he smiled and noted "the power of prayer," in reference to the team coming together, taking a knee, and sharing a moment after Jeanty left the field. Jeanty did not practice on Tuesday. If the Raiders were to put Jeanty on injured reserve at the time of roster cuts, then he would be eligible to return after four weeks.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Kyle Shanahan hoping Nick Bosa will practice next week
summary: 49ers defensive end Nick Bosa has not practiced since August 3 because of pain in his surgically repaired right knee, but 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan hopes to see him on the practice field soon.
full_text: 49ers defensive end Nick Bosa has not practiced since August 3 because of pain in his surgically repaired right knee, but 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan hopes to see him on the practice field soon. Shanahan said today that Bosa is improving, and should be back at practice next week. NFL players get a mandatory three days off after the end of the preseason and then the 49ers will have three practices before leaving for Australia for the season opener against the Rams, and Shanahan wants to see Bosa at those three practices. "He's doing good. Hoping he can get into practice next week. We'll see how those three days go after the mandatory three days off," Shanahan said. Bosa suffered a torn ACL in his right knee in Week Three of last season. He previously missed most of the 2020 season after tearing his left ACL.
author: Michael David Smith

title: NFLPA sends email to all players after new CTE study
summary: The impact of a medical study can be assessed in part by the reaction to it.
full_text: The impact of a medical study can be assessed in part by the reaction to it. The NFL Players Association reacted swiftly and strongly on Tuesday to the new CTE study , sending an email regarding the study to all players, and to all player agents. The full text of the message appears below: "As members of this union, protecting your health and safety is one of our core priorities. Every day, we are focused on improving player safety on the field and supporting healthier lives long after football. "Today, Massachusetts General Brigham and Boston University released a new study examining the prevalence of CTE among NFL players. The findings are a sobering reminder that football carries serious risks that can have lasting consequences for players and their families. "In short, the study suggests that CTE may be significantly more common among NFL players than previously understood, reinforcing the importance of continued research, care, and support. "We understand that studies like this can create concern for you and your loved ones. At the same time, they should not diminish hope. "While CTE can only be definitively diagnosed after death, many symptoms commonly associated with CTE, including memory challenges, mood changes, depression, anxiety, sleep disturbances, and cognitive difficulties, may also be caused by other medical or neurological conditions, many of which can be treated or managed. That is why a thorough medical evaluation is so important. "According to Dr. Daniel Daneshvar, one of the lead researchers on the study, 'Many of the symptoms associated with CTE are treatable with the right care.' He stressed that, 'While we don’t have a cure yet, we have seen improvements in players who receive care from doctors specializing in neurodegenerative disease and who know how to treat athletes. No one should walk away thinking there's nothing they can do.' "Research continues to improve our understanding of brain health and identify new ways to support players. That is why the NFLPA has made major investments in brain health research and care with leading institutions such as the American Brain Foundation and the Football Players Health Study at Harvard University. "We also provide resources for former players through our Former Players Department, the Professional Athletes Foundation, and the Trust, offering comprehensive evaluations, wellness support, care navigation, and treatment resources. "These findings should serve as a call to action across the entire football ecosystem. We all share a responsibility to advance research, improve access to care, develop better treatments, and support those affected by the long-term impacts of the game. While we have learned a great deal over the past two decades, there is more work to do. "Pay attention to your cognitive, neurological, and overall health. If you have concerns, seek evaluation and support. Early intervention matters. Resources are available today that can help. "We'll also host calls with medical experts over the next two weeks to provide additional context and answer questions. More details will be shared in the coming days." The key words are "call to action." The information should prompt everyone associated with football to work zealously to make the game safer, to strive for advances in technology that will minimize concussions and/or the effects of them, that will make it possible to spot CTE in living patients, and that will support former players who fear the inevitability of cognitive problems.
author: Mike Florio

title: Commanders to sign former Pro Bowl LT D.J. Humphries after Laremy Tunsil injury
summary: Washington reversed course and sought outside help after Tunsil underwent surgery to repair a torn triceps
full_text:
Depth is on the way to the Washington Commanders ' offensive line. The Commanders are set to sign former Pro Bowl left tackle D.J. Humphries to a one-year contract, according to ESPN , which bolsters a unit that recently lost its greatest asset, Laremy Tunsil , to a torn triceps. Tunsil is expected to miss most of the 2026 season .
Humphries is available to the Commanders as a free agent. It has been half a decade since Humphries was considered one of the best tackles in football, and in the four years since his Pro Bowl selection, he played more than eight games just once.
Unable to recreate the high level of production that came in his stellar 2021 campaign, Humphries is now set to play for his fourth team in the last four years. He played two games with the Kansas City Chiefs in 2024 and was most recently a member of the Los Angeles Rams , for whom he suited up in eight games last year.
Tunsil, meanwhile, suffered his torn triceps during practice on Aug. 8 while attempting to block a bull rush from edge rusher Odafe Oweh . He required surgery for the injury and carries the risk of missing the entire campaign. His absence heightened the need for an additional body in the trenches, hence the signing of Humphries.
Tunsil's injury was ill-timed, considering the Commanders had just made him the highest-paid left tackle in the NFL . His two-year, $60.2 million extension made him the first player at his position to earn an average of $30 million annually. It was the second time in his career that he reset the left tackle market.
While he was at one point a premier left tackle, Humphries joins the Commanders as a depth piece rather than a viable starter. His regression over the last four years puts him in line for a second- or third-team role on his new team.
Coach Dan Quinn announced after Tunsil's injury that Brandon Coleman will start at left tackle so long as Tunsil is unavailable, and Josh Conerly Jr . is locked into the No. 2 job on the right side. Quinn also said the Commanders were not planning to look outside the organization for help, so while that ultimately changed, it is clear that team leadership is content with Coleman leading the charge as long as needed.
Humphries will provide experience in the locker room and create competition with second-teamer Andrew Wylie for the backup role.
author: Carter Bahns

title: Vikings' Jeshaun Jones suspended three games for violating NFL substance abuse policy
summary: Jones may participate in the remainder of the preseason before beginning his suspension on Aug. 30
full_text:
Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Jeshaun Jones faces a three-game suspension without pay for a violation of the NFL substance abuse policy. He is eligible to participate in the Vikings' remaining preseason activities and will begin his suspension on Aug. 30. The third-year wideout will be eligible for reinstatement on Monday, Sept. 28, the final day of Week 3.
Due to a change to the substance abuse policy in 2024, the Vikings were not informed of the substance that caused the positive test.
All NFL players receive an annual test for the seven types of drugs the league classifies as substances of abuse: Cocaine, synthetic marijuana, amphetamines, opiates, opioids, PCP and MDMA. Players who are entered into the substance abuse program can also be tested up to 10 times per month.
Jones is in a battle to make the Vikings' roster and likely stands on the outside looking in. Minnesota figures to carry only a modest number of options outside of superstar Justin Jefferson , returning No. 2 weapon Jordan Addison and offseason addition Jauan Jennings .
If the Vikings cut Jones by the Aug. 30 deadline, it will continue a trend. Jones has been on and off the roster since his arrival in 2024 as an undrafted free agent and served on the team's practice squad in both of his professional seasons.
Jones has one career appearance, and it came in the final game of the 2025 regular season. He served as Minnesota's punt returner and handled two reps, one of which went for a five-yard return.
author: Carter Bahns

title: Ja'Marr Chase injury scare: Bengals All-Pro goes down awkwardly in practice, OK after 'hyperextension'
summary: The Bengals had a scare today at practice, but their star receiver confirmed he avoided a serious injury
full_text:
Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase appeared to suffer a lower body injury on Tuesday, limping and heading to the sideline during practice. After practice, Chase told ESPN 1530-AM that he suffered a little "hyperextension" and could have kept going if needed. Chase also told ESPN he felt "fine."
Quarterback Joe Burrow threw the ball down the nearside of the field to Chase, who landed awkwardly and immediately grabbed at his left leg. He crawled on the field and was visibly hobbling as he went to the sideline. After reaching the sideline, Chase went back down on the field, once again crawling and appearing in pain. Trainers immediately ran to him to assist.
Here is a look at what happened:
Ja’Marr Chase is hurt. #Bengals pic.twitter.com/k04E1olC50
His limp seemed to subside after some time, according to CBS Cincinnati.
Ja’Marr walking on his own off the field with a trainer. Doesn’t look to have any limp anymore. pic.twitter.com/pivnQpHopM
The two-time first-team All-Pro was seen walking around and talking to his teammates.
Ja’Marr Chase continues to walk around the field. Some words with Joe Burrow and an embrace with DJ Turner. pic.twitter.com/nqx30m2CBW
Ja’Marr Chase walking it off. Appears to be walking OK, we’ll see if he goes back in to practice but wasn’t taken off in a cart or anything #Benfals pic.twitter.com/tZovyrnJBo
The five-time Pro Bowler is a valuable part of the Bengals offense and any absence would be a major blow to the team.
The 26-year-old finished last season with 125 receptions for 1,412 yards and eight touchdowns and did so without Burrow, who was out with a toe injury, for nine weeks. His best season came in 2024, when he finished with career highs in receptions (127), yards (1,708) and touchdowns (17). The exceptional year helped him earn a four-year, $161 million contract extension.
The former LSU star has been Burrow's favorite pass catcher since joining the team as the No. 5 overall pick in 2021. The wide receiver room also includes star Tee Higgins , who was second in receiving yards the last two seasons.
Chase missed five games in 2022 due to a hairline hip fracture and an AC joint sprain cost him one game in 2023.
author: Shanna McCarriston

title: Browns coach Todd Monken walks back claim that Lane Kiffin called about Dae'Quan Wright
summary: The Browns coach accepted responsibility for incorrectly suggesting Kiffin contacted him directly about Wright's availability
full_text:
Cleveland Browns coach Todd Monken walked back earlier remarks suggesting that LSU's Lane Kiffin called him about Dae'Quan Wright , the latest twist in a bizarre transfer portal saga involving the former NFL tight end. Kiffin publicly denied the conversation happened, saying Monday there were "inaccuracies" in Monken's story and that he does not have his number or know him personally.
Monken initially claimed last week that Kiffin reached out regarding Wright's availability and possible return to college football . Now, Monken agrees that no such call took place, clearing up a claim that quickly generated headlines across the sport.
"First off, I should not ... one of our staff had said, that's why I said 'us' and not 'me' ... one of our staff had said they had gotten a text," Monken said. "I should've followed through with it. Maybe they meant someone from (LSU's) staff. That's on me. Should not throw someone's name on there without following through on it.
"I was just making light of it. I was really not trying to make a big thing of it. I was just like, 'man, what this world has come to.' It was almost silliness and goofiness. It's really not a big deal other than I probably shouldn't have (said that) without following through."
Monken, who has worked at LSU previously (2005-06) and most recently served as Kirby Smart's offensive coordinator at Georgia, before joining the Baltimore Ravens and Browns.
"I've never had to deal with (this)," Monken said. "It happens in college with everybody. They catch word of something. You have players on your own team, 'I'm catching word from so and so that they're thinking about entering the portal.' It's word of mouth. They're not going to come to you. It was a weird situation. He got hurt, he's going back to college and it is what it is.
"Good luck to him. He's a good kid. And they're going to do a great job at LSU. That's what they should do. Their job is to get the best players they can and to win games. I'm not mad at anybody. Like I said, I shouldn't have taken what I'd heard and ran with it."
Wright's decision to enter the transfer portal after reaching the NFL would have sounded absurd not long ago. Now, amid courtroom victories, temporary restraining orders and eligibility rulings that continue to erase the sport's old boundaries, it represents another opportunity.
Kiffin is not responsible for cleaning up the NCAA's mess. He is responsible for building LSU's roster , and if the rules — or a judge — allow him to pursue an NFL player, he likely sees it as negligent not to make the call.
"Because of the rulings, they are going to play for you or someone else," Kiffin said . "We made the decision to recruit them. It's wrong to be critical of these kids. They were granted a fifth year and a judge said they were wronged."
Agent Drew Rosenhaus confirmed that multiple teams called about Wright , but LSU was the winner. The Browns waived Wright, and if he clears waivers, he will be part of LSU's 2026 roster, per Rosenhaus.
Wright initially signed with the Philadelphia Eagles as an undrafted rookie before landing with the Browns following his release earlier this month.
Kiffin is familiar with Wright, who played his final two collegiate seasons at Ole Miss. One of the offense's top targets, Wright recorded 39 catches for 635 yards and five touchdowns at tight end.
author: Brad Crawford

title: Latest NFL injury updates: Ashton Jeanty avoids major injury, other running backs uncertain for Week 1
summary: Who will be ready for season openers, and who's trying to get there?
full_text:
The second week of the preseason is over, and that means all preseason action for expected starters is a thing of the past, too. Teams generally treat the final preseason game as a chance to evaluate depth charts, battles for backup roles, roster spots and practice squad spots. Starters, meanwhile, will have their attention fully turned to Week 1 at last.
This training camp and preseason cycle have been particularly busy on the injury front, unfortunately. Hopefully, that's mostly behind us as teams hone in on Week 1 prep. As such, we've turned our injury analysis toward Week 1. As injury news continues to filter in, we'll be tracking not only the bumps and bruises (and sometimes more) but also their impact on season openers' availability.
Aug. 25: Warren is expected to be out at least through this week with the groin injury he suffered last week, per Steichen, who said the Colts are going to be "pretty smart" with the injury so that the tight end can be ready for Week 1. Warren should be a major factor for the Indianapolis passing game, assuming he returns to full health, alongside Pierce, Josh Downs and the recently signed Keenan Allen .
Aug. 25: After sitting out the entire offseason program following ankle surgery, Pierce will "hopefully" return to practice later this week if all goes well, head coach Shane Steichen said. It would be an extremely welcome development for the Colts to get Pierce back on the field, given how much they paid him this offseason and how much the offense relies on his field-stretching capabilities.
Aug. 24 -- Lower-body injury. Dan Quinn said Monday that Jacory Croskey-Merritt is dealing with an undisclosed injury, potentially sustained near the end of last week, and reporters said he has a lower-body injury. He could be back next week.
Aug. 24 -- Hamstring. Dave Canales said Monday that Chuba Hubbard is expected to return for Week 1 and that Hubbard and Jonathon Brooks would operate in a committee in that case. Hubbard himself said his hamstring feels good, but the team is protecting him from himself after he returned too early last year.
Aug. 19 -- Calf strain. Oweh, who signed a four-year, $96 million deal with the Commanders this offseason, suffered a calf strain either Aug. 17 or 18 (he did not practice on the 18th), and Quinn announced the injury on the 19th.
Aug. 17 -- Groin. Hall suffered a non-contact groin sprain, but coach Aaron Glenn said it would sideline him for 2 to 3 weeks and not carry over into the regular season. The Jets ' Week 1 opener was nearly four weeks away when Glenn provided the timetable.
Aug. 24 -- Neck injury recovery. Jesse Minter said, "I don't know the answer to that right now," when asked about Madubuike's Week 1 availability. Madubuike suffered the injury -- thought to be career-threatening at one point -- early last season. He has practiced in a limited capacity so far this training camp.
Aug. 23 -- Ankle sprain. Just as soon as it looked like we were done with injury news over the weekend, one more player got added to the list, and it's a big one. Ashton Jeanty went down during a non-contact catching drill and could not put any weight on his leg. Hours later, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported it's an ankle sprain, and the Raiders are unsure how long it will keep last year's No. 6 overall pick out.
Aug. 23 -- Torn Achilles recovery. George Kittle's impressive recovery from a torn Achilles suffered in the playoffs hit a new high Sunday, when the 49ers activated him off the PUP list . A Week 1 appearance against the Rams in Australia is still on the table, though not a certainty by any measure.
Aug. 17 -- Knee hyperextension diagnosis. Kyle Monangai hyperextended his right knee on Aug. 16, and the next day, Ben Johnson described Monangai's status as "week-to-week."
Aug. 20 -- Hip. Dan Campbell said Sam LaPorta's status for Week 1 is up in the air as he deals with a hip issue.
Aug. 19 -- Pectoral injury recovery. Meeting with the media on Wednesday, Eagles defensive coordinator Vic Fangio said there's concern regarding Greenard's availability for Week 1 due to a pec injury. The Eagles acquired Greenard from the Vikings for a third-round pick and gave him a four-year, $98 million contract this offseason.
Aug. 18 -- High ankle sprain. While seeing a surprisingly large role -- 14 touches while playing nearly the entire first half -- in Week 1 of the preseason, Jeremiyah Love suffered a high ankle sprain, leaving his status for Week 1 up in the air. The No. 3 overall pick got bent awkwardly during a tackle on his final touch of the game, and after it took a few days to get a full diagnosis, it was not good news.
Aug. 25 -- Serious knee injury. What was supposed to be his debut season with the Giants is now in jeopardy. According to ESPN , trainers carted Austin off the practice field with what was described as a serious knee injury. If Austin misses extended time, it would open the door for one of New York's veteran signings -- like Odell Beckham Jr . or Braxton Berrios -- to make the roster.
Aug. 24 -- Torn patella. Jesse Minter told the media that Pinter is out for the season with a torn patella. He had been working as the Ravens ' first-team center during training camp. Ethan Pocic , coming off a torn Achilles, will likely take his spot.
Aug. 23 -- Broken ankle. Mike Macdonald said Clark, a second-round pick out of TCU, will miss "several months" with a broken ankle suffered in Seattle's preseason Week 2 game against the Titans . Clark was carted off the field with his lower leg, ankle and foot in an air cast.
Aug. 23 -- Placed on IR. Tyler Biadasz suffered a gruesome-looking injury in an Aug. 18 joint practice with the 49ers, and the initial diagnosis of "out indefinitely with ACL damage and other knee damage" wasn't promising. On Aug. 23, the Chargers officially put Biadasz on IR, a difficult blow for a team in need of much better offensive line play this season.
Aug. 23 -- Placed on IR. Alex Wright , who got a three-year extension after a strong 2025, suffered a torn Achilles in an Aug. 20 joint practice with the Bills . The Browns officially placed him on IR on Sunday and signed Derek Barnett in a corresponding move.
Aug. 21 -- Placed on IR. Jayden Higgins tore his ACL in an Aug. 18 joint practice with the Ravens, leaving a considerable hole in the Texans ' wide receiver room behind standout Nico Collins . He officially went on IR on Friday.
Aug. 19 -- MCL sprain diagnosis. Kamara sprained his MCL in a joint practice with the Cowboys on Aug. 18, and one day later, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported he'd miss at least a month. The Saints ' Week 1 matchup with the Lions was less than a month away at the time of Schefter's report.
Aug. 17 -- Hamstring injury diagnosis. Jordyn Tyson will reportedly miss two months after suffering a right hamstring injury on Aug. 13 during a joint practice with the Jaguars . The No. 8 overall pick in April's draft, Tyson has dealt with several hamstring issues, though this one is separate from previous episodes.
author: Zachary Pereles

title: Ranking all eight NFL 'Rivalries' uniforms from best to worst: Vikings near the top, Lions close to bottom
summary: Here's who has the best 'Rivalries' uniform in the NFL this year
full_text:
The NFL's newest batch of "Rivalries" uniforms have officially been released , and now it's time to rank them from best to worst.
There were a total of eight uniforms released on Tuesday with each team in the NFC North and AFC South getting a new look, as part of the "NFL x Nike Rivalries" program, which kicked off last year with teams in the AFC East and NFC West each getting a new uniform.
Here's what the release schedule looks like going forward:
But we don't need to worry about what's coming down the road, because we need to focus on right now, and right now, we're going to rank this year's crop of uniforms, so let's get to it.
I love everything about these uniforms and I also love the fact that the Texans are the pettiest team in the league. The Texans claim that these uniforms were designed in honor of the city of Houston, but it really kind of seems like they're actually honoring the Houston Oilers.
By the 🤘. For the 🤘. pic.twitter.com/IHauXWcogf
Texans are going with the white helmets for their Rivalries series. They will be dropping the black helmet with red speckles. pic.twitter.com/jJhTgR27vV
The Texans aren't allowed to wear an Oilers throwback uniform -- because the Titans own the rights to the all things Oilers -- so it feels like their ultimate plan here was to design something that had an Oilers feel to it.
The whole Oilers thing has actually been a sore subject between the two teams. Back in April 2024 , Texans co-owner Hannah McNair, the wife of Texans owner Cal McNair, made it clear that the rights to the Oilers jerseys should have stayed with the Texans when the Oilers/Titans moved from Houston to Tennessee in 1997.
"Houston takes a lot of pride in [the uniforms], and you know, Tennessee doesn't care as much," McNair said. "It's not as meaningful to their fans."
The Oilers had one of the most iconic uniforms in NFL history and you can't really go wrong by copying the look, which is why I'm a big fan of everything the Texans did.
Although I don't have the Vikings at the top of my list, I almost feel bad for that, because I feel like Minnesota spent more time than any other team on the fine details in their uniform.
Close look at the Vikings Rivalries jerseys pic.twitter.com/gBWlJ1ae4D
I mean, this entire uniform is basically an ode to the Nordic Gods. For one, the white color on the jersey isn't actually white, it's Ivory, and the Vikings picked that color to match their giant Gjallarhorn.
According to the team , the uniform also features the word SKOL, but it's " transcribed in Rune characters. The Rune system, called Younger Futhark, features a 16-character runic alphabet used in Scandinavia during The Viking Age." If you have any Rune on your uniform, that's an automatic win in my book.
And the then there's the stripe on the sleeve, which is actually a Nordic knot. I mean, the Vikings thought of everything.
Let me start by saying that I actually like the Titans jersey and helmet. If I had only been ranking those two things, I might have put them at No. 1, but I'm ranking the entire look.
Yeah, these uniforms are hot pic.twitter.com/Y6MHt6FQVx
The Titans are wearing Navy blue pants with their uniform and that's the part I don't love. Back in 2015, the NFL did a Color Rush thing where each team picked a color and wore that from head to toe. With the pants and jersey being the same color, this feels like a Color Rush jersey. It's too much blue. That being said, I'm still a huge fan of what the Titans did here, especially the helmet.
The Vikings also went with a monocrome look, but I have them one spot higher because all the details on their uniform blew me away.
After starting at these uniforms for two straight hours, I have to admit, they're really starting to grow on me. When I started this list, I actually had the Packers at SIXTH, but I moved them up to fourth, because I decided that I actually love everything about them.
For our history. For our future. For you. pic.twitter.com/a2cVbuLlhE
They used a vintage green for the jersey color and the best part is that the helmet and pants are alabaster instead of white. I didn't even know alabaster was a color until three months ago when my wife said she wanted to paint our bathroom that color.
As for the Packers using alabaster, that had nothing to do with the paint color my bathroom, They used it because "The alabaster palette is reminiscent of the aged paper of historic Packers stock certificates."
New favorite color is Alabaster pic.twitter.com/59rxgLDZM3
The team is trying to look like a stock certificate and I actually like it. What a weird day.
The Jaguars were the hardest team to rank because I love the teal helmet, but it just doesn't make any sense with this wardrobe.
If you've ever wondered what the Jaguars would look like with a teal helmet, we finally have our answer with their new Rivalries uniform. #Jaguars pic.twitter.com/AbFWIegxrq
The white jersey and black pants would have looked good with a black or white helmet. The teal helmet would have looked good with a white jersey and teal pants. The teal helmet might have even worked with a black jersey and black pants. This is literally the one combination where the teal feels kind of iffy. That being said, I will 100% be buying a teal helmet to put in my background, and once I do, you'll be able to see it during the videos I do on CBS Sports HQ.
I don't hate the Lions look, but here's my one problem: It's like they forgot that they were supposed to design a "Rivalries" jersey and since they didn't have time to come up with one, they decided to just steal the Panthers ' look.
The Lions are never beating the “Detroit Panthers” allegations 💀 pic.twitter.com/zfYcoak1xW
Fortunately, the Lions won't be wearing these uniforms against the Panthers. And that's a good thing, because I'm not sure the universe could handle it.
When the NFL told the Bears to create a "Rivalries" uniform, they somehow interpreted that as "make another throwback uniform," because that's exactly what Chicago ended up doing. The Bears had orange numbers on their uniform for most of the 1940s, which also happened to be their "Monsters of the Midway" era, and the team is paying homage to that.
Inspired by the past. Built for the future. pic.twitter.com/WzxAIyzOcA
As a throwback uniform, this is nice, but as a "Rivalries" uniform, I don't love it. The Packers designed a completely new uniform using a vintage look, and to me, that was the smart way to go. Instead, the Bears created a throwback.
The problem for the Colts is that their standard uniform is so iconic that it's hard make an upgrade to it. The Colts have two colors -- blue and white -- and whenever they introduce a new color to that scheme, things get kind of rocky and I feel like that's the situation here. The blue helmets are awesome, but I'm not a huge fan of the "Anvil Steel" jerseys.
Colts 2026 Rivalries pic.twitter.com/wQ40sPivKG
Although the Colts ranked at the bottom here, I don't hate their uniforms. I actually think each team did a good job of creating something new for the their fans.
Each team will only get to wear their "Rivalries" uniform once and here's the full schedule (And remember, only the home team will be wearing the new uniform. The visiting team will NOT be wearing their "Rivalries" uniform):
After wearing the new uniform this year, each team will be allowed to keep it in their rotation for the next three years.
author: John Breech

title: Cowboys' Joe Milton showing he's more than a big arm, but backup QB battle remains unsettled
summary: Two strong outings have strengthened Milton's case for the No. 2 job and demonstrated how much his command of the position has improved
full_text:
Dallas Cowboys backup quarterback Joe Milton III is coming off an inspired performance, having lit up the Arizona Cardinals by going 9-of-13 for 179 yards and two touchdowns. That followed a preseason opener against the Seattle Seahawks , where he went 12-of-15 for 107 yards and a score. Add it all up, and Milton has been the league's most efficient quarterback during the preseason, according to TruMedia's version of expected points added (EPA) per play.
Coach Brian Schottenheimer took notice.
"I first remember hearing about Joe Milton when he was at the University of Michigan, and everyone applauded him for how hard and how far he could throw the ball," Schottenheimer said, via The Athletic . "Cool. That's awesome. Go be in a carnival somewhere. That's not what playing an NFL quarterback is. It's not. … You're throwing through small windows, you're throwing over people, you're changing arm slots.
"So to me, arm strength is cool. Go to the fair and win a teddy bear. But you got to play quarterback. And that's what I think you see Joe learning is he's playing quarterback. And he's playing quarterback at a high level. He's checking the ball down. He's making blitz adjustments. He's solving problems. He's reading from his first, second to third, and even fourth progression at times. It takes time. You don't stop learning as a quarterback. The only way to do it is to play. I'm really, really proud of him."
Milton showed off those skills in Dallas' second preseason game. Early on, he sidestepped pressure in the pocket, stepped up and through the rush, then found running back Malik Davis leaking out into the flat for a touchdown.
the offense turns the INT into a TD 💪 #DALvsAZ | @Campaign_Lik 📺: #DALvsAZ on CBS11 📲: Stream on NFL+ https://t.co/7pAfvQ9tid pic.twitter.com/3TOSx2hFAw
Schottenheimer detailed exactly why that play made an impression on him.
"Honestly, last year this time, on the touchdown to Malik, it's probably from me to [a nearby reporter], and he probably would've blistered it at Malik," the head coach said. "Probably would've put a dent in Malik's chest because he's capable of doing that. He just kind of softened his elbow, and just kind of flipped it and made it really easy for Malik."
Later, Milton hit Jonathan Mingo for a deep ball up the left sideline for a long touchdown, then scrambled around and found undrafted free-agent wideout Camden Brown for a big gain -- two plays that Schottenheimer separately referred to as "beautiful."
GOIN' DEEEEEEP 👀 #DALvsAZ | @ogmingo1k 📺: #DALvsAZ on CBS11 📲: Stream on NFL+ https://t.co/7pAfvQ9tid pic.twitter.com/dyIt4aRRyg
. @Qbjayy7 to @CamdenBrown7 for a HUGE gain❗️ 📺: #DALvsAZ on CBS11 📲: Stream on NFL+ https://t.co/7pAfvQ9tid pic.twitter.com/vj4VZ0O8Wo
"Last year at times, this time of year with Joe, it was a little bit difficult to call plays for Joe because I wasn't sure exactly what's going to happen here and there," Schottenheimer said, before detailing the progress Milton has made and saying that the quarterback has put together "two really, really good performances" in the preseason games.
In other words, it looks like Milton is becoming more of a quarterback rather than just a passer. And that's a great sign for his development and his potential future in the league. We've seen over the last few years that teams are increasingly willing to give talented backups a chance to start, and it's worked out quite well for some of them.
It's important not to get ahead of ourselves, though. Most of those backup quarterbacks getting chances to be starters have been first-round draft picks like Sam Darnold or mid-round picks like Malik Willis -- not sixth-rounders like Milton, who has thrown all of 53 regular-season passes and so doesn't have either the pedigree or track record of any of those types of players.
There's also the fact that Milton's preseason success has come exclusively against backups and third-stringers. It's hard to read too much into that level of performance, and it doesn't sound like the Cowboys are, either. That's evident in Schottenheimer's assertion that Milton hasn't won the backup job in Dallas just yet. He's still in a battle with Sam Howell , the former fifth-round pick of the Commanders who has not shown much in his career to indicate that he's a starting-caliber player.
"If you would just take the training camp competition, it's probably neck and neck, and Sam maybe a little bit ahead," Schottenheimer said. "That's why we actually started Sam in the first game against Seattle. But Joe's put together two really good performances, and this will be another fun week for them to keep battling."
If Milton beats out Howell for the No. 2 role behind Dak Prescott , then his encouraging performances in the preseason should perhaps have the Cowboys feeling better about their backup quarterback situation than they did last year. Anyone thinking bigger than that -- like that Milton is ready to be a starter -- is probably thinking too big, at least for now. But turning into a quality backup would be a fantastic outcome for a former sixth-round pick, because most sixth-rounders don't stick in the league for very long.
author: Jared Dubin

title: Damien Harris calls Dae'Quan Wright's move from NFL to NCAA transfer portal 'embarassing,' 'elementary'
summary: The former NFL player isn't a fan of young athletes going back to college football after time in the NFL
full_text:
Tight end Dae'Quan Wright stirred up some controversy last week when he went from NFL training camp to NCAA's transfer portal , becoming the first active player to do so. The former Ole Miss player went undrafted, signed with the Philadelphia Eagles first and was a member of the Cleveland Browns practice squad, participating in training camp and dressing for a preseason game , although sidelined due to an apparent injury.
Wright was then waived by Cleveland on Aug. 24. The NFL rookie already has his next spot, with an agreement in place at LSU if he clears waivers. It's believed he would be the first ex-NFL player to go back to play college football .
The move is one not everyone agrees with.
Former NFL running back and two-time CFB national champion Damien Harris had strong words about the situation, calling it "embarrassing" and "elementary."
"This isn't the type of history that you want to be making. And to be honest, I'm going to be very candid, I think this is embarrassing," the former Alabama running back said to CBS Sports . "To go through an NFL training camp, go through the process of being selected or being signed as an undrafted free agent, going through the preseason, playing preseason football, playing NFL football and then returning to college and taking up a roster spot from somebody who is deserving of their time there, I think that this is very elementary."
The 22-year-old will likely not be the only one to attempt to go back to college after time in the NFL. A new NCAA rule gives most Division I athletes five years of eligibility over five years, but the two-month-old rule didn't include Wright and doesn't take effect until next season. Wright, along with a group of other athletes, filed a lawsuit in Louisiana and were granted a temporary restraining order to return to college for one more year.
"I know that there … are a lot of different things going on in college football to where the players have the control and they're doing exactly what they want with it and this is an exact example of that," Harris said.
The former New England Patriots and Buffalo Bills back continued to say if he was in a front office, the move would impact how he made decisions regarding the player in the future.
"If I'm an NFL GM and I'm looking at guys like this who could potentially be coming out next year, these aren't guys I want to draft, because I don't know how competitive they are. I don't know how much they love football. I don't know how hard they're willing to work in order to prove themselves on a football team and earn their spot. I can't guarantee that a guy like this is a guy I'd build a program around," Harris said.
Overall, Harris called it "bush league," noting that this is what he feels the college football and NCAA "landscape has become" over the last few years.
"... Athletes are trying to finesse the system of both college and NFL I think it's very elementary," Harris added.
Browns head coach Todd Monken seemingly felt similarly, saying , "Man, isn't this shit crazy? I don't even know what to say," when asked about Wright.
"I wondered why Lane Kiffin reached out to me a week ago; now I know. I didn't call him back. I guess I should have," Monken added.
Wright had 113 passes for 1,603 yards in his time with Virginia Tech and Ole Miss.
author: Shanna McCarriston

title: NFL's new 'Rivalries' uniforms are here for NFC North and AFC South: Eight teams just got a new look for 2026
summary: All eight NFC North and AFC South teams unveiled city-themed alternate designs and new helmets, which each club will wear once during the 2026 season
full_text:
Last year, the NFL started a tradition of letting eight different teams release a new "Rivalries" uniform just before the start of the season and those uniforms came out on Tuesday with all eight of them being released at the same time.
Every team in the both the NFC North and AFC South unveiled both a new helmet and a new uniform. Those eight teams will each get to wear their new look for one game this season.
If you're wondering what the "Rivalries" program is, it's like the NFL's Color Rush campaign from a few years ago: It gives all 32 teams a solid excuse to create a new uniform. For Color Rush, each team picked one color and wore it from head to toe. For the "Rivalries" program, each team was asked to create a uniform based on a theme that's local to each city.
Without further ado, let's check out the new uniforms, starting with the four teams in the NFC North.
The Bears took their classic blue uniforms and threw in a slight twist by adding orange numbers.
You could almost consider this a throwback uniform considering the Bears had orange numbers on their uniform for most of the 1940s, which also happened to be their "Monsters of the Midway" era.
Inspired by the past. Built for the future. pic.twitter.com/WzxAIyzOcA
The Bears will also be wearing a lot of orange as the Rivalries look includes both an orange helmet and orange pants.
The Packers decided to honor the fact that they're owned by the fans with a vintage green that has stock certificate-inspired details woven into the numbers and sleeves.
For our history. For our future. For you. pic.twitter.com/a2cVbuLlhE
Here's a fun fact: The helmet and pants are both alabaster. According to the team , "the alabaster palette is reminiscent of the aged paper of historic Packers stock certificates."
The Vikings went with a purple jersey that features a Vikings-knot design on the shoulder and on the pants, which is a nice touch.
Feel The North 😈 https://t.co/h0zACZWDHy pic.twitter.com/M7aVLQLOgg
The Vikings' new uniform would have also worked as a Color Rush uniform because Minnesota is going purple from head to toe.
The Lions ended up being the only team in the NFC North that ended up going with a white jersey.
Defend. The. Den. pic.twitter.com/PiIQN5cf0u
If this uniform didn't say "Detroit" on the front, you might mistake it for the Panthers ' white uniform. The Lions are bringing back their blue helmet, which goes well with these uniforms.
And now, let's head to the AFC South.
The Texans aren't allowed to wear an Oilers throwback uniform -- because the Titans own the rights to the Oilers name -- so this might be the closest the Texans ever get to honoring the Oilers.
For the 🤘. By the 🤘. pic.twitter.com/kBn5tLsKHY
They used Columbia blue and red and threw it on a white jersey and came up with a sharp look.
Of the eight teams that got a new "Rivalries" jersey this year, the Jags arguably did the least with their design. It's not much different from their standard white uniforms, but they did get wild with their helmet. For the first time ever, the Jags have unveiled a teal helmet.
If you've ever wondered what the Jaguars would look like with a teal helmet, we finally have our answer with their new Rivalries uniform. #Jaguars pic.twitter.com/AbFWIegxrq
The Jags also decided to go with black pants.
