Milton’s second preseason performance was difficult to overlook: 9-of-13 passing for 179 yards and two touchdowns, plus a rushing touchdown, as he led Dallas to a 24-6 halftime advantage. NFL.com described his performance as potentially separating him from Sam Howell in the QB2 competition, while the Associated Press called it another strong effort in Milton’s bid for the job. The national conversation around Milton is clearly shifting. And this time, it isn’t just Cowboys observers taking notice. National outlets are increasingly highlighting Milton as a legitimate candidate to win the QB2 job behind Dak Prescott — and some are starting to wonder whether his ceiling might be considerably higher. Here’s what they’re saying. Cowboys backup QB opens eyes with preseason performance – Nick Brinkerhoff, USA Today While Milton has thrived in his preseason action, it’s important to remember that he is still firmly behind Prescott on the depth chart. He will remain there unless an injury forces the star out of action. If nothing else, Cowboys fans can sleep a little better at night with the belief they have a capable backup behind Prescott. After all, that’s what the preseason is all about – seeing what you have up-and-down the roster. After the first half in Arizona, the Cowboys might be feeling even better about the quarterback room. What we learned from NFL preseason games: QB Joe Milton was the star of the night. – Staff, The Athletic The backup competition between Milton and Sam Howell saw Howell start last week and play the entire first half before Milton played the entire second half. In a dominant win over Arizona on Saturday, those roles were reversed. Milton was outstanding, looking confident and calm in the pocket. His deep ball up the left sideline to Jonathan Mingo was perfect, resulting in a 53-yard touchdown. And he never came close to turning the ball over. Milton finished 9 of 13 passing for 179 yards, two touchdowns and a 151.4 passer rating, and added a short TD run. Shannon Sharpe thinks Joe Milton deserves a chance to start in the NFL – Zach Ragan, AtoZ Sports Pro Football Hall of Famer Shannon Sharpe has been impressed enough by Milton that he believes the former Vol is going to find himself in a starting situation at some point in the not-too-distant future. “I feel like Joe Milton is going to find himself in a situation like Malik Willis,” said Sharpe . “He could be a starter. There’s ain’t no way in hell you’re going to tell me there’s 32 quarterbacks better than this man.” As for where Milton could land as a starter? Sharpe says to keep an eye on Cleveland. “Keep an eye on that Cleveland situation,” said Sharpe. “He’s going to play himself into a starting job somewhere. I think people have seen enough. You look at the Browns’ situation, I don’t think they’re settled on their quarterback. Whoever wins the job, I don’t think they’re settled.” Sharpe also pointed out the Pittsburgh Steelers as a team that could be in the market for a quarterback when Aaron Rodgers calls it a career (which is expected to happen at the end of the 2026 season). Joe Milton is a much better option https://t.co/cX5JbhF11E — Chase Daniel (@ChaseDaniel) August 23, 2026 Has Joe Milton III separated himself in the No. 2 quarterback battle? – Todd Archer, ESPN Milton’s command of the offense is so much greater than it was in 2025, and the results have been telling. In two games, he has completed 21 of 28 passes for 286 yards and three touchdowns. He also ran for a score. He has made the big plays — a TD of 56 yards and a completion of 70 yards vs. the Cardinals — but more importantly, he avoided mistakes. Milton’s arm strength is unquestioned, but his poise and decision-making have impressed the coaches. Sam Howell has done nothing to lose the job (though that late-game pick with the Cowboys in the red zone against Arizona didn’t help), but the roster gymnastics required by keeping three quarterbacks on the 53-man roster could be too costly when the Cowboys look to fill their spots at wide receiver, linebacker and cornerback. Joe Milton has strong game, but Cowboys backup QB competition “long from over” – Josh Alper, PFT.com Brian Schottenheimer credited him with “two good halves” on Saturday, but said the competition remains open. “This is long from over ,” Schottenheimer said. “We’re going back to Frisco, thankfully, get a chance to be home and put some more training camp days in. You’ve got to give Joe his credit, he’s played really well the past two games, but we have a lot of confidence in Sam as well.” Milton joined the Cowboys late in the 2025 preseason and said he feels a “ major difference ” from where he was a year ago. We’ll find out soon whether that difference has been enough for him to secure the backup job. Milton throws 2 TDs in 1st half, makes case for Cowboys’ backup job in 34-13 win over Cardinals – David Brandt, AP News. Joe Milton had another good day in his quest to become the Dallas Cowboys’ backup quarterback. The third-year player — who is battling Sam Howell for the No. 2 role behind Dak Prescott — threw two touchdown passes and ran for a score in a second straight impressive preseason effort, sparking the Cowboys to a 34-13 victory over the Arizona Cardinals on Saturday night. Milton finished 9-of-13 passing for 179 yards, connecting on a 53-yard touchdown pass to Jonathan Mingo and a 70-yard strike to Camden Brown that set up Milton’s 1-yard touchdown run a play later. The play to Mingo was perfectly executed, with the receiver making a double move before Milton hit him in stride down the left sideline. “This game is about to being able to control the RPMs of the football and throw it with different speeds and touches,” Schottenheimer said. “He’s done that at a very high level.” Joe Milton states his case for QB2 role – Calvin Watkins, DMN Milton started the second preseason game and took a lead over Sam Howell for the No. 2 job at quarterback. Milton completed 9 of 13 passes for 179 yards with two passing touchdowns and one rushing score. Milton finished with a 151.4 quarterback rating. Milton had six first-half possessions, with four ending in scores. One of Milton’s best throws was a 53-yard touchdown pass down the Cowboys’ sideline on a fade route to Mingo. Depending on the roster construction, the Cowboys might keep both quarterbacks on the 53. It seems the final preseason game Friday against New Orleans will decide. ‘Bro Is Built Like Cam Newton’: Saints Coach Left in Awe of Joe Milton After Joint Practice With Cowboys – Shubhi Rathore, Essentially Sports Saints guest coach Nicholas Williams, who is assisting the team’s coaching staff during the preseason, was impressed by Milton’s physical abilities during the practice. “Just had a joint practice against Joe Milton. Bro is built like Cam Newton and has a cannon for an arm,” Williams wrote on X, replying to former NFL quarterback Chase Daniel. The trail of appreciation started when ESPN analyst Dan Orlovsky suggested that the Atlanta Falcons should trade a late-round pick for Los Angeles Rams quarterback Stetson Bennett. Daniel then offered Milton as a better option. That said, the Cowboys will next face the Saints in the final preseason game. That matchup could give Milton another opportunity to show what he has in store against the team whose guest coach compared him to Newton.

title: Cowboys insider predicts veteran not on team will make roster
summary: There is officially less than a week to go. By Sunday’s end the Dallas Cowboys will have finished up their preseason, but they will also have finished up their 53-man roster. At least their initial 53-man roster. If you have been around for a minute then you know that the first “final” 53 will hardly […]
full_text: Jul 29, 2026; Oxnard, CA, USA; Dallas Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker at training camp at River Ridge Playing Fields. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect There is officially less than a week to go. By Sunday’s end the Dallas Cowboys will have finished up their preseason, but they will also have finished up their 53-man roster. At least their initial 53-man roster. If you have been around for a minute then you know that the first “final” 53 will hardly be the group that heads into Week 1 preparation for the New York Giants. Roster gymnastics are a thing and so the Cowboys will have to make sure they get players the right designations through this or that mechanism, and some of that may include actual movement of players. An outside veteran might be on this team soon Movement happens in both directions. Players currently on the team will not be soon, and vice versa. Consider that 10 days ago Von Miller was not on the Cowboys. In his latest 53-man roster prediction, one he deemed to be final , ESPN’s Todd Archer leaned into this ideal. At cornerback Archer carried five players on the team, one that is to be determined at a later point in time. Cornerbacks (5) DaRon Bland, Cobie Durant, Shavon Revel Jr., Veteran not on roster, Devin Moore Depth is a worry beyond the top three. While Revel has had an excellent camp, he has to show he can do it in the regular season. The fourth corner might not be on the roster at the moment. Adding a veteran free agent or making a small trade for one is not out of the question. Archer is among the most plugged-in Cowboys insiders on the beat so when he says something like this we should listen. The four that he has on the team make sense, Devin Moore hasn’t popped but he is a draft pick, but that TBD is interesting. If you are curious, this is the only position in which Archer provided this caveat across his roster prediction. This doesn’t necessarily mean that corner is the most likely place in which the Cowboys could bring in external help, but it certainly underscores what we have all known for a while in that this is an area of concern.

title: Weaknesses in the Broncos’ roster
summary: The hype all offseason with the Broncos is how good it is that they are running it back. They have an unprecedented number of starters and contributing depth players back on the roster this season. Hope springs eternal in the offseason and through training camp, but my eyes tell me there are areas of concern […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 13: Taylor Rapp #9 of the Buffalo Bills runs on field prior to an NFL football game against the Atlanta Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 13, 2025 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The hype all offseason with the Broncos is how good it is that they are running it back. They have an unprecedented number of starters and contributing depth players back on the roster this season. Hope springs eternal in the offseason and through training camp, but my eyes tell me there are areas of concern on this roster to look out for. Heck, I’ve posted about it earlier this year. Let’s revisit the areas of weakness on the roster and have a No Bull look at what the status is now. Inside Linebackers The major moves this offseason to help bolster the inside linebacker position were drafting Red Murdock in the seventh round and signing undrafted free agent Taurean York. We’ve seen plenty of quality snaps and play from Murdock with a lot of praise from the coaching staff. York also has been talked up but may need another season before he’s going to be ready to be leaned on heavily. I’m pretty bullish on Murdock. He’s a guy that can step in for Alex Singleton in a pinch—focusing mainly on 1st and 2nd downs. Even so, this position is still the main weakness on the defense, which we got a reminder about again last week with Singleton giving up an easy touchdown while vacating his area of the field. There are at least a couple of young players getting coached up in and waiting in the wings, which is an improvement as far as roster management goes. Wide Receivers All we really have to say here is Jaylen Waddle. The cherry on top is the consistent news that Pat Bryant is absolute fire as well. The crazy thing to me is that a player like Troy Franklin got so many snaps last season and may have trouble consistently getting on the field of play. Cameron Ross is charging forward from the undrafted free agent class and making a name for himself. The receiver position may have turned into a strength of the offense. I was pretty down on this position group back in March, but I think the offense has far greater worries at this point. Tight Ends The one area of concern I have on offense is the tight end position. Yes, the Broncos drafted Justin Joly in the fifth round as well as Dallen Bentley in the seventh. I like where both are at as rookies, but the offense is going to be leaning on Evan Engram and Adam Trautman as the season gets rolling. I do think the position improved, but like the ILB position, it lacks pizazz. Running Backs I was very pleased with the Broncos taking Jonah Coleman in the fourth round. Coleman looks superb and is a back that can step in this year and make a difference in the run game. The Broncos also resigned JK Dobbins, which I’m not overly fond of due to his injury history. Dobbins is a player that is easy to cheer for, though. The guy I think is going to look really good this year is RJ Harvey. He was already looking the part of a red-zone playmaker last season. He’s the joker that the Sean Payton offense has been missing, and I think he will be the second most impactful weapon on this offense behind Jaylen Waddle. Overall, the Broncos’ running back room looks far better than it was last year. Safety Another big concern is the depth at the safety position. The Broncos tried to see if J.L. Skinner or Devon Key would be the answer to depth at safety, but it became apparent that they weren’t quite at the level that Vance Joseph was looking for. Taylor Rapp was signed recently to add veteran depth to the position. While I do think that does help a bit, Rapp is another player that needs to prove he is healthy and can stay that way after playing only six games last season. Final Thoughts Let me know in the comments the top position group you are concerned about on the team and why. I’d love to get the pulse from Broncos Country on where they see problems on the roster. title: Broncos hoping to correct miscues, start off fast as regular season approaches
summary: After their 20-point loss to the Green Bay Packers last Friday, the Denver Broncos are back to the drawing board. It was an uninspiring performance with few things of note to write home about. With just one game left before the start of the regular season, there isn’t much time left for the Broncos to […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - AUGUST 21: Denver Broncos head coach Sean Payton looks on in the second half during a preseason game between the Green Bay Packers and the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High on August 21, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Dustin Bradford/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images After their 20-point loss to the Green Bay Packers last Friday, the Denver Broncos are back to the drawing board. It was an uninspiring performance with few things of note to write home about. With just one game left before the start of the regular season, there isn’t much time left for the Broncos to work out some of the major issues they’ve seen in the preseason. Coming off back-to-back double digit win seasons and their first AFC West title in a decade last year, Denver enters the 2026 season with big expectations and Super Bowl aspirations. They boast a quality roster that added more talent in the offseason, though face a daunting schedule to begin the year. Head Coach Sean Payton wasn’t sure if the loss to the Packers last Friday was a minor wake up call for them. However, he reflected on his first three years coaching the team and came away with one big thing the Broncos need to be a lot better at—starting off fast. “I always feel like during the course of training camp, you have this stretch and you have some peaks and you have some lows. You just hope that you’re moving the needle the right direction when you have those days. Now some days it might be better for the defense, not as good for the offense or vice versa,” stated Payton. “All that, trying to keep in mind starting faster. I don’t think we’ve really started fast here in my three years. I’m pretty sure we haven’t, so I think that’s going to be important,” remarked Payton. While the Broncos started off with a 9-2 recover before the Bye Week last season, a lot of those games were a lot closer than they would have liked. In six of those games, the team scored less than 21 points and struggled converting third downs. For as good as Bo Nix has been in his two years with the franchise, Year 3 will be a big opportunity for him to hit the ground running and perform better in the early half of the season. There were some peaks as Payton had mentioned, but those lows and inconsistencies offensively held them back from their potential despite the number of marks in the win column. In that span, the offense had a combined 12 turnovers and with the lack of takeaways on defense—found themselves on the wrong end of turnover differential. Payton’s right—the Broncos have to find a way to come out the gate fast this season—especially with the number of high caliber teams they will face early on. In three weeks, the Broncos start their Lombardi Trophy quest against a familiar and formidable foe. They kick off their regular season on the road against the Kansas City Chiefs on Monday Night Football . Every game in the regular season matters, but rivalry games in primetime hit different. Veteran inside linebacker Alex Singleton diverged from Payton a bit with his commentary after practice yesterday. With the poor performance against the Packers, he believes it can be a spark to get guys to compete, take a good look in the mirror, and do whatever it takes to rectify those issues before the rubber truly meets the road at Arrowhead. “I just think it should on a competitive level. Just to get that push, when that happens on Friday, then how we practiced Saturday and how we practiced today, just to see who guys are. Coach Payton always talks about the debrief after the game is more important than the game,” stated Singleton. “It’s those things, just being able to look at yourself. People say when you point fingers, your thumb points back at you. So those things, it’s really, ‘What can you do to get better?’ We do get the preseason. You get time to learn those things about yourself, and your team and stuff like that. It is to use them as learning lessons and take advantage of that.” This Friday, the Broncos will host the Minnesota Vikings in the preseason finale. It’s their last shot to try and solve some issues that have been constant throughout the preseason. Let’s hope the Broncos rise to the occasion and find a way to put their best foot forward as the regular season nears.
author: Christopher Hart

title: Sean Payton says that Broncos WR Pat Bryant is having a ‘heck of a camp’
summary: The story of Broncos Camp this summer has been the emergence of second-year wide receiver Pat Bryant. We saw the beginnings of this breakout last season, but it carried over into the offseason and now into camp and the preseason. He stayed healthy and was making plays throughout camp, catching everything thrown his way, and […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - AUGUST 16: Pat Bryant #13 of the Denver Broncos warms up against the Arizona Cardinals during the NFL Preseason 2025 game at Empower Field at Mile High on August 16, 2025 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images The story of Broncos Camp this summer has been the emergence of second-year wide receiver Pat Bryant. We saw the beginnings of this breakout last season, but it carried over into the offseason and now into camp and the preseason. He stayed healthy and was making plays throughout camp, catching everything thrown his way, and earning constant praise from the media, his teammates, and the Broncos coaching staff. That continued today when, after Monday’s practice, Sean Payton was asked about Bryant making a second-year jump this season. Pat Bryant is having a “heckuva camp,” per Sean Payton. Big-time praise for No. 13 pic.twitter.com/M8mm8OsQMY — Zac Stevens (@ZacStevens) August 24, 2026 Payton gave Bryant some big-time praise after today’s practice. He told reporters that Bryant has strong hands and once again praised his footwork and ability to not leave his feet to make a catch. He added that Bryant is smart, sudden, big, super intelligent, and that it all has been consistent throughout the summer and that he is having a “heck of a camp”. “His consistency; he has really strong hands. I’ve said this before, if you watch tape and you’re looking at it, rarely does he have to leave his feet to make a clean catch. Even if you just skip to catch it, at that moment, everyone’s moving and you’re kind of frozen, and rarely does he do that. So his yards-after-catch are noticeably different because his feet are on the ground as he runs through a ball. He’s smart, he’s sudden, he’s big. He’s having a heck of a camp. You guys have seen it, and it’s been consistent. He’s super intelligent. It’s really important to him, and I like his size.” Like Bryant’s play this summer, the praise about him has also been consistent. He entered the summer and training camp competing for the WR3 job behind star wide receiver Jaylen Waddle and veteran Courtland Sutton and will leave camp firmly as the Broncos WR3. He gives the Broncos and quarterback Bo Nix another big and physical target who can make plays all over the field. He has great hands; he is big, runs good routes, can play inside or outside, can block, and has sneaky run-after-the-catch potential. While he may not have a flashy 40-time, Payton has noted multiple times now that his feet stay on the ground and he runs through the ball. We saw this a few times in his rookie year, and I believe we will see it more this upcoming season. With Jaylen Waddle and his speed and veteran Courtland Sutton getting the majority of attention from opposing defenses, Bryant has the potential to fly under the radar a bit and be a playmaker for the Broncos this season. I think the hype is real. Bryant looks like the real deal, and I believe he will have a breakout year for the Broncos this upcoming season. I think the addition of Waddle and the breakout of Bryant will help this Broncos offense take that next step this upcoming season.
author: Scotty Payne

title: Horse Tracks: The Nix-Webb connection is working well
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country! One of the more intriguing storylines coming out of this offseason and preseason wasn’t about a player. It was that there’d be a new voice in Bo Nix’s ear. The voice of Denver’s new offensive play caller  – Davis Webb. Since it was announced that the offensive coordinator would take over […]
full_text: Good morning, Broncos Country! One of the more intriguing storylines coming out of this offseason and preseason wasn’t about a player. It was that there’d be a new voice in Bo Nix’s ear. The voice of Denver’s new offensive play caller – Davis Webb. Since it was announced that the offensive coordinator would take over play calling duties for Sean Payton this season there’s been a lot of attention paid to how it’s going. If you’re wondering, it’s going well. “[It was] about like I thought from practice. Just very smooth getting in and out of the huddle,” said quarterback Bo Nix after his first game with Webb in his ear. “[He] put us in good situations, and then it’s our job to go out there and execute. Nothing crazy. It was about like I thought, and I’m excited to see how the season goes.” Nix noted that taking direction from Webb now instead of Payton is “obviously different” but it’s also in line with his development as a quarterback. “Sean [Payton] did a really good job my first couple years not distracting me with different things, and not being extra and just giving me the play,” Nix said. “He would give me a few reminders if I needed them, but really it was just the play, and he kept me in it and it was very beneficial for me as a young kid getting in the league.” But the chemistry Nix is developing with Webb appears to be solid. “Davis understands where I’m at on my level, and he can also push me, give me a little bit more, and also be a little extra at times,” Nix said. “He’s always going to be the guy that sends me a joke [in the huddle] every once in a while and sort of keeps it lighthearted. Just as serious as this game is, it can also be fun at the same time.” Even Payton, who still reserves the right to interject his thoughts on the offensive scheme, admits the transition has gone well. “It was smooth, it was good,” he said. “Communication process was good. No issues. It was all clean.” I don’t think people quite understand that the Broncos win the SuperBowl last year if Bo Nix is healthy. Now he’s entering year 3 under Sean Payton with Davis Webb calling plays and a drastically improved roster. Watch out. pic.twitter.com/QQioEYCkkr — Denver Broncos 365 (@DailyBroncos) August 22, 2026 Guard Quinn Meinerz, who spent chunks of the offseason working with Webb, noted that even though it’s the same offense, there are new wrinkles here and there. “It’s not like a complete overhaul of the offense, but there are a lot of new fun elements, new wrinkles, new stuff to it,” Meinerz said. Tight end Adam Trautman pointed to the energy that Webb is bringing to the offense as well. “He is a little ball of energy out there honestly, and it’s pretty fun,” Trautman said. “It’s cool to get into meetings and just watch him talk about concepts, scheme, everything as a whole. For Webb, the transition hasn’t seemed like a big deal at all, talking like a veteran OC after the first preseason win against the Falcons “We’re trying to clean up some details, but I love the way we came out. Six plays, go get a touchdown,” he said. “You felt the energy on the sideline kind of go throughout the team. That’s what we want to do, and that was a good start. Now we have to go back-to-back.” That didn’t work out too well in the preseason loss to the Packers, but the good news is that Nix looked good in his series, and the chemistry Webb has developed with Nix the past two seasons as his QB coach has transitioned well with his new role. For Nix, the transition has been easy. “Honestly I feel like we picked up right where we left off. I feel like Davis is doing a really good job of communicating with me and not overcommunicating, but just give me a few things here and there, reminders, little things about a play, like, ‘Hey, don’t forget this. Hey, remember you have this,” Nix said after the first week of training camp. “It’s been really good.”

title: Detroit Lions host RB Kareem Hunt, try out two cornerbacks
summary: In one of the more fascinating visits to Allen Park, the Detroit Lions hosted former Pro Bowl running Kareem Hunt at the team facility on Tuesday, per the NFL transaction list. Hunt was a third-round pick in 2017 and immediately put together an impressive rookie season with the Kansas City Chiefs, rushing for 1,327 yards, […]
full_text: Kansas City Chiefs running back Kareem Hunt (29) scores a touchdown during the fourth quarter of an NFL football matchup at EverBank Stadium, Monday, Oct. 6, 2025, in Jacksonville, Fla. The Jacksonville Jaguars edged the Kansas City Chiefs 31-28. [Corey Perrine/Florida Times-Union] | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co In one of the more fascinating visits to Allen Park, the Detroit Lions hosted former Pro Bowl running Kareem Hunt at the team facility on Tuesday, per the NFL transaction list. Hunt was a third-round pick in 2017 and immediately put together an impressive rookie season with the Kansas City Chiefs, rushing for 1,327 yards, eight touchdowns, and 4.9 yards per carry. Unfortunately for Hunt, that would turn out to be his best career season. He has since dealt with several injuries and an ugly off-field incident where video surfaced of him assaulting a 19-year-old girl. He was promptly released by the Chiefs less than two years into his career, but never faced criminal charges. Since then, Hunt spent five seasons with the Browns before returning to the Chiefs in 2024. He has had three seasons where he eclipsed 700 rushing yards (2018, 2020, 2024) and is coming off a pretty strong season in which he somewhat ironically outpaced new Lions running back Isiah Pacheco. In 2024, Hunt rushed for 611 yards, 3.7 yards per carry, and eight touchdowns. Pacheco only managed 462 yards and a single rushing touchdown despite starting 12 games. The reasoning for the Lions’ presumed interest in Hunt is not entirely clear. Detroit did recently lose two running backs in their latest preseason game. Raheem Blackshear was placed on injured reserved and promptly released with an injury settlement, while Jabari Small suffered a concussion against the Commanders. The Lions still have Jahmyr Gibbs, Sione Vaki, Jacob Saylors, Trayveon Williams and newly signed Roydell Williams healthy, but they may not want to play most of those players in their preseason finale on Saturday. The one unknown is the health of presumed RB2 Isiah Pacheco. The veteran running back has been sidelined with an MCL sprain, but at the time, coach Dan Campbell said they weren’t fearful of that threatening his start to the regular season. “We feel pretty good about him being ready to go, certainly when the season gets here,” Campbell said two weeks ago. “So, I’m not concerned about that.” On top of that, the Lions also hosted two cornerbacks for a tryout: Shaun Jolly and Eric Scott. Jolly went undrafted out of Appalachian State in 2022 and spent three seasons with the Rams—appearing in six games—before losing his entire 2025 season to injury. At 5-foot-9, 180 pounds, Jolly has some versatility to play on the outside and inside. Scott is more of a pure outside cornerback at 6-foot-2, 197 pounds. He has yet to make his first NFL appearance since being drafted by the Cowboys in the sixth round back in 2023, but he’s spent time on both Dallas’ and Kansas City’s practice squad.
author: Jeremy Reisman

title: Detroit Lions training camp Day 17 observations: Takeaways from each drill
summary: Entering the Detroit Lions’ final week of training camp, practices are more important than ever. It’s one of the final opportunities for the starters to build chemistry and shake rust. And for the rest of the crew, it’s a chance to leave a lasting impression. Here’s what I noticed from a lengthy Day 17 of […]
full_text: Detroit Lions cornerback D.J. Reed (4), center, practices next to cornerback Rock Ya-Sin (23) and cornerback Ennis Rakestraw Jr. (2) during training camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Thursday, July 30, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Entering the Detroit Lions’ final week of training camp, practices are more important than ever. It’s one of the final opportunities for the starters to build chemistry and shake rust. And for the rest of the crew, it’s a chance to leave a lasting impression. Here’s what I noticed from a lengthy Day 17 of Lions camp. There was a lot of injury news, so make sure you’re caught up on all of that here. 11-on-11s, part 1 Screens galore The Lions offense ran several bubble screens, normal screens, and tosses in this section. Clearly, they are trying to get their playmakers the ball in their hands with a bunch of open space. And with an athletic group of offensive linemen, they can often get blockers downfield in a hurry to take out some linebackers and defensive backs. Malcolm Rodriguez vs. Devin White heats up There is clearly a competition brewing for the starting WILL linebacker role alongside Jack Campbell and Derrick Barnes. Rodriguez and White have been sharing first- and second-team reps for the past week or so, and on Tuesday they often shared the field at the same time alongside Campbell in three linebacker sets. Additionally, with Trevor Nowaske leaving practice early, both seemed to get double the reps with the second team. It feels like the staff is intentionally trying to douse both with reps to see who wins. Rodriguez had a nice sideline-to-sideline pursuit on a toss play, while White shined more later in practice. Hello, Ben Bartch Bartch has had trouble staying on the field, leading to him falling out of the starting left guard competition. But on Tuesday, he reminded media why the Lions were hopeful of him. He delivered one of the most punishing downfield blocks in camp, plowing over White on a screen play. Bartch is unlikely to take the starting job away from Christian Mahogany, but if he can put together a strong week of camp, a good preseason finale, and stay on the field, it’s possible that the position battle continues into the season. 11s, part 2 Sione Vaki bounces back Early in practice, Vaki got chewed out after failing to finish a run. But in the next set of 11-on-11s, he flashed some of his offensive potential on back-to-back plays. On the first, he absorbed a huge hit from a blitzing Jack Campbell, but he regrouped himself, squared up, and kept Campbell at bay. The pocket stayed clear and Jared Goff connected with a wide-open Amon-Ra St. Brown for 20+ yards. On the second play, Vaki found the soft spot in the zone between Campbell and White for a conversion on third-and-5ish. After the sequence, Vaki got a ton of love from running backs coach Tashard Choice. Jameson Williams screen is dangerous Without getting into too many details, let’s just say that if the Lions can run the kind of WR screen they did in Tuesday’s practice, Jameson Williams is a danger for a house call. That’s exactly what he did on this play, and while it looked for a second like D.J. Reed may catch him, Jamo’s speed is just different. OL vs. DL drills Interior offensive line starts to settle in While the offensive line has to work on chemistry more than anything, I thought the 1-on-1 performance from Detroit’s projected interior offensive linemen was highly encouraging. Mahogany managed the strength of Alim McNeill on his rep, Juice Scruggs absolutely swallowed Tyleik Williams, and Tate Ratledge put Skyler Gill-Howard on the ground. Then, when they were working on defending stunts, Mahogany and Penei Sewell easily took care of Aidan Hutchinson and McNeill in back-to-back reps. It was more of a split between Blake Miller/Ratledge vs. Gill-Howard/DJ Wonnum, but I would still tip the scales in the offensive line’s favor. Tyler Lacy is STRONG About a week ago, Lions coach Dan Campbell noted how Lacy—and Levi Onwuzurike—were likely the two strongest players on the defensive line. On Wednesday, Lacy showed that by just slowly and steadily shoving Larry Borom into the pocket. Aidan Hutchinson vs. Penei Sewell is cinema Hutchinson kicked off the rep with his nasty spin move, getting inside of Sewell for the sack. When the two lined up a second time, Hutchinson decided to just give him pure power, and the defensive end was able to get Sewell pretty far back into the pocket. However, Sewell eventually found his anchor, and I gave him the slight win. Special teams — gunners vs. jammers 3 winners As always, Vaki stood out as a big winner from these reps, beating Jacob Saylors pretty handily with a nice re-anchor as a jammer, freeing the return man for a nice rushing lane. In perhaps the biggest upset of the day, I had rookie defensive back Keith Abney winning both of his reps (as a gunner and jammer) against special teams ace Khalil Dorsey. I’m not accustomed to seeing Dorsey lose a single rep, let alone back-to-backs. Lucky Jackson, who is fighting for a reserve receiver role, also won both of his reps… against struggling cornerback Ennis Rakestraw. Situational drills The Lions ran three situational drills. Here are the results of each: Situation 1 (first teamers): Tied 20-20 51 seconds left Offense has the ball on its own 40-yard line 3 timeouts The offense gained just 18 yards on six plays, but it was enough to get Jake Bates to try a 60-yard field goal, and he nailed it for the win. Situation 2 (second teamers): Tied 20-20 51 seconds left Offense has the ball on its own 40-yard line 3 timeouts A big 21-yard pickup by Tay Martin immediately put the offense in scoring position, and Bates drilled a 47-yard field goal to win. Situation 3 (first teamers): Offense down 21-30 Starting on the opponent’s 18-yard line 3:31 left 3 timeouts It took a while, but the first-team offense scored on a 1-yard Jared Goff QB sneak. After the second-team offense was forced into a three-and-out on three straight runs, the offense got the ball back down 2 points with 1:42 left on their own 16-yard line. Two Aidan Hutchinson sacks later, a pass slipped through Jahmyr Gibbs’ hands for a game-sealing interception by D.J. Reed. Now, some takeaways from these drives: Rock Ya-Sin dominates Locked in Rock! pic.twitter.com/oiSRuwJVBs — Detroit Lions (@Lions) August 25, 2026 Ya-Sin started these drills with a nice pass breakup on a wheel route to St. Brown. Then he forced the incomplete pass to Isaac TeSlaa (as seen above) on third down to force the 60-yard field goal attempt. But his best work was done in the red zone against St. Brown. He blanketed the veteran receiver on a post route and gave him hell on another—but was called for defensive pass interference. For the entire day, I had Ya-Sin with a sack and/or pressure and three pass breakups—and I didn’t even watch 7-on-7s. Aidan Hutchinson calls game I already alluded to it, but Hutchinson logged two sacks during team drills, probably should’ve been credited with another, and had a pocket collapsing pressure that forced an incomplete pass. This is coming against both Miller and Sewell. Skyler Gill-Howard with plenty of first-team work On top of repping against starters in one-on-ones, rookie defensive tackle Skyler Gill-Howard saw a ton of work with the first-team defense during end-of-game drills, as Detroit clearly trusts him in a pass-rushing role right now. Admittedly, he wasn’t nearly as disruptive as he has been against second-teamers, but it’s still encouraging to see him get that work. Miscellaneous: Jake Bates’ day: Makes: 34, 40, 44; 39, 44; 60, 47, XP Misses: 49, 49 (again… I think) Keith Abney got nearly all of the first-team nickel reps with Christian Izien sidelined. I thought it was one of his best practices, with strong red zone coverage against St. Brown, as well. He forced an incompletion on one play, then followed it up by keeping St. Brown short of the goal line on…

title: Lions injury news: Sam LaPorta returns, Detroit short on safeties
summary: As the Detroit Lions returned to the practice field for the first time in nearly a week, there were a lot of new developments when it comes to the team’s injury situation. Let’s get into it. Returned to practice: The headline is Sam LaPorta returning to practice after suffering a hip injury last week. Last […]
full_text: Detroit Lions tight end Sam LaPorta warms up during training camp at Detroit Lions Headquarters and Training Facility in Allen Park on Monday, July 24, 2023. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co As the Detroit Lions returned to the practice field for the first time in nearly a week, there were a lot of new developments when it comes to the team’s injury situation. Let’s get into it. Returned to practice: TE Sam LaPorta (hip) G Ben Bartch (concussion) The headline is Sam LaPorta returning to practice after suffering a hip injury last week. Last we heard from Dan Campbell, LaPorta’s injury could have leaked into the regular seasons, but the Lions tight end not only returned but got plenty of team reps during Tuesday’s practice. Lions fans can take a deep breath. Bartch also returned from concussion protocol and served as the team’s second-string left guard all practice. As someone on the roster bubble, his return is huge for his chances to make the 53. Injured during practice/left early LB Trevor Nowaske DB Nick Whiteside S Dan Jackson Note: The team did not provide any official updates on these players after practice Nowaske left practice very early before any team drills started, as trainers were looking at his lower body. Eventually he walked off with a limp under his own power. Jackson also left practice early. I did not see if anything happened to him, but it’s worth noting he left Saturday’s preseason game early, so this may have been a planned limited practice for him. As for Whiteside, he played for most of practice, but during the final few drills he was walking around with a trainer. It’s unclear what he was dealing with, but he, too, eventually walked to the locker room under his own power. Working with trainer LB Jimmy Rolder (leg) The Lions rookie linebacker continues to get daily work with a trainer, and even spent the last segment of practice standing on the sidelines with his teammates. Campbell did say last week that he doesn’t believe Rolder will return to practice before the end of training camp, but it’s clear he’s getting close. Not practicing: RB Isiah Pacheco (knee) RB Jabari Small (concussion) OT Giovanni Manu (NFI) C Cade Mays (wrist) G Michael Niese (leg) OL Miles Frazier (undisclosed) EDGE Payton Turner (back) LB Damone Clark (undisclosed) S Thomas Harper (ankle) S Christian Izien (undisclosed) S Kerby Joseph (PUP, knee) S Brian Branch (PUP, Achilles) Let’s start at the bottom, because the Lions are severely shorthanded at safety right now. Joseph and Branch remain on the PUP list, and Campbell said Joseph is still away from the team (dealing with a personal issue), but is expected back soon. Unfortunately, much of Detroit’s safety depth is currently depleted. Harper has missed a few practices, and Campbell revealed on Tuesday that he’s dealing with an ankle injury that will likely keep him out for the rest of the week. “Could he be ready this weekend? I think it’s unlikely, but you never know,” Campbell said. Christian Izien, who has mostly been playing nickel as of late, was also out from practice, although it’s unclear if he’s dealing with an injury. Izien played five defensive snaps and seven special teams reps in the preseason game on Saturday. Add Dan Jackson to the injury list, and the Lions were essentially down five safeties. And the one person they had borrowed from another position—Whiteside, who logged a few safety reps in the preseason—also left practice early. Don’t be surprised if the Lions opt to add some late reinforcements for Saturday’s preseason finale. Elsewhere, Niese missed practice after leaving Saturday’s game in crutches. Detroit signed center Gus Hartwig to help their depth there. Miles Frazier was gone with an unexplained absence, leaving Mason Miller and Ben Bartch to play as the second-team guards.
author: Jeremy Reisman

title: Detroit Lions sign C Gus Hartwig; Damone Clark to IR
summary: The Detroit Lions have just three training camp practices and one preseason game remaining in their offseason before they need to make final cuts on Sunday. On Tuesday, they announced they signed center Gus Hartwig to their 90-man roster and placed veteran linebacker Damone Clark on injured reserve. Hartwig was a 48-game starter at Purdue, […]
full_text: Jun 11, 2025; Florham Park, NY, USA; New York Jets center Gus Hartwig (63) and defensive tackle Fatorma Mulbah (62) participate in a drill during minicamp at Atlantic Health Jets Training Center. Mandatory Credit: John Jones-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Detroit Lions have just three training camp practices and one preseason game remaining in their offseason before they need to make final cuts on Sunday. On Tuesday, they announced they signed center Gus Hartwig to their 90-man roster and placed veteran linebacker Damone Clark on injured reserve. Hartwig was a 48-game starter at Purdue, and after going undrafted in 2025, he signed with the New York Jets. Unfortunately, he suffered an early camp leg injury and spent his rookie season on injured reserve. He began the offseason with the Jets, but was released after spring camp. Primarily a zone-based center, Hartwig won with intelligence and lateral foot quickness at Purdue, but, similar to Lions reserve center Seth McLaughlin, he struggled with his anchor against power in pass protection. With starting center Cade Mays out with a wrist injury, and reserve center Michael suffering a leg injury—and was spotted on crutches in the locker room —in last Saturday’s preseason game, the Lions only had two true centers on the roster: presumed interim starter Juice Scruggs and McLaughlin. The addition of Hartwig will allow the Lions to roll three offensive lines for the final week of training camp, and if he impresses, he could earn a spot on the practice squad. By placing Clark on injured reserve, he will be lost for the season unless the team reaches an injury settlement with him at a later date. However, with coach Dan Campbell noting that Clark is “done indefinitely,” it’s also likely he will spend the season on Detroit’s injured reserve. Clark opened training camp amongst the Lions’ top-6 linebackers and looked like he had a real chance to contribute. However, while he has been sidelined, the Lions signed Devin White and have seen several reserve linebackers level up their game, including Erick Hunter, Joe Bachie, and Troy Reeder. With Clark now out of the picture—and if rookie Jimmy Rolder starts the season on injured reserve/return—it could open up a great opportunity for one of the three reserves to find their way onto the 53-man roster.
author: Erik Schlitt

title: Detroit Lions injury updates: Veteran LB out ‘indefinitely’
summary: As the Detroit Lions kick off their final week of training camp, coach Dan Campbell kicked off Tuesday afternoon with an injury update on two players who have missed some time as of late: linebacker Damone Clark and safety Thomas Harper. Clark has been out of practice for several weeks now, and Campbell shared the […]
full_text: Aug 3, 2026; Allen Park, MI, USA; Detroit Lions linebacker Damone Clark (11) participates in a linebacker drill during Detroit Lions training camp. Mandatory Credit: Paul Barnick-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect As the Detroit Lions kick off their final week of training camp, coach Dan Campbell kicked off Tuesday afternoon with an injury update on two players who have missed some time as of late: linebacker Damone Clark and safety Thomas Harper. Clark has been out of practice for several weeks now, and Campbell shared the bad news on why. Apparently, the injury he suffered is quite serious. “He is done indefinitely,” Campbell said. “This injury took place, shoot, man, three weeks ago, two weeks ago. So, unfortunately, it’s significant enough where he’ll be out indefinitely.” It’s a tough blow for Clark, who was in line for a reserve role in Detroit’s stacked linebacker room. He was regularly repping with the second-team defense and has a ton of experience on special teams, so he seemed likely to grab a spot on the 53-man roster. The good news for Detroit is that they have plenty of depth in that room, and most of them have experience on special teams. Troy Reeder is a seven-year vet with 1,750 special teams snaps. Joe Bachie has 1,128 snaps on special teams over six seasons. Amen Ogbongbemiga has 1,431 snaps over five seasons. This could also be an opportunity for undrafted rookie Erick Hunter to slide onto the 53-man roster following some flashy plays in both training camp and the preseason. As for Harper, the news is much more positive. While he’s dealing with an ankle injury, it doesn’t sound like it will keep him out too much longer. “Could he be ready this week? I think it’s unlikely, but you never know,” Campbell said. With Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph still on the Physically Unable to Perform list and likely to stay there for the start of the season, Harper is the primary depth behind temporary starter Avonte Maddox and Chuck Clark. That said, the Lions also have Christian Izien and Dan Jackson.
author: Jeremy Reisman

title: Detroit Lions roster bubble predictions: Big decision coming at linebacker
summary: We’re less than a week away from NFL roster cuts, and the Detroit Lions defense is starting to separate the wheat from the chaff. Don’t get me wrong, there are still positions up for grabs and players who can make a final push for the roster. But every week our staff has been making 53-man […]
full_text: ALLEN PARK, MICHIGAN - JULY 29: Roy Lopez #51 and Jimmy Rolder #41 of the Detroit Lions walk together during Detroit Lions Training Camp at Detroit Lions Meijer Performance Center on July 29, 2026 in Allen Park, Michigan. (Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images) | Getty Images We’re less than a week away from NFL roster cuts, and the Detroit Lions defense is starting to separate the wheat from the chaff. Don’t get me wrong, there are still positions up for grabs and players who can make a final push for the roster. But every week our staff has been making 53-man roster predictions for the defensive players, and we’re all starting to converge on our opinions of these players. Maybe some of it is groupthink, but I think the more likely scenario is that there’s actually some serious clarity on how things will shake out. However, there is one exception. The linebacking corps is particularly hard to predict, and our staff seems to be split in two directions. Here are our latest predictions for the players on the roster bubble, and a full explanation of each position below. View Link Defensive end : Assumed in: Aidan Hutchinson, DJ Wonnum, Derrick Moore Ahmed Hassanein: 11 “IN” votes (no change) Payton Turner: 0 votes (no change) Anthony Lucas: 0 votes New to bubble watch: Eric O’Neill (0 votes) The only change here is that Eric O’Neill has worked his way onto the roster bubble after a very strong week. It started with a pick-six in training camp, and ended with a few disruptive snaps against the Commanders in Saturday’s preseason game. None of us have been able to find a roster spot for him, but he could be a late riser or a priority spot on the practice squad. Defensive tackle: Assumed in: Alim McNeill, Tyleik Williams Levi Onwuzurike: 11 votes (no change) Tyler Lacy: 11 votes (no change) Skyle Gill-Howard: 11 votes (no change) Chris Smith: 10 votes (no change) Mekhi Wingo: 1 vote (up 1) Tyre West: 0 votes (no change) NEW TO BUBBLE WATCH: Ben Stille (0 votes) Two small changes here. First, Mekhi Wingo gets a vote back this week after finally getting back on the field and having a pretty disruptive preseason game. It’ll still be tough for him to find a spot on the roster given how well Skyler Gill-Howard—a very similar player—has played, but he’s certainly back in the conversation. I also added Ben Stille to the roster bubble this week. He has been repping very high in camp, has played just about every spot along the defensive line, and has been pretty darn disruptive for over a week now. I do wonder if he could challenge for a spot currently held by Chris Smith or even warrant consideration as an 11th defensive lineman. Linebacker: Assumed in: Jack Campbell, Derrick Barnes, Malcolm Rodriguez Devin White: 11 votes (no change) Trevor Nowaske: 10 votes (no change) Jimmy Rolder: 8 votes (up 8) Damone Clark: 2 votes (down 6) Troy Reeder: 1 vote (no change) Erick Hunter: 0 votes (no change) Joe Bachie: 0 votes (no change) The status of Jimmy Rolder remains one of the biggest decisions the Lions need to make. Last week, he was hopeful he’d return from injury for the final week of training camp, but a few days later coach Dan Campbell shut that down. Regardless, it certainly seems like he’s almost healthy enough to return to practice. But should the Lions place him on injured reserve (to return) anyway? He’s a rookie who has missed nearly all of training camp. Would he even play in the first four games if healthy? But you’d only be pushing back his development by placing him on IR, where he wouldn’t be able to practice for those four weeks, either. It’s a tough decision, but right now, most of the staff is opting to keep him off IR. Making that decision a little easier is the fact that Damone Clark has now missed well over a week of practice. The veteran linebacker was zeroing in on a key reserve and special teams role, but he’s now missed a considerable amount of time, and Detroit has a few other veterans on the roster who may have jumped him, including Troy Reeder, Joe Bachie, and Amen Ogbongbemiga. Cornerback: Assumed in: DJ Reed, Rock Ya-Sin, Keith Abney Ennis Rakestraw: 11 votes Nick Whiteside: 11 votes (no change) Roger McCreary: 11 votes (no change) Khalil Dorsey: 9 votes (no change) Surprisingly, no change here. Whiteside had a tough preseason game, but his extremely strong training camp supersedes that. Rakestraw had an injury scare (again), but managed to play in the preseason game as he clings to a roster spot. McCreary has been one of the Lions’ best cornerbacks in the preseason, even though he hasn’t flashed a ton at camp. I still continue to believe Dorsey is a lock as a special teams ace, but I can understand that this room looks awfully crowded with seven players. Safety Assumed in: Christian Izien, Avonte Maddox, Chuck Clark Thomas Harper: 11 votes (no change) Dan Jackson: 0 votes (down 1) Brian Branch: 0 votes (no change) Kerby Joseph: 0 votes (no change) The only thing that could possibly shake up this room is if the Lions unexpectedly activate Brian Branch or Kerby Joseph from the Physically Unable to Perform list. But our last update from Campbell seemed to suggest neither will be ready to start the season .
author: Jeremy Reisman

title: UPDATE: Detroit Lions new 2026 ‘Rivalries’ uniform leaked
summary: The long-awaited Detroit Lions “Rivalries” uniform is scheduled to be unveiled on Tuesday, Aug. 25. But it looks like Fox News may have leaked them before any team had a chance to announce them. In a post featuring an image straight from Fanatics, the news website revealed jerseys from all eight teams (every team from […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - DECEMBER 21: The NFL logo is pictured on a uniform during the game between the Detroit Lions and Pittsburgh Steelers at Ford Field on December 21, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images) | Getty Images The long-awaited Detroit Lions “Rivalries” uniform is scheduled to be unveiled on Tuesday, Aug. 25. But it looks like Fox News may have leaked them before any team had a chance to announce them. In a post featuring an image straight from Fanatics, the news website revealed jerseys from all eight teams (every team from the NFC North, AFC South) who will have “Rivalries” uniforms this season. SEE THE 2026 NFL RIVALRIES UNIFORMS HERE UPDATE: The Lions made the drop official at 10 a.m. ET, with this promotional video, pairing the leaked jersey with gray pants and the alternate blue helmet: Every opponent is an intruder. pic.twitter.com/LcMzpfIjuu — Detroit Lions (@Lions) August 25, 2026 The Lions also have a completely photo gallery of the new uniforms here. And they have a website just for the new uniforms, breaking down all the choices they made. The new design—which rotates through NFL divisions every year—features mostly an all-white jersey with a sleek design on the shoulder and the trademarked Honolulu Blue displayed with “DETROIT” stamped just above the player number. It’s unclear which pants the Lions would wear with this jersey. Here’s an official explanation of the Lions’ design: “Takes a futuristic approach to Lions identity, pairing Honolulu blue with carbon-fiber-inspired numbers that nod to the city’s automotive and racing heritage. Lion-eye shoulder details reinforce the team’s ‘Defend the Den’ mentality.” It’s a pretty unique look that doesn’t really resemble anything they’ve worn recently, which could either be a positive or negative, depending on your outlook. It certainly is different , but time will tell whether fans like it or not. Earlier this month, the Lions announced that they would wear these uniforms for their home Week 8 matchup against the Minnesota Vikings on Nov. 1. Coincidentally, the Vikings will be wearing their version of the “Rivalries” uniform when they host the Lions in Week 15—currently scheduled to be the “Sunday Night Football” game that week (Dec. 20). title: Detroit Lions film breakdown: Rookies Derrick Moore, Skyler Gill-Howard bolster run defense
summary: When asked what he needs to see in the preseason to feel good about the 2026 season, Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell said this: “I want to know that we can run the football. I want to know we can stop the run. And I want to know that we’re ready for situational football. Probably […]
full_text: When asked what he needs to see in the preseason to feel good about the 2026 season, Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell said this: “I want to know that we can run the football. I want to know we can stop the run. And I want to know that we’re ready for situational football. Probably those three things, if you want me to feel comfortable. The other stuff will come.” Let’s back up for a second and focus on the second sentence of that quote. I want to know we can stop the run. That’s something this regime has hung their hat on since the beginning back in 2021 when Campbell and general manager Brad Holmes were hired with the task of making Detroit a winner. Unfortunately for everyone involved, they couldn’t do either consistently down the stretch of the 2025 season, and it became a major factor in their frustrating 9-8 finish. As most could have predicted, 2025’s failures reignited something in the ultra-competitive Campbell, prompting him to get his team back to some of the basics they first relied on back in 2022 and 2023. To put it simply, Detroit wants to get back to imposing their will along the line of scrimmage, and defensively, that starts with being excellent against the run. And while it was only a preseason game in August, the Lions’ defense held Washington to just 35 yards on 17 carries. In this week’s film review, we will be taking a look at how two rookie defensive linemen, edge defender Derrick Moore and defensive tackle Skyler Gill-Howard, contributed to the Lions’ defensive dominance against the Commanders. Derrick Moore When the Lions drafted Moore in the second round of the 2026 NFL Draft, it felt like a portion of the fanbase breathed a deep sigh of relief. Along with the addition of veteran DJ Wonnum, drafting Moore felt like Holmes and his staff were putting a priority on rushing the passer. Still, we know in order to play for Campbell—and for defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard—you better be able to play the run, regardless of whether you can sack the quarterback on third down or not. And at 6-foot-3 and 260 pounds, with long, powerfully built arms, Moore is a do-it-all player on the edge. In his preseason debut against the Commanders, not only did he record a sack and a quarterback hit, but he was sound and violent against the run, too. In our first clip for Moore, we get a glimpse of the power that made him such a productive player at Michigan. Detroit counters the 12 personnel (one running back and two tight ends) with a five-man front that has both Moore and linebacker Trevor Nowaske in two-point stances outside the tight ends. Right before the ball is snapped, you will see Moore, circled in red, take a few steps down the line of scrimmage, while linebacker Joe Bachie fills in to set the edge in the run-fit. Moore jolts the Washington tackle into the backfield, forcing the running back to change direction before he is stopped for no gain on the play. In our next play below, Washington is once again under center in 12-personnel, with Moore in a two-point stance outside of the right tackle. The Commanders attempt to stretch the run out towards the right side of the screen, but Nowaske, Bachie, and defensive lineman Ben Stille cave in the left side of the offensive line, once again forcing the runner to try and reverse field… right into the waiting arms of Moore, who does an excellent job of staying disciplined on the backside of the run. Lastly, we have something that won’t show up in the box score, but it showed up a few times in the Washington film. Being the physical force on the edge that teams will certainly attempt to “cut” when they can. Executed properly, a “cut block” is a useful tool that can be used by offensive skill players as a means to get larger, stronger defenders on the ground, making it something defenders must prepare for in today’s NFL. And just like he did in the clip below, Moore disposed of multiple cut attempts against Washington with ease. He executes perfect technique by defeating the block with his hands while keeping his eyes up where they need to be. If we can see more of this from the rookie on a consistent basis, there should be a nice rotation between Moore and Wonnum at the edge spot opposite Hutchinson. Skyler Gill-Howard From a stature standpoint, Gill-Howard is a different kind of player than his teammates at defensive tackle. At 6-foot and 280 pounds, he is shorter and lighter than the likes of Alim McNeill (6-foot-2, 310 pounds) and Tyleik Williams (6-foot-3, 325 pounds). To make up for that, the rookie defensive tackle has to play faster, as well as be more technically sound than his opponents if he wants to consistently win against NFL-caliber offensive linemen. From a coaching standpoint, that also means putting someone like Gill-Howard in positions to utilize his unique skill set. In this particular clip, we can see him lined up at the three-technique on the left side of the screen. Once the ball is snapped, the left guard immediately fires off and attempts to climb to the second level in order to reach the linebacker. Seeing this, Gill-Howard wastes no time getting across the face of the left tackle, who tried, and failed, to cut the rookie off, allowing him to make the tackle on the ball carrier for a loss on the play. In our final clip of the study, we see a similar instance to the play above. Gill-Howard is at the three-technique on the outside shoulder of the right guard. The guard climbs up to the off-ball linebacker, while the right tackle is tasked with reaching the three-technique. It’s a tough block for anyone to execute, let alone against someone with the quickness of Gill-Howard. However, Gill-Howard gets his feet caught up, causing him to lose his footing and go down to the turf. It’s certainly nitpicky, but coaches will always tell you that good football players stay off the ground. If he can continue to show that he can hold up against the run, I think he can potentially carve out a role for himself as a situational interior pass-rusher on obvious throwing downs. Overall, it was an impressive performance from both of the rookie defensive linemen. They were effective and made plays in both the passing and running games. Now it’s time to build on those performances heading into the third and final week of the 2026 preseason. If you’ve missed any of our other film breakdowns from the Lions preseason, make sure to check out: How the Lions are finding their own way to play more nickel Juice Scruggs makes case for starting role at center

title: Discussion: Which Detroit Lions player needs a final training camp push the most?
summary: Detroit Lions training camp is nearly over. This week—from Tuesday to Thursday—the Lions will take part in the three final practices of 2026 training camp. It’s the final opportunity for players on the roster bubble to make their case for the 53-man roster in the lead-up to the preseason finale on Saturday afternoon. Roster cuts […]
full_text: Detroit Lions cornerback Ennis Rakestraw Jr. (2) practices during training camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Wednesday, July 29, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Detroit Lions training camp is nearly over. This week—from Tuesday to Thursday—the Lions will take part in the three final practices of 2026 training camp. It’s the final opportunity for players on the roster bubble to make their case for the 53-man roster in the lead-up to the preseason finale on Saturday afternoon. Roster cuts will take place in the 24 hours after the game. Sometimes leaving a final impression late in the game can be the difference between playing on Sundays and looking for a new job entirely. It not only stays fresh in coaches’ minds, but it also shows the ability to grow and evolve throughout the course of training camp. There are a ton of players sitting on the Lions’ roster bubble right now, but which one would benefit most from a late push? Today’s Question of the Day is: Which Lions player needs a strong finish to camp more than anyone else? My answer: I’ll list a few. On offense, it feels like both quarterbacks are still very much jockeying for the backup quarterback job. I still believe Josh Dobbs is the favorite due to his experience, but after making a few critical mistakes in the preseason opener, he needs to finish strong to maintain that spot. Luke Altmyer has certainly surpassed expectations, but he’s cooled a little since his hot start. Additionally, I’m looking for anyone amongst the receiver group to stand out and challenge front-runner Tay Martin for the WR5 role. With Cedrick Wilson Jr. now on injured reserve , that competition is wide open. Players like Dominic Lovett, Lucky Jackson, and Tarik Black should have more opportunities now, and they need to take full advantage. On defense, it’s all about the linebacking corps to me. With Damone Clark and Jimmy Rolder still sidelined with injury, the likes of Erick Hunter, Troy Reeder, and Joe Bachie will continue to get a ton of reps and need to finish strong to land a spot on the 53-man roster. Finally, there’s cornerback. More so than anyone else, I think Ennis Rakestraw needs to finish strong here. It’s been a rough camp for him, and while he had a decent set of practices last week, it ended with an injury and a nondescript performance in the preseason game. I don’t know if his roster spot is truly up for grabs, but a strong finish would certainly give some peace of mind that he’s improving and could eventually challenge for a starting primary backup role. title: Explaining the Green Bay Packers’ new 3-safety package
summary: I’ve been getting some questions about the Green Bay Packers’ “three-safety package,” and how it’s different — if at all — from the team’s Nickel package. After all, if we’re playing a third safety in the slot in Nickel, a role that Javon Bullard has usually played, then how is this package any different? I’m […]
full_text: Kamal Hadden #36 of the Green Bay Packers holds a football during training camp at Ray Nitschke Field in Ashwaubenon, Wisconsin, on August 2, 2026. (Photo by Ross Harried/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images I’ve been getting some questions about the Green Bay Packers’ “three-safety package,” and how it’s different — if at all — from the team’s Nickel package. After all, if we’re playing a third safety in the slot in Nickel, a role that Javon Bullard has usually played, then how is this package any different? I’m hoping to answer that question today, with the help of some screenshots from the Packers’ most recent game against the Denver Broncos — when Green Bay played a lot of three-safety looks after primarily showing a blitzing Nickel front in Week 1 of the preseason. First, let’s outline what a typical Nickel looks like, so we can compare and contrast. Typical Nickel Here’s a look at the Packers’ Nickel package, which, to be clear, they still use a lot against three-receiver looks. You’re all probably used to this. Green Bay is playing four players on the line of scrimmage, two off-ball linebackers, two safeties (one is just off-screen here), two outside cornerbacks and a true slot defender (Javon Bullard in this case). In this particular down, Lukas Van Ness, usually an edge rusher, kicked inside (more on this later) because it was a third and long. Still, generally the Packers play two 300-pounders on the interior and two edge defenders on the line. To make it short and simple, a Nickel defense is basically a 4-3 with a slot defender subbing out the strong-side outside linebacker, from a personnel perspective, so that the fifth defensive back can match up against a slot receiver instead of a linebacker. 3-Safety Penny: The Front To explain what is being called the Packers’ “three-safety” look (and maybe we need to just call it “Penny”), I want to look at the front first. Notice anything different? Yes, there are five guys on the line of scrimmage. Instead of two interior linemen, there are three of them, and they’re all 300-pounders. So far, I haven’t seen a player like Lukas Van Ness (usually the guy Green Bay kicks in) on the interior, unlike in their Nickel packages. There’s a half-ton of human flesh from B-gap to B-gap when the Packers play their “three-safety Penny.” The reason Green Bay is calling this defense is to actually stop the run against three-receiver sets, not to get after the quarterback. Right now, with the games NFL offenses can play with big receivers functionally inserting as tight ends, this is called to help give the defense a little bit of an advantage in the run game. By keeping that extra interior lineman on the field, though, it comes at a cost. You’re essentially playing a 3-4 on the line of scrimmage in Penny, compared to a 4-3 on the line of scrimmage in Nickel. If what would be the Sam linebacker comes out for the slot defender in Nickel, then who comes out for the Packers’ 3-4 defense when they go into Penny? That’s where things get interesting. If you look at the screenshot above, Green Bay keeps a player on each edge, but the players are Will linebacker Edgerrin Cooper (left) and edge rusher Lukas Van Ness (right). So instead of pulling off a 300-pounder (or two, depending on if LVN kicks inside) from the 3-4 base defense to play Nickel, the Packers take off a true edge defender so that the slot defender can get on the field. At this point, you’re probably piecing together why it’s more of a run-defending front than a pass-rushing front, not just because there’s five players on the line of scrimmage but also because there’s only one true edge rusher among them — compared to Nickel looks where there’s two or three on the field at once. With the first-team defense, Cooper plays the role of the second edge defender. For whatever it’s worth, when the Packers play their second-team units and below, though, they just take off the Will linebacker and play a second edge defender and roll with just one “true” linebacker. My guess on why: They don’t want to take Cooper off the field, because he’s a good football player. It will be interesting to see if this is a package they use when Micah Parsons comes back, because the question then becomes if they will sit Cooper, Parsons or Van Ness for the rep, as it’s difficult for them to keep all three on the field at the same time, unless Van Ness kicks inside (which, again, is something they haven’t done in this package). 3-Safety Penny: The Backfield Okay, now that we’ve talked about the front, it’s finally time to talk about the backfield. The screenshot below is from the same play as our front explanation. This is why this is being called the “three-safety” package. The Packers already had three safeties on the field in Nickel, as Bullard has been the primary starter in the slot going on his third season. It’s not the personnel; it’s the shape of the defense that is driving the name “three-safety” in Green Bay. Green Bay plays split safeties at around 8 to 10 yards from the line of scrimmage, which includes the “slot” defender, but then has Xavier McKinney playing the post in the deep middle of the field on top of that. Most of the time on broadcast looks, McKinney is so deep that he’s not caught on the television screen at all. Here’s an interesting quirk to this package: The slot defender is treated differently from the safety position, from a personnel standpoint. One of the “split” safeties in this package (with the first-team defense) is always Evan Williams (the number two safety). The other “split” safety is the slot defender. Sometimes, the next man up in the slot isn’t the next man up at “true” safety, but the slot still gets the looks as a split safety in these Penny snaps. Here’s the pecking order at safety ( from our full Packers depth chart that was updated after Week 2 ): Xavier McKinney Evan Williams Javon Bullard Kitan Oladapo Mark Perry Murvin Kenion III Trey Dean III Tra Fluellen Here’s the pecking order at slot defender, including the “third safety” role in Penny: Bullard Kamal Hadden Oladapo Jaylin Simpson So while Oladapo is the next man up at “true safety,” if there were another injury while Bullard was out, it’s Hadden, officially listed as a cornerback on the Packers’ roster, who is getting these looks as the preferred split safety in Penny while Bullard is sidelined. In Week 2 of the preseason, Hadden exclusively played the slot/“third safety” role for Green Bay, getting zero total reps at either outside cornerback or “true” safety in his preseason debut. Here’s something I want to bring up, because it will almost certainly come up during the season. When the offense spreads out the Penny defense, it essentially forces the defense to declare how many players they are rushing. Basically, the three interior defensive linemen are always coming on a rush. The question is whether both edge defenders will come, leaving the defense with just six in coverage (compared to the typical seven on non-blitzes), or if one will drop, leaving the defense with just one edge rusher adding to the 300-pounders trying to hunt after the quarterback. Spreading the Penny defense out helps to force the defense to declare their intentions. Above is an example of an empty look against the Penny. As you can see, Cooper, playing the role of zone-dropping edge defender, ends up split from the formation and actually outside two eligible targets. What’s left behind on the line of scrimmage is one true edge defender (Van Ness) and three defensive tackles. Again, this is a run-stopping front with bodies allocated to stop shot plays, not a pass-rushing front ( the Packers have a lot of pass-rushing fronts installed, don’t worry ). Usually, Cooper is the designated “dropper” when the defense is spread out and is only rushing four. Hopefully, he’ll look better in space than Preston Smith did under Joe Barry in the same role. — In short, a Nickel defense is a 4-3 where…
