title: Steve Spagnuolo still figuring out Chiefs’ secondary through injuries
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs will take the field and play the Denver Broncos to begin the season in less than three weeks. There is still a lot to learn about the Chiefs’ new-look defensive backfield, and it’s more than the fans who are saying that. Defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo finally got a glimpse of the […]
full_text: ST. JOSEPH, MO - JULY 29: L'Jarius Sneed #38 walks to the field before practice during the Kansas City Chiefs training camp on July 29, 2026 at Missouri Western State University in St. Joseph, MO. (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs will take the field and play the Denver Broncos to begin the season in less than three weeks. There is still a lot to learn about the Chiefs’ new-look defensive backfield, and it’s more than the fans who are saying that. Defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo finally got a glimpse of the sixth-overall pick in this year’s draft, cornerback Mansoor Delane, during the Week 2 preseason game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . At the podium before Tuesday’s practice, Spagnuolo acknowledged that it was nice to see Delane in live action, and shared the one play that stuck out in his mind. Spags reflected on his first time seeing Mansoor Delane in live action today, pointing out "the one quick trigger on the rocket screen, which was nice" Worth pointing out Delane's playing 7 yards off the ball, not like he makes this play starting on the L.O.S. pic.twitter.com/UduCtUfxni — Ron Kopp Jr (@RonOnChiefs) August 25, 2026 “He had the one quick trigger on the rocket screen, which was nice,” Spagnuolo reflected. As he continued to talk through the state of the secondary in Kansas City, he acknowledged the in-and-out availability of veteran cornerback L’Jarius Sneed (Knee) factoring into the equation. “We still haven’t had LJ out there very much, so that’s a piece of the puzzle,” Spagnuolo noted. “Certainly Nohl [Williams] and Mansoor have done a good job out there, along with the other guys… We have another game to evaluate them, so we’ll see where we are; we’re kind of moving some pieces around.” Spags also pointed out the absence of his two starting safeties: Alohi Gilman (Low-back spasms) and Chamarri Conner. “Alohi didn’t play,” Spagnuolo reminded reporters. “So we’re working through that, and Chamarri is not out there right now, so we have a lot of moving pieces right now. Hopefully, as we get into next week, all that stuff will start to take fold.” Throughout the preseason, third-year defensive back Christian Roland-Wallace has manned the starting “slot” position in the team’s most common personnel package. “He’s playing a lot of spots right now,” Spagnuolo described Roland-Wallace. “In any defense, I think that’s valuable when you can be that versatile… he has become a real, reliable player for us.” However, it sounds like Sneed’s presence could reshape how the starting defense has looked to this point. “We have to get LJ back; we have to get everyone back to figure out where everyone is going to slot in,” Spagnuolo said. Sneed, who spent the last two seasons with the Tennessee Titans , has a familiar routine for injury management. During his initial stint in Kansas City, he had a unique practice schedule as he played through a knee issue; it sounds like that has continued since he returned this offseason. Spagnuolo told local media that he checks in with the team’s head trainer, Rick Burkholder, daily regarding Sneed. “We just don’t want any setbacks,” Spagnuolo shared. “The one thing about having LJ here is we know exactly what he is and what he can do, so I feel confident in that. He knows the system; he’s kind of right back into it and has embraced it. He’s a student of the game in the meeting rooms, which is good for the young guys to see.” “We’re just kind of chipping away at building a number of reps to get him ready, hopefully, to play in the regular season,” Spagnuolo said. “One of the things I’m always cautious about is I don’t want him to go backward, health-wise.” In training camp, Sneed was around or on the field quite a bit, even if he wasn’t cleared for full contact. He hasn’t dressed for either preseason game. Sneed has clearly earned the defensive coaching staff’s trust over the four seasons he spent as a young playmaker in the unit. “I think we’ve been smart with it, and I think it helps that we know him,” Spagnuolo said. “It would be different if he brought somebody in brand new, and he missed all this time. With LJ, I think we’re confident he can do it.” #Chiefs DC Steve Spagnuolo speaks on reuniting with L’Jarius Sneed: “It’s like having a son come back.” pic.twitter.com/8amg1VcXyV — Sports Radio 810 WHB (@SportsRadio810) July 30, 2026 The final piece to the Sneed puzzle is exactly where he could be lining up within the defensive formation this season. Early in his career, Sneed manned the slot and excelled. Eventually, he excelled on the perimeter. Spagnuolo still sees — and hears — that versatility from Sneed. “LJ and I have talked about it a lot; he’s comfortable in both,” Spagnuolo shared. “Here’s his response, always, when I ask him: ‘Wherever you need me.’ That’s what he says. So a little bit of it will be determined by who else is out there and what they can do.” “LJ was always a lot like Trent [McDuffie],” Spagnuolo pointed out. “LJ was always effective inside, but when we needed him to match up on somebody outside, that kind of dictated it, so that same thing might happen. We’ll see where the other guys are.” Just because we haven’t seen No. 38 out on the field with the Chiefs’ defense much this preseason doesn’t mean he’ll be on the sidelines once the live bullets start flying.
author: Ron Kopp Jr.

title: Dave Toub says ‘competition is real’ to be the Chiefs’ return man
summary: Less than a week remains before the Kansas City Chiefs must cut their offseason roster to 53 players ahead of the 2026 regular season. The fringes of the roster will always be impacted by the special teams, especially in Kansas City with coordinator Dave Toub. On Tuesday, he stepped up to the podium and spoke to local […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - AUGUST 22: Nikko Remigio #81 of the Kansas City Chiefs against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the first half of a preseason game at Raymond James Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Less than a week remains before the Kansas City Chiefs must cut their offseason roster to 53 players ahead of the 2026 regular season. The fringes of the roster will always be impacted by the special teams, especially in Kansas City with coordinator Dave Toub. On Tuesday, he stepped up to the podium and spoke to local media before practice ahead of Friday’s preseason finale against the Seattle Seahawks . He was asked about the battle at the return positions, acknowledging that the current starter, wide receiver Nikko Remigio, is staving off pressure from teammates for that role. “The competition is real. There’s nothing given,” Toub said. Running back Brashard Smith is the immediate backup to Remigio in the return game and is, seemingly, the closest to Remigio in the battle for a starting role. “Brashard continues to get better,” Toub pointed out. “He had an opportunity in the game… he probably could’ve just went and hit it and got to the wall; we’re not getting to the wall. The wall is there, and we’re not getting there. We have to be more aggressive to get to that point; we have to trust our speed back there instead of always looking for that up-the-field play.” “Nikko had no choice, he had the wall there but there was a guy,“ Toub continued. ”He had it wide open up the middle and he hit it up in there, it’s where we had the penalty. He had a 15-yard return, which was nice.“ Toub went on to mention that wide receivers Tyquan Thornton and Xavier Worthy can do it, too, but if it sounds like Toub feels more comfortable relying on Remigio to do the job right, he spelled it out for local media. “Nikko, right now, he’s the most solid guy,” Toub declared. “[The most] dependable that we’re working right now at the fifth or sixth receiver spot.” However, Toub ended his points on the return job by pointing out the one negative trait he sees with Remigio, one that others in this competition — like Brashard Smith — may have as an advantage. “The one thing we can’t change is his top-end speed,” Toub admitted. “I wish he had Worthy’s speed on the top end, but he does so many other things; his intangibles are just different from other guys.”

title: Chiefs Mailbag: Putting numbers to positions ahead of cutdown day
summary: Welcome back to the Arrowhead Pride Mailbag! Throughout the season, keep watching The Feed for an opportunity to submit your questions about the Kansas City Chiefs! The Chiefs have now played two preseason games. Those in consideration for the final roster spots have one more chance to shine on Friday against the Seattle Seahawks before […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - AUGUST 15: Tight end Jake Briningstool #88 of the Kansas City Chiefs runs after a second quarter pass catch in an NFL preseason game against the Los Angeles Rams at Arrowhead Stadium on August 15, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome back to the Arrowhead Pride Mailbag ! Throughout the season, keep watching The Feed for an opportunity to submit your questions about the Kansas City Chiefs ! The Chiefs have now played two preseason games. Those in consideration for the final roster spots have one more chance to shine on Friday against the Seattle Seahawks before the final roster is revealed on Sunday. Let’s see what’s on our readers’ minds. CasualFanatic asks: Do the Chiefs keep 4 TEs or 7 WRs, and if so, who makes those spots? I am guessing those outcomes are mutually exclusive. I predict the Chiefs will carry some combination of 10 wide receivers and tight ends. I feel very safe that six of those spots are already spoken for: tight end Travis Kelce and wide receivers Rashee Rice, Xavier Worthy, Tyquan Thornton, Cyrus Allen, and Jalen Royals. Tight end Noah Gray is probably a lock given the inexperience of the room behind Kelce. However, there are salary cap considerations, and the Chiefs could save almost $4 million against the limit by moving on. Assuming Gray stays, I think these five players are competing for three slots: wideouts Andrew Armstrong and Nikko Remigio, and tight ends Jared Wiley, Jake Briningstool and Trey Watson. Of that group, I think Briningstool stands above as the most difficult to pass through waivers. I do not think the Chiefs would have any trouble getting the other four to the practice squad. Briningstool has put up enough good film in preseason that I think a team would claim him. I haven’t seen evidence that the Chiefs trust anyone else on punt returns enough to cut Remigio. I suspect the final decision on the roster will be whether to keep Armstrong or a fourth tight end. If the front office keeps Armstrong as a seventh wide receiver, he would theoretically offer enough as a rotational red zone target to not need a fourth tight end. ChiefTigerfan24 asks: In what order do we place our “waiver wire” wants after roster cut-downs? I’m guessing offensive line options will top the list. A blocking tight end would also be nice, and that might help shore up a weak right side of the line. The Chiefs will have their highest waivers priority to start the season since 2013, and I expect them to take advantage. We might need to wait out a couple of days of league transactions reports to really know what Kansas City’s “final roster” will look like. Three positions stand out to me for the Chiefs to be scouting from other teams. The interior of the offensive line is a major need. Right now, the Chiefs look like they would need to get extremely creative to account for more than one offensive line injury. I expect Hunter Nourzad and Mike Caliendo to make the initial roster, but I wouldn’t be surprised if one of them is waived the next day after the Chiefs claim another player. At least one will probably stick for the season because the Chiefs will want to keep a backup to Creed Humphrey, who worked at center in camp. Linebacker could also be a need. Starter Drue Tranquill has had a back injury managed much of camp. The direct backup to middle linebacker Nick Bolton, Jack Cochrane, has been sidelined with a knee injury. If Cochrane is a candidate to be put on injured reserve and designated to return, the team will probably want to add a linebacker unless one of the reserve options plays like Derrick Johnson in the third exhibition game. Tight end is a sneaky option as well. I think the Chiefs’ receiving options at the position are what they are right now. But I could definitely see the team adding a blocking option. ACE asks: Will offensive line injuries derail the season? It seems like we don’t have enough quality depth, especially on the interior. The offensive line’s preseason performance has definitely been concerning. I haven’t seen any evidence that left tackle Josh Simmons’ back injury is serious, but the second-year pro does still need to prove he can dependably stay on the field. Fortunately, right guard Trey Smith returned to practice on Monday after missing the second half of camp with a hip injury. Rookie Kahlil Benson underwhelmed at tackle on Saturday, but he looks to be an acceptable sub at guard if needed. There are usually veteran guards available as free agents during the season if the need arises. I think the Chiefs have the pieces in place to handle a single offensive line injury. If more than one starter goes down, however, the current room could be overwhelmed quickly. DynastyMode2024 asks: How bad is Jaylon Moore that he had his first-string right tackle reps taken by Benson? What’s going on here? I feel like camp reporting was a little covert on how both guys were actually doing. We go live with this thing in a couple of weeks. Can Moore play RT or not? As the current roster stands, I’m not sure Moore has any choice but to play right tackle. I expect him to get the nod over Benson unless the third preseason game drastically changes things. Moore has mostly played on the left side, and he’s generally been an acceptable, if unspectacular, option. We’re also not far from the accolades he received last season when he stepped in for Simmons on just hours’ notice and played a big part in shutting down the Detroit Lions ‘ pass rush. We also haven’t seen Smith lined up at right guard next to either right tackle option. If the other four starters are playing to their abilities, I believe the Chiefs can put some help on the right side to make their right tackle situation work. I will be interested in the third preseason game if second-year pro Esa Pole looks like he is getting some late consideration for the job. I will also be watching where Ethan Driskell is lined up. The Chiefs will probably have to make do with the situation they have. If an experienced right tackle surprisingly becomes available after roster cuts, I don’t think you can rule out a move before the season starts. Thank you for reading this week’s Arrowhead Pride Mailbag ! We will be next week reacting to the team’s roster cuts on Sunday. Keep watching The Feed for an opportunity to ask your questions.

title: Chiefs News: Chiefs lead ESPN’s list of teams most likely to improve
summary: The latest In 2025, it wasn’t fun to be on the wrong side of the extreme results in one-score games after the Kansas City Chiefs were undefeated in such contests during the 2024 season. Last year, the Chiefs faltered in nearly every tight game with incredibly poor situational play. From the positive extreme to the […]
full_text: Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes (15) heads to the huddle after a chat with coach Andy Reid in the first half against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday, Nov. 23, 2025, at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, Missouri. (Tammy Ljungblad/The Kansas City Star/Tribune News Service via Getty Images) The latest In 2025, it wasn’t fun to be on the wrong side of the extreme results in one-score games after the Kansas City Chiefs were undefeated in such contests during the 2024 season. Last year, the Chiefs faltered in nearly every tight game with incredibly poor situational play. From the positive extreme to the negative over the last two years, the Chiefs are set up to find their level, which should help them dramatically improve on last season’s 6-11 record. Predicting NFL teams most likely to improve in 2026 season | ESPN Kansas City Chiefs I don’t think there will be much pushback against the idea that the Chiefs will improve in 2026. How much they improve, though, might be the more meaningful discussion. And unless we see a dramatically different underlying level of play from this team, so much of that might come down to those one-score games and how things pan out in the final minutes of close contests. Winning half of such games would get the Chiefs back into the playoffs. And winning about 65% of the time — which is Mahomes’ new career rate in games decided by seven points or fewer — might push Kansas City back atop the AFC West. Andy Reid remains patient with Chiefs rookie offensive tackle Kahlil Benson | The Kansas City Star What also didn’t aid Benson is that the Chiefs had their quarterbacks use a silent count in Tampa to replicate a true road environment. “We went silent count too, which was new to him,” Reid said, “so you saw he was late off the ball a couple times.” Still, it seems Kansas City isn’t ready to give up on Benson’s path to a rookie starting role. “All of that he banks, and it’ll be important once we start the season for him,” Reid said. Chiefs just watched their best remaining wide receiver option disappear | Arrowhead Addict The options weren’t all that exciting if the Kansas City Chiefs were considering a preseason upgrade to the wide receiver corps. But on Monday, with only six days to go before active roster cuts were due, the Houston Texans removed the best remaining player from the trade block. The Texans and New England Patriots agreed to a trade that sends wide receiver Kayshon Boutte to Houston in exchange for a player and a pick. Andy Reid says Mahomes ‘doing great’ as playing status for Week 1 remains undecided | KCTV5 The Chiefs will host the Denver Broncos on Monday Night Football on Sept. 14 – a game Mahomes has been very open about wanting to play in. “I’m going to be ready to go for that first game of the year, God willing,” Mahomes said on the broadcast of Saturday’s second preseason game. But whether or not he’ll be medically cleared to play – exactly nine months after tearing his ACL and LCL – is the deciding factor. 5 position groups Kansas City Chiefs GM Brett Veach must try to upgrade via trade or waiver wire during 53-man roster cuts | A to Z Sports Offensive Line Things weren’t much better when players like Esa Pole, Ethan Driskell, and Chu Godrick got into the game. Generally speaking, this feels like a situation not too dissimilar from a season ago. The Chiefs’ starting offensive line was very capable, but a couple of injuries quickly changed that. They don’t have the depth to sustain those injuries, and that’s not just an issue at tackle. It’s also an issue on the offensive interior. Around the NFL Browns name Deshaun Watson starting QB for Week 1 of 2026 season | NFL.com For a variety of reasons, it is likely to be an unpopular decision, easily the most important so far for Todd Monken in his first year as head coach. “[I] took in the whole body of work over the course of offseason to training camp to games, the joint practice,” Monken said Monday, “and ultimately felt like, to start the season on the road, Deshaun gave us the best chance to move the ball and score points. That’s really what it’s about. “I felt that way going into the last game but wasn’t sure. title: Chargers QB Justin Herbert to start preseason finale vs. Rams
summary: Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert will get a chance to shed some rust off before taking the field for Week 1 against the Arizona Cardinals. Charter side coach John Harbaugh said that Harbaugh will play “about six to nine plays” in the team’s preseason finale against the Los Angeles Rams on Thursday. “Just want […]
full_text: Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert (10) warms up before an NFL football game at EverBank Stadium, Sunday, Nov. 16, 2025 in Jacksonville, Fla. [Corey Perrine/Florida Times-Union] | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert will get a chance to shed some rust off before taking the field for Week 1 against the Arizona Cardinals. Charter side coach John Harbaugh said that Harbaugh will play “about six to nine plays” in the team’s preseason finale against the Los Angeles Rams on Thursday. “Just want it to be crisp and clean,” Harbaugh said via the team’s website . “We got several things that we were working on offensively and we want to see those show up. We want to see improvement. Everybody doing what they’re supposed to do.” He later added: “It’s never perfect, but you want to see that level of crispness and execution, that’s what you want to see the most.” Herbert struggled in his limited action during the team’s 41-17 loss against the San Francisco 49ers last week. He completed just one of his two attempts for nine yards as the offense went three and out on their opening drive. It’s clear after the team’s bad loss against the Niners that they want to go into the regular season with a little bit more momentum. Playing briefly during the game against the Rams should help them get closer to that goal. The Chargers don’t want to overwork their starters because there is a chance of injury, but they also want to make sure they are in the best position possible to succeed right out of the gate. Kickoff between the Rams and Chargers is scheduled for Thursday at 7 p.m. PT inside SoFi Stadium.

Rams as the backup quarterback , the head coach left the door open for rookie Ty Simpson to take the job away by Week 1’s game against the San Francisco 49ers. McVay left it in no uncertain terms on Tuesday: One of those two quarterbacks “will be the backup in Australia”. title: How Rams could revise Aaron Donald’s current contract
summary: With Aaron Donald’s potential return to the Los Angeles Rams still pending, NFL insiders are beginning to wonder whether he could want more than the current one-year, $30 million contract he has left on the deal he had when he retired. While $30 million would represent an enormous salary for a player returning from retirement, […]
full_text: BEVERLY HILLS, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 15: Aaron Donald attends Harold and Carole Pump Foundation 25th Anniversary Celebrity Dinner at The Beverly Hilton on August 15, 2025 in Beverly Hills, California. (Photo by Michael Tullberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images With Aaron Donald’s potential return to the Los Angeles Rams still pending , NFL insiders are beginning to wonder whether he could want more than the current one-year, $30 million contract he has left on the deal he had when he retired. While $30 million would represent an enormous salary for a player returning from retirement, Donald’s stature within the organization and his potential impact on a championship-caliber defense could make another contract adjustment worth exploring. What is Aaron Donald worth if he unretires and plays in 2026? What could the Rams do to revise his contract to bring him back in 2026? 💻 @AlbertBreer Is the reason Aaron Donald hasn't made his comeback official with #RamsHouse really about money? #NFL pic.twitter.com/h8vJx2MJTi — Rich Eisen Show (@RichEisenShow) August 24, 2026 The idea to change Donald’s contract would not be unprecedented for the Rams. In 2022, Los Angeles essentially ripped up the remaining structure of Donald’s existing contract and reworked it, adding $40 million over the final three years and giving him a new three-year commitment worth $95 million. That move made Donald the first non-quarterback to average more than $30 million per season. If Donald wants additional compensation in 2026 or beyond, the Rams could once again get creative in their negotiations without making other moves with their roster . Option 1: Add Performance Incentives The cleanest solution could be revising Donald’s current contract to include significant incentives. Rather than simply guaranteeing Donald another large amount of money, the Rams could give him opportunities to earn additional compensation based on his production. Sack totals could be one component, with escalating bonuses for reaching certain benchmarks. Snap counts could also be included, rewarding Donald for proving that he can handle a substantial workload after stepping away from football. Team success could be another major component. The Rams could give Donald bonuses for reaching the playoffs, winning the NFC West, advancing to the Super Bowl or winning Super Bowl LXI. That type of structure would give Donald considerable control over his earning potential while protecting the Rams from paying the maximum amount until he actually performs. It also creates a compelling dynamic: Donald would literally have the opportunity to earn his money on the field. If he returns and looks like the dominant defensive tackle Rams fans remember, the additional compensation would be justified. If his workload or production is limited, Los Angeles would not be locked into paying the maximum incentive package. Option 2: Add Void Years The second option could be more complicated but potentially more useful for the Rams’ salary-cap situation: adding void years to Donald’s contract. Void years allow a team to spread certain bonus money across additional contract years for salary-cap purposes. The tradeoff is that the financial obligation does not necessarily disappear. Instead, some of the cap charges can be pushed into future seasons, potentially creating dead-money charges after the player’s active contract expires. Keep in mind that Los Angeles reworked Myles Garrett’s contract following the blockbuster trade, the team increased his 2026 compensation while lowering his 2027 cap hit. Los Angeles could give Donald void years to push part of the cap burden into 2027. That would allow the Rams to maximize their current roster while effectively saying, “We’ll deal with the future cap consequences later.” And with the Rams already manipulating Garrett’s financial structure, adding a larger Donald cap charge in 2027 could be a logical extension of the team’s broader salary-cap strategy. Ultimately, the question may not be whether the Rams can afford to give Donald more money. It may be whether they can structure the contract creatively enough to make both sides happy. If Donald truly wants more than $30 million, another contract revision could be the solution.

title: Sean McVay won’t name a Matthew Stafford backup yet
summary: The Los Angeles Rams made a bold move by drafting Ty Simpson in the first round this year, but that does not mean Les Snead’s gutsy decision will help give Sean McVay an adequate 2026 backup for Matthew Stafford. Neither Simpson nor Stetson Bennett have been consistent enough (or had enough opportunity) in the preseason […]
full_text: BIRMINGHAM, ALABAMA - MAY 30: Steven Gilmore #22 of the Birmingham Stallions prior to a game against the Houston Gamblers at Protective Stadium on May 30, 2026 in Birmingham, Alabama. (Photo by Stew Milne/UFL/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams made a bold move by drafting Ty Simpson in the first round this year, but that does not mean Les Snead’s gutsy decision will help give Sean McVay an adequate 2026 backup for Matthew Stafford. Neither Simpson nor Stetson Bennett have been consistent enough (or had enough opportunity) in the preseason to make it obvious to anyone who should be L.A.’s second quarterback on the depth chart, and that includes McVay. As of Monday, McVay told reporters that he still does not know who the Rams backup quarterback will be in Week 1 against the 49ers. McVay added that while Simpson is guaranteed to play against the Chargers in the preseason finale on Thursday, he hasn’t decided if Bennett will get any more reps. What does it mean? We’ll know by Sunday, which is when teams must turn in their final cuts and 53-man rosters. Here’s the rest of the Rams news from Monday: Rams Make Multiple Roster Moves, Sign Brother of Former All-Pro Cornerback (sports.yahoo) “Following their second preseason game , the Los Angeles Rams made two additional signings on Monday. The Rams signed edge rusher Devean Deal and cornerback Steven Gilmore to the roster. They placed cornerback Zech McPhearson and edge rusher Keir Thomas on injured reserve in corresponding moves. Deal was an undrafted free agent out of TCU who was signed by the Seattle Seahawks after the draft. However, he was cut on May 14 to make room on the roster for wide receivers Rashad Rochelle and Trayvon Rudolph.“ Leveling up 📈 Steven Gilmore has signed with the Los Angeles Rams! #UFLtoNFL pic.twitter.com/UTgOJyHtqY — United Football League (@TheUFL) August 24, 2026 Rams Still Unsettled on QB2 After Stetson Bennett’s Strong Week 2 (athlonsports.com) “Head coach Sean McVay has not decided whether Stetson Bennett or Ty Simpson will serve as Matthew Stafford’s backup this season , with the Rams’ final preseason game Thursday against the Los Angeles Chargers . McVay confirmed Simpson will play, while Bennett’s status remains to be determined. Simpson was the story in Week 1, completing 84 percent of his passes for nearly 200 yards and two touchdowns. Bennett, meanwhile, played just two series before his day was done, giving Simpson the edge in the competition. But Week 2 belonged to Bennett. He received the bulk of the playing time in the Rams’ second game of the preseason and made the most of it in a 34-0 victory over the Saints.“ Sean McVay talks roster moves, allocating reps to Stetson Bennett IV & Ty Simpson, the importance of trust & more (therams.com) “Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay spoke with the media following Monday’s practice in Woodland Hills. Watch him discuss preseason roster moves, allocating reps to quarterbacks Stetson Bennett IV and Ty Simpson, the importance of trust, and more.” Brenda Song Loves the Los Angeles Rams So Much She Ended Up in a Broadcast Booth at SoFi Stadium (hollywoodreporter.com) “ Brenda Song, we are sitting in a golf cart in the bowels of SoFi Stadium moments after you made your broadcast debut. How did that feel? I’m on a high. I’m not joking when I say it was my dream. I grew up loving sports but I’m 5’2” — my feet barely touch the ground when I’m sitting in a chair — so I just love watching from the sidelines as a couch analyst. I’m just so grateful to the Ramily for letting me go up there and live out my dream and call the game. Sitting next to Rob Havenstein, an incredible right tackle, was insane.“ Breaking down the Rams’ 6 roster moves made on Monday (ramswire) “Waive/injured LB Daniel Rickert Rickert injured his knee against the Saints and was unable to return to the game. Unlike Thomas and McPhearson, he wasn’t placed on IR, but rather waived with an injury designation. If he clears waivers, he will revert to the Rams’ injured reserve. OL Justin Dedich passes physical Sean McVay said last week that Dedich was expected to return to practice soon, and on Monday, he was back on the field after being activated off the NFI list. Dedich had been on the NFI list since injuring his hand at home in July, causing him to miss all of camp and the preseason up to this point. Now that he’s healthy, he can resume practicing.“ Rams chose wisely in passing on Zach Wilson reclamation project (ramblinfan) “But at one point, many fans lobbied hard for general manager Les Snead to save Wilson’s career, back when he played for the New York Jets. LA’s need for a quarterback succession plan led fans to consider almost every young hurler. And you needn’t turn back the calendar too far to revisit the Wilson-Rams rumors. At the time, restoring luster to tarnished quarterback reputations was an LA specialty. But that restoration was only possible because Snead has a fine eye for talent. title: Raiders’ offense: Glimpses of Klint Kubiak’s fullback usage bodes well
summary: An actual lead-blocking fullback charging ahead of the running back. That was absent the last two season for the Las Vegas Raiders and the glaring omission of a “true” fullback on the roster ended a 40-year run of consistently deploying one. Klint Kubiak course corrected with the quickness. An old-school truther of the vitality of […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - AUGUST 13: Head coach Klint Kubiak of the Las Vegas Raiders leaves the field after the team's 27-14 loss to the Arizona Cardinals in a preseason game at Allegiant Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images An actual lead-blocking fullback charging ahead of the running back. That was absent the last two season for the Las Vegas Raiders and the glaring omission of a “true” fullback on the roster ended a 40-year run of consistently deploying one. Klint Kubiak course corrected with the quickness. An old-school truther of the vitality of a dying breed, the Raiders head coach wasn’t playing any games on his desire to have a fullback on his roster. As free agency began this past March, the Silver & Black pounced on a player Kubiak deemed fit for the position by signing Connor Heyward, a versatile tight end by trade the Pittsburg Steelers wanted to keep. (This also explains the quote I used above for true fullback.) “Running the ball is important, we think that’s a huge part of winning football games,” Kubiak said when asked about the importance of the fullback in his offense. “Running the ball, stopping the run on defense. Just in our scheme, it’s a very versatile player. Guy that plays tight end, plays fullback, that can pass pro, that has to be a four-core special teams player, he’s got to be one of the smartest players on your team. So, we’re going to keep getting Connor and get him better. And (Patrick) Gurd’s coming along.” Lofty expectations from the Raiders head honcho, but if there’s someone who can do what Kubiak wants, it’s Heyward who was listed as a tight end but who blocked, ran the ball, ran patterns and caught the rock, and was special teams mainstay during his four years in the Steel City. It’s easy to see why Kubiak wanted Heyward as the Michigan State product not only has the build to withstand the rigors of versatility — 6-feet and 230 pounds — but he has the mentality and willingness to do what needs to be done. “Just being selfless and being one of 11. You might get the ball here and there, but that’s not what it’s about,” Heyward began when explaining the mentality it takes to play fullback in the NFL. “It’s about opening up lanes and getting the run game going and having the run game area with the pass game and just honestly doing the dirty work on special teams as well. So, it’s a full day’s work and it’s never going to stop.” Fullback news: Connor Heyward has agreed to terms with the #Raiders on a 2-year, $5.5M max value deal with $2M fully guaranteed, per agent @PerrettM of @PrioritySports . The #Steelers wanted Heyward back, but Klint Kubiak wants him as his FB for what he’s building in Vegas. pic.twitter.com/nDdrPjMcMj — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) March 12, 2026 In the Raiders first preseason game against the Arizona Cardinals, we got a window into how Kubiak is slated to use the fullback in his offense. Heyward was often plugged in the backfield with either starting running back Ashton Jeanty and/or rookie Mike Washington Jr. providing a pathfinder for the tailbacks. The 27-year-old also initially lined up as a tight end before formation shift/motion saw No. 34 move back to a traditional lead blocking fullback role and plunge towards the defense at the snap looking to block linebackers and defensive backs who entered the fray. In Las Vegas’ second preseason game — against the Houston Texans on Thursday night — Heyward was in his usual spot as the fullback providing a lead-blocking presence in the backfield and even lined up at tight end for a catch. What a sight to see in Kubiak’s offense. “Yeah, you can throw the ball, run the ball, stretch the defense horizontally and vertically. But that’s Coach (Kubiak’s) and his scheme. It’s just not myself,” Heyward said regarding how unpredictable an offense can be with a versatile fullback on the roster. “It’s just a scheme and buying in honestly. You guys saw that on the first drive and you guys saw that glimpsed throughout the game. But we just got to ultimately put it together, and it’s not the finished product right now, and we don’t want it to be. We just want to continue to get better, and this camp is about growth, and the season is about growth.” The All-11 approach showed up in a big way on Washington’s breakaway 53-yard run against the Cardinals in the preseason opener. Second-string left tackle Charles Grant started the play off absolutely pancaking a defender to open the gap and Heyward charged forward into it, helped seal a defender that allowed the rookie tailback to use his speed and agility to make a break for it. Raiders FB Connor Heyward breaks down the blocking and vision on rookie RB Mike Washington Jr.’s 53-yard run vs. the Cardinals: “I know Chuck [Charles Grant] had a really good block, and I just played off Chuck’s block. Mike Washington Jr. did what he did, and he had 50+ yards… pic.twitter.com/A5Woq3xuPc — Vegas Sports Today (@VegasSportsTD) August 16, 2026 While we’re far from seeing the full gamut of Kubiak’s offensive playbook, the glimpses we’ve seen provide encouraging signs of what’s to come. The football watching world knows the Raiders head coach and play caller loves the wide zone running scheme and the Silver & Black are most assuredly going to run that aplenty. But during his time dialing up plays for the Super Bowl-winning Seattle Seahawks last season, Kubiak mixed in more power into the zone schematics he’s long preferred. That helped put players on the Seahawks roster in the best possible position to succeed and with Kubiak bringing over assistant coaches from Seattle with him to the Las Vegas — such as offensive coordinator Andrew Janocko and offensive line coach Rick Dennison — he’s brought plenty of experience and sounding boards with him to the desert. We’ve seen instances where the Kubiak has called for zone and power, creating a mix of finesse and smashmouth football in both practices and preseason tilts. And that’s going that mix is going to be important when the Raiders get to games that count on the win-loss record. “Yeah, we’ve obviously got to stay balanced. There’s a lot of great defenses out there, so you can’t just go out there and just run counter and power run the whole game,” Heyward said. “But we’re a wide zone team, and when you put stress on the corners and make them tackle like that. We have very capable backs, and it’s really just about putting our backs on the corners and safeties and even linebackers, whether that’s just running routes out the backfield because they’re just so versatile. So, we can mix and match so many guys on our offense, so it’ll be interesting to see.” Mike Washington Jr. has a rare combination of size and speed 👀 pic.twitter.com/cFccsypbN7 — NFL Draft Files (@NFL_DF) August 21, 2026 Lauded for creativity concocting an offense, the always pragmatic Kubiak provided one of his patented responses when asked for the origins of his ingenuity. “I think I’d rather be known for being fundamentally sound,” Kubiak said. “That’s things that we stress offensively, and as you put more and more film on tape, you get more and more predictable. So, you’ve got to keep finding ways to evolve. But as a coach, I’d rather be much more about the basics and being great at the fundamentals so that’s what we’re going to harp on.” The basic of being able to effectively run the football has been elusive for the Raiders. But perhaps with Kubiak as play caller, Dennison coaching up the offensive line, and Heyward as the fullback, the Silver & Black Express can once again, get rolling.

title: Klint Kubiak on Ashton Jeanty: ‘He’s on the mend’
summary: For those hoping to get concrete information on the injury status of Las Vegas Raiders’ starting tailback Ashton Jeanty, you’re out of luck. In his first interview since Jeanty went down at practice Sunday afternoon, Raiders coach Klint Kubiak declined get into details of Jeanty’s status. He said he would not discuss injuries and only […]
full_text: HENDERSON, NEVADA - MAY 20: Head coach Klint Kubiak of the Las Vegas Raiders looks on as Ashton Jeanty #2 practices during an OTA offseason workout at the Las Vegas Raiders Headquarters/Intermountain Health Performance Center on May 20, 2026 in Henderson, Nevada. (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images For those hoping to get concrete information on the injury status of Las Vegas Raiders’ starting tailback Ashton Jeanty, you’re out of luck. In his first interview since Jeanty went down at practice Sunday afternoon, Raiders coach Klint Kubiak declined get into details of Jeanty’s status. He said he would not discuss injuries and only stated that Jeanty “is on the mend.” Earlier Tuesday, NFL Media reported that the Raiders believe Jeanty’s ankle injury is “more low than high” and they are unsure if he will be ready for Week 1 at home against the Miami Dolphins in 19 days. The report stated that the Raiders don’t believe the injury will be long term. There was initial concern that the injury was more serious. Jeanty had to be helped off the field and he couldn’t put weight on his right leg. The entire team took a knee and prayed in silence. Rookie Mike Washington has been working with the first-team offense with Jeanty out. Kubiak said he thinks the rookie understands the team is counting on him. Second-year wide receiver Dont’e Thornton continued to be out. Rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza did get some reps with the first-team offense, but Kirk Cousins took most of the first-team reps. Kubiak still declined to name his starter, even though all signs point to Cousins playing Week 1. Kubiak indicated guards Jackson Powers-Johnson and Caleb Rogers will both play Thursday night in the preseason finale as their battle for a starting job continues. In another strong indication that veteran Matt Gay will win the kicking job, Las Vegas special teams coach Joe DeCamillis said undrafted rookie Kansei Matsuzawa has a chance to be on an NFL roster “later down the road.” DeCamillis said Matsuzawa’s practices have been better than his preseason game performances. If he is cut, as expected, Matsuzawa could be a candidate for the practice squad.

title: Where Las Vegas Raiders’ 2026 NFL draft class stands in final week of training camp
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders are in the final week of training camp for what’s expected to be a rebuilding year/season. With that in mind, let’s take a look at where the Raiders’ 2026 NFL draft class stands on the depth chart since the Week 1 matchup against the Miami Dolphins is right around the corner. […]
full_text: Las Vegas Raiders safeties Treydan Stukes (31) and Dalton Johnson (30) interact during an NFL rookie camp at the team's headquarters on Saturday, May 2, 2026 in Henderson, Nev. (Heidi Fang/Las Vegas Review-Journal/Tribune News Service via Getty Images) The Las Vegas Raiders are in the final week of training camp for what’s expected to be a rebuilding year/season. With that in mind, let’s take a look at where the Raiders’ 2026 NFL draft class stands on the depth chart since the Week 1 matchup against the Miami Dolphins is right around the corner. QB Fernando Mendoza Klint Kubiak has made it pretty clear that he wants Kirk Cousins to begin the campaign as the starting quarterback in Las Vegas, and that hasn’t changed in training camp. Reportedly, Mendoza has had reps with the first-string offense but has primarily been working with the second team over the summer. As expected with a rookie quarterback at this stage, camp reports note a mix of good and bad practices, and that he’s even fluctuated throughout the day on occasion. In other words, there’s been no indication that the Raiders are going to deviate from their original plan of easing Mendoza into the NFL. DB Treydan Stukes The playmaking ability Stukes displayed in his final season at Arizona hasn’t shown up in Las Vegas yet. He’s been solid but nothing spectacular in camp, and that was the case in the first preseason game. Granted, the coaching staff has admitted that they’ve thrown a lot at the second-round pick, and he’s getting comfortable at a new position after primarily being a nickelback in college. Also, he had a solid outing in Houston. Stukes has reportedly been getting more reps in practice with the first-team defense lately, but it still seems like he’s firmly behind Isaiah Pola-Mao for the starting free safety job. EDGE Keyron Crawford An injury held Crawford back a bit, sidelining him for a few practices at the beginning of training camp. But he’s healthy now, and from the sounds of it, he’s made a few splash plays here and there. However, edge is the deepest position group on the Raiders’ roster, and undrafted rookie Cian Slone has caught the coaching staff’s eye . Baring a roster shake-up before cutdown day, Crawford will likely spend this season behind Maxx Crosby, Kwity Paye and Malcolm Koonce. And the Auburn product will have to fend off Slone from creeping up on the depth chart. OL Trey Zuhn III At the beginning of training camp, it felt like every report I read had Zuhn playing a different position from one day to the next. It seems like he’s settled in at right tackle more recently, though, where he could push DJ Glaze for a starting spot. However, Glaze has been the starter all summer, and it appears as if the Texas A&M product will begin the regular season as a versatile backup who could fill in if anyone is struggling or injured. On that note, Jackson Powers-Johnson’s recent injury could open up another opportunity for Zuhn to see the field in year one if Caleb Rogers isn’t getting the job done. CB Jermod McCoy The hopes of McCoy pushing Darien Porter for a starting spot right away never came to fruition. The Raiders had the fourth-round pick on a pitch count during the spring practices and the beginning of camp, making it difficult to climb up the depth chart quickly. Plus, the emergence of fellow rookie corner Hezekiah Masses hasn’t helped McCoy’s cause. However, beat writers have noted that he’s been getting some run with the starters more recently. From the sounds of it, it wouldn’t be surprising if the Tennessee product doesn’t get much playing time early in the year, and instead will be a prime candidate to get more opportunities in the second half of the season. RB Mike Washington Jr. Outside of maybe Mendoza, no rookie has fulfilled the “meets expectations” criterion for me more than Washington so far. The Arkansas product does appear to have a strong role in Kubiak’s offense, which could grow depending on if or how long Ashton Jeanty has time at the beginning of the season. Plus, Washington’s first two preseason games highlighted the home-run hitting style of back that he is, with five carries and 53 and 33 yards. S Dalton Johnson There hasn’t been much chatter about Johnson in camp, as he doesn’t appear to be standing out in either direction. That’s fine for a fifth-round pick, as he’ll probably contribute the most on special teams and serve as a versatile backup in the secondary this season. But both Jeremy Chinn and Pola-Mao are entering contract years, allowing the Arizona product to learn this year and potentially compete for a bigger role in 2027. CB Hezekiah Masses As referenced above, Masses started hot with strong performances in OTAs, minicamp and the beginning of training camp to be a surprise contender for a starting job. However, he seems to have cooled off more recently, highlighted by a tough outing in the Raiders’ first preseason game. The coaching staff has been experimenting with ways to get Eric Stokes, Porter and Masses on the field at the same time, reportedly giving the rookie a shot at nickel corner . He may not fit that role, but it sounds like the Cal product will at least be the first cornerback off the bench in year one, especially if Porter isn’t getting the job done. WR Malik Benson Benson has been turning heads in camp, wisely establishing a connection/chemsitry with Mendoza and pushing Jack Bech for the third wide receiver role. But the sixth-rounder has reportedly been working with the second-team offense primarily, only receiving a significant amount of snaps with the starters when Jalen Nailor was sidelined. So, it seems like Bech has the upper hand for the job, but Benson will likely begin the campaign as WR4 and a special-teamer. That’s good value in year one for a late Day 3 pick. DT Brandon Cleveland It wouldn’t surprise me if Cleveland gets cut and spends 2027 on the practice squad. There’s been little to no buzz about him in camp while the defense needs a defensive tackle to step up against the run. The NC State product has that type of skill set, but he hasn’t proven to be a diamond in the rough yet. At this rate, even if the seventh-round pick makes the team, one has to imagine he’ll be a healthy scratch on gamedays to begin the campaign.

title: Raiders roster: About the wide receivers
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders group of wide receivers are under the microscope this week in the final days before the team is required to set its initial 53-man roster on Sunday afternoon. Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak recently fueled speculation about the unit last week when he said the group took a step backward in […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - JANUARY 04: Jack Bech #18 of the Las Vegas Raiders warms up prior to a game against the Kansas City Chiefs at Allegiant Stadium on January 04, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Ian Maule/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders group of wide receivers are under the microscope this week in the final days before the team is required to set its initial 53-man roster on Sunday afternoon. Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak recently fueled speculation about the unit last week when he said the group took a step backward in Week 2 of the preseason and it needs players to step up for the regular season. Let’s look at where the unit stands: Safe: Tre Tucker, Jalen Nailor, Jack Bech. You can question whether this tope three is good enough to help win games in the regular season. But these players should be part of the mic for sure. Likely safe: Malik Benson. The sixth-round pick had two drops at Houston. But he’s had an otherwise strong summer and it would be somewhat stunning if he doesn’t make the roster. He’d need a really bad final preseason game Thursday. On the bubble: Dont’e Thronton, Shedrick Jackson, Brandon Johnson, EJ. Williams, Chase Roberts. Dareke Young, Deven Thompkins, Phillip Dorsett. The Raiders will likely keep five or six wide receivers and special teams play will be a factor in the final decisions. Thornton, a fourth-round pick last year who had a big role to start the season, is in real danger of being cut. He has been hurt for some time and was not impressive before then. Outside help: The Raiders could try to trade for a receiver with the free-agent market very thin at this point. Watch the waiver wire Monday. Las Vegas has the No. 1 waiver priority to start the season and they could be very active next week.

summary: The Miami Dolphins placed veteran offensive lineman Jamaree Salyer on injured reserve last week, seemingly ending his season, with a knee issue. On Tuesday, ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler indicated Salyer’s season may not be over as the Dolphins have agreed to an injury settlement with the former sixth-round pick of the Los Angeles Chargers, releasing him […]
full_text: Jul 31, 2026; Miami Gardens, FL, USA; Miami Dolphins offensive line coach Zach Yenser speaks to guard Jamaree Salyer (69) during practice at Baptist Health Training Complex. Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Miami Dolphins placed veteran offensive lineman Jamaree Salyer on injured reserve last week, seemingly ending his season, with a knee issue. On Tuesday, ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler indicated Salyer’s season may not be over as the Dolphins have agreed to an injury settlement with the former sixth-round pick of the Los Angeles Chargers, releasing him from the roster. Salyer will be able to sign with a team, including the Dolphins, during the 2026 season once his recovery is complete. The Dolphins signed Salyer to a one-year contract in March, expecting him to compete with second-year lineman Jonah Savaiinaea for the starting right guard position. Savaiinaea has played well on the right side, improving his play from last season when he was on the left, and seemed to close the door on Salyer’s chances of starting. The veteran seemed to be settling into being a primary reserve option for the Dolphins, able to play both tackle and guard if needed, but then landed on IR. Now, he will focus on recovery before looking to join a team in season. Salyer appeared in 64 games, including 40 starts, in his four season with the Chargers.

title: Jeff Hafley ‘concerned’ that Kenneth Grant may miss Dolphins opener
summary: Miami Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley met with the South Florida media ahead of Tuesday’s practice and discussed various topics, including injuries to multiple players on the team’s roster. One player who is on the wrong side of the health spectrum is second-year defensive tackle Kenneth Grant. According to Hafley, Grant’s availability is in doubt […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDNES, FL - JUNE 09: Miami Dolphins offensive defensive lineman Kenneth Grant (78) speaks with reporters during the Miami Dolphins OTA on Tuesday, June 9, 2026 at Baptist Health Training Complexr in Miami Gardens, FL (Photo by Peter Joneleit/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Miami Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley met with the South Florida media ahead of Tuesday’s practice and discussed various topics, including injuries to multiple players on the team’s roster. One player who is on the wrong side of the health spectrum is second-year defensive tackle Kenneth Grant. According to Hafley, Grant’s availability is in doubt for the team’s regular season opener on the road against the Las Vegas Raiders on September 13th. “He’s week-to-week, so, I think, of course there’s going to be concern [about his Week One availability]. If I felt like he was going to, for sure, be back next week, I would tell you that. Am I hopeful he will be? Yeah. But, there’s always going to be concern until I see a guy out there… Until he has his helmet and shoulder pads and he’s practicing with us, I’m going to have concern, for sure.” Hafley’s words present a “mixed-signals” type of scenario for Kenneth Grant’s availability moving forward. Could Miami’s coach be using the media to send a message to Grant about the way he’s gone about his rehab process? Possibly. However, the longer Grant’s injury forces him to miss time, the more opportunities guys like Jordan Phillips, Zeek Biggers and others will have to pass the former first rounder on the team’s depth chart. We will continue to keep you updated on all things Miami Dolphins as the team prepares for its final preseason contest against the Atlanta Falcons this Friday.

title: Dolphins plan for rookie receiver Chris Bell to play in preseason finale
summary: The Miami Dolphins selected wide receiver Chris Bell out of Louisville in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft despite the pass catcher’s ACL tear in November of last year. The hope was that he would eventually be healthy enough to contribute to Miami’s offense at some point during the regular season — but […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - AUGUST 20: Chris Bell #18 of the Miami Dolphins looks on during joint practice with the New York Giants at Baptist Health Training Complex on August 20, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Rich Storry/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins selected wide receiver Chris Bell out of Louisville in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft despite the pass catcher’s ACL tear in November of last year. The hope was that he would eventually be healthy enough to contribute to Miami’s offense at some point during the regular season — but after head coach Jeff Hafley’s pre-practice media availability on Tuesday morning, it’s clear that Bell will be contributing much sooner than most expected. While speaking with the South Florida media on Tuesday, Hafley said that the team plans for Chris Bell to play in the Dolphins’ preseason finale against the Atlanta Falcons on Friday. “You guys saw yesterday, he was out of his red [non-contact] jersey. He did team [drills], so he was in contact drills because we’re thudding. So the plan would be — today we’re going to treat like a Thursday in the season. Tomorrow we’re going to treat like a Friday in the season, so we’ll have a pretty bigger load today in practice where he’ll get more reps and hopefully he’ll continue to progress forward. And if he continues to do so, then I’d like to see him play in the game.” Obviously, if all goes well on Friday, it sounds like Bell will be ready to take the field on September 13th when the Dolphins start their season on the road against the Las Vegas Raiders. Yesterday, it was reported that Bell stayed after practice with quarterback Malik Willis so the two could get extra work together in an effort to get the rookie receiver on the same page with Miami’s new gunslinger. Hopefully that continues so that Bell can be ready to be a playmaker for the Dolphins during the 2026 season and beyond.

This year is not expected to be anything special in South Florida, with many analysts considering Miami among the most likely teams to finish the year with the worst record and the first-overall pick in next year’s NFL Draft. The roster turnover and lack of salary cap space have made Miami the youngest team in the league, but it also means the team is lacking depth across the entire roster. The Dolphins are just five days from having to drop their roster from the 90-man preseason limit to the 53-man regular season authorization. According to the Miami Herald’s Omar Kelly, the problem for Miami may not be who to cut, but rather who to keep. Kelly writes Miami only has “roughly 45 legitimate NFL players.” It is a rough assessment of the team, but he explains: When $179 million of the team’s cap space is committed to paying off debt from players who aren’t on the roster, there are a limited amount of resources the front office gets to use to improve the talent base. That somewhat explains why Miami’s backups have looked disappointing in the two joint practices and preseason games. This roster needs reinforcements, which is why Sullivan needs to view next week’s cut-down day (Aug. 30), and the days of releases that will follow it, as a supplemental draft for Miami, claiming talent at all positions that can potentially improve this roster. title: Jeshaun Jones Suspended for First Three Games of Regular Season
summary: A member of the Minnesota Vikings who is currently fighting for a spot on the 53-man roster has just seen his chances of not being a part of the team’s final cuts increase dramatically. . .for the wrong reasons. The National Football League has informed Vikings’ wide receiver Jeshaun Jones that he will be suspended […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - AUGUST 22: Jeshaun Jones #82 of the Minnesota Vikings lines up for a play against the Baltimore Ravens during the second quarter of the preseason game at U.S. Bank Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images A member of the Minnesota Vikings who is currently fighting for a spot on the 53-man roster has just seen his chances of not being a part of the team’s final cuts increase dramatically. . .for the wrong reasons. The National Football League has informed Vikings’ wide receiver Jeshaun Jones that he will be suspended for the first three games of the 2026 regular season for violating the league’s substance abuse policy. He can continue participating in the team’s preseason program, including Friday’s game in Denver against the Broncos, before starting his suspension on 30 August. Jones was reportedly arrested outside of Tampa on 18 April for refusing to submit to a blood test to determine his blood-alcohol level. He pleaded guilty to a lesser charge of reckless driving last month, with a sentence that includes twelve months of probation. While Jones’ chances of making the active roster appear to be slim, he would not count against the 53-man roster during the time he is on the suspended list if the Vikings wanted to keep him around. Jones, who leads the Vikings in receiving yardage through the first two preseason games, has been on the team’s practice squad the past two seasons and would likely be a candidate to be there again this season. Jones will be eligible to return at the start of Week 4, so we will see if this incident plays any role in whether or not the team brings him back or decides to cut ties with him completely.

McCarthy #9 of the Minnesota Vikings warms up before the preseason game against the Baltimore Ravens at U.S. Bank Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings 53-man roster projection is here, and Tyler Forness has J.J. McCarthy OFF the roster. Vikings roster battles, quarterback controversy, and surprise cuts dominate this episode of The Real Forno Show . In the latest episode of The Real Forno Show , Tyler Forness and producer Dave Stefano broke down the Vikings’ final 53-man roster position by position, and the biggest bombshell came at quarterback. Tyler projects the Vikings keeping Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz — but not J.J. McCarthy. “I believe, from my purview, that the Vikings are done with him,” Tyler said. “McCarthy has shown that you really just cannot trust him to play a football game right now and that sucks.” The discussion covered McCarthy’s $5.96 million dead cap hit, the possibility of a trade, and even a potential Anthony Richardson swap. Tyler was blunt: “You can’t trust J.J. McCarthy to go in right now and play in an NFL game.” The show also explored the new NIL landscape and how the “five-for-five” eligibility rule could change quarterback development for future drafts. The roster breakdown featured several surprising calls. At running back, Demond Claiborne edges out Zavier Scott: “Clayborn, with his explosiveness, they love it.” At wide receiver, only five make the cut — Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison, Jauan Jennings, Tai Felton, and Myles Price. On the offensive line, Tyler didn’t mince words about the depth: “Vershon Lee is a turnstile.” Regarding third-round pick Caleb Tiernan, Tyler quoted Locked On Vikings’ Luke Braun: “His performance was like Willie Beavers level cuttable. It was awful.” At edge rusher, Tyler flagged a glaring need: “I think they’re still gonna find a way to add a veteran edge rusher… if it somehow was both [Dallas Turner and Andrew Van Ginkel injured], this room turns into a train wreck.” At cornerback, UDFA Da’Veawn Armstead is the surprise inclusion, while Dwight McGlothern is “cooked, cooked.” At safety, Theo Jackson is OUT, and undrafted Jacob Thomas is IN: “Jacob Thomas has just absolutely obliterated every expectation.” Tyler also addressed the Harrison Smith situation, saying he assumes Smith isn’t returning until a possible Week 4-5 announcement. Key Points from the Episode: Quarterback: J.J. McCarthy projected OFF the 53-man roster; Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz make the team. A trade is more likely than a cut. Running Back (4): Aaron Jones, Jordan Mason, Demond Claiborne, Max Bredeson. Zavier Scott cut due to poor pass protection in camp. Wide Receiver (5): Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison, Jauan Jennings, Tai Felton, Myles Price. Dontae Fleming, Dillon Bell, and Jeshaun Jones projected to the practice squad. Tight End (3): T.J. Hockenson, Josh Oliver, Gavin Bartholomew over Ben Yurosek. Offensive Line (9): Christian Darrisaw, Donovan Jackson, Blake Brandel, Will Fries, Brian O’Neill, Ryan Van Demark, Michael Jurgens, Joe Huber, Caleb Tiernan (IR candidate with ankle injury). Defensive Line (5): Jalen Redmond, Levi Drake Rodriguez, Caleb Banks, Domonique Orange, Elijah Williams. Edge Rusher (6): Dallas Turner, Andrew Van Ginkel, Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins, Bo Richter, Tyler Batty, and one TBD — a veteran addition expected. Linebacker (5): Blake Cashman, Eric Wilson, Jake Golday, Ivan Pace Jr., Jacob Roberts. Pace could be a trade candidate due to his $3.52M salary. Cornerback (5): Byron Murphy Jr., Isaiah Rodgers, James Pierre, Charles Demmings, Da’Veawn Armstead (UDFA surprise). Safety (5): Josh Metellus, Jay Ward, Tavierre Thomas, Jakobe Thomas, Jacob Thomas. Theo Jackson on the trade block. Harrison Smith’s return uncertain. Specialists (3): Will Reichard, Andrew DePaola, Johnny Hekker. Brett Thorson targeted for the practice squad. title: Is Kendre Miller finally putting it together?
summary: There weren’t many positives for the New Orleans Saints in their 34-0 preseason loss to the Los Angeles Rams, but Kendre Miller gave the team one worth watching. Miller received a heavy workload this past week throughout two joint practices and a preseason showing, recording six carries for 22 yards while forcing one missed tackle […]
full_text: There weren’t many positives for the New Orleans Saints in their 34-0 preseason loss to the Los Angeles Rams, but Kendre Miller gave the team one worth watching. Miller received a heavy workload this past week throughout two joint practices and a preseason showing, recording six carries for 22 yards while forcing one missed tackle and converting one first down on just 24 total snaps against the Rams on Saturday. Most importantly, the opportunity was significant, and Miller made it through the game healthy while also impressing. The 24-year-old has shown flashes of being an impactful player at the next level, but every time he appears to gain momentum, an injury seems to derail him. Staying on the field has been the biggest hurdle of his young career. Now, Miller may have another opportunity in front of him. Alvin Kamara is dealing with a knee injury suffered during joint practice with the Dallas Cowboys that will sideline him about a month, while Devin Neal suffered a hamstring injury against the Rams. That said, Miller could suddenly find himself with a much larger role heading into year four. That’s where the overreaction comes in: Can we actually expect Miller to stay healthy this time? Maybe that’s asking too much based on his history. But the Saints don’t need Miller to suddenly become their featured back. They added star RB Travis Etienne Jr. this offseason in free agency, but behind him is where Miller could be essential. New Orleans needs him to be available, productive and reliable when his number is called. This is also a critical season for Miller. He’s entering the final year of his rookie contract, giving him plenty to prove if he wants to remain in New Orleans beyond 2026. The talent has never really been the question. Availability has. Miller makes the Saints better when he’s on the field. If he can finally stay there, he could have a much bigger opportunity ahead of him than many expected entering the preseason.

full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know as Giants get set to face off with the their stadium roommates, the New York Jets. Arvell Reese ‘making a lot of progress real fast’ in establishing himself on Giants defense | New York Post Reese has already solidified himself as a critical piece of the Giants defense and continued to impress, adding another two total tackles during their preseason game Saturday. Reese sits second among defensive rookies for the best PFF grade through two preseason games (88.2), trailing just the Buccaneers’ Rueben Bain Jr. (88.8). “He hasn’t really missed a beat at all,” coach John Harbaugh said. “He learns very quickly, and he executes the defenses really well. And then when he doesn’t, he listens to every word of the coaching and applies it on the next opportunity. He’s making a lot of progress real fast.” Why the presence of Malik Nabers is a game changer for the Giants | The Record Malik Nabers is no longer seeing red. Which means the end game for the New York Giants and their star wide receiver is almost upon us. 2026 New York Giants training camp: Latest intel, updates | ESPN.com John Harbaugh huddled a group of veterans after practice. They went over schedules, practice details and other team-related stuff. This is how John Harbaugh operates. He assembles a leadership group and consults with them on decisions. For the Giants that consists of quarterback Jaxson Dart, left tackle Andrew Thomas, outside linebacker Brian Burns, middle linebacker Tremaine Edmunds, safety Jevon Holland, punter Jordan Stout, backup quarterback Jameis Winston and tight end Chris Manhertz. They were voted as leaders by their teammates. “We’ve been doing it for a long time. It’s good,” Harbaugh said of the leadership group. “I do kind of try to emphasize to the team that everybody’s a leader and everybody has every opportunity to speak their mind. Talk to anybody. … But sometimes it just kind of helps because guys don’t always want to do that.” Top Potential Trade Packages and Landing Spots for Steelers’ Joey Porter Jr. | Bleacher Report New York Giants receive: CB Joey Porter Jr. Pittsburgh Steelers receive: 2027 second- and sixth-round draft picks. Adding Joey Porter Jr. into the mix would massively improve the secondary and give Big Blue the elite defensive back it needs to contend with the talented NFC East wideouts it is set to come up against in 2026. Rather than hope Adebo and Newsome return to form and Hood comes out of the gate strong, the Giants could instead trade for Porter and instantly solidify the cornerback position. Armed with a pair of Day 2 picks in the 2027 draft, the Giants could easily put a fair offer on the table for Porter’s services. It’s a bold move, but one New York shouldn’t hesitate to make if it truly believes it’s ready to return to Super Bowl contention under head coach John Harbaugh. Which NFL win total projections are too low, too high or just right? | The Athletic New York Giants. Projected wins: 7.1. Verdict: Just right. This may seem like a disappointment in John Harbaugh’s first season, but there needs to be an understanding of the situation the Super Bowl champion coach inherited. The Giants have won seven games combined over the past two seasons. Second-year quarterback Jaxson Dart’s play is the variable that could swing the win total dramatically in either direction. But with some growing pains expected and a defense that features questions around a potentially dominant pass rush, seven wins feels right. Malik Nabers working in practice Tuesday More work for Malik Nabers today at practice pic.twitter.com/966E1pq9Fv — SNY Giants (@SNYGiants) August 25, 2026 Pro Bowl WR Allen Robinson II: ‘Prolific’ potential for Giants’ top weapons in Matt Nagy’s offense | New York Daily News Robinson was Nagy’s guy in Chicago. And said a major reason he had a ton of individual success in the context of Chicago’s offensive output is that Nagy does not tie his offense down to his scheme. He zeroes in on matchups in the game plan and gives his top players, especially the quarterback and his go-to weapons, flexibility to adjust on the fly. “We went to the playoffs two out of those first three years,” Robinson said. “And I had a lot of success in that as a receiver from just his ultimate trust in me building with Mitchell Trubisky and us kind of also having the keys being able to make in-game adjustments and double-moving routes on the fly. He gives the players — ‘say’ is the wrong word — but once you get to the line of scrimmage, you have a lot of ability as you practice through different checks, you can get to a lot of different things.” From Big Blue View Calvin Austin appeared to suffer serious knee injury at Tuesday practice Unofficial depth chart: Giants’ RB Tyrone Tracy drops to second team Are the Giants primed for a breakout in 2026?
