title: Josh Ezeudu trade: NY Giants send offensive lineman to Kansas City Chiefs
summary: The New York Giants have traded guard Josh Ezeudu to the Kansas City Chiefs, per a report form Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo of NFL.com. The Giants are receiving a seventh-round pick in return for Ezeudu. Ezeudu, 26, was originally drafted by the Giants out of North Carolina in the third round of the 2022 […]
full_text: New York Giants offensive lineman Joshua Ezeudu.﻿ | Getty Images The New York Giants have traded guard Josh Ezeudu to the Kansas City Chiefs, per a report form Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo of NFL.com . The Giants are receiving a seventh-round pick in return for Ezeudu. Ezeudu, 26, was originally drafted by the Giants out of North Carolina in the third round of the 2022 NFL Draft. He primarily served as depth at left guard as a rookie, playing 289 snaps at the position. He was used as a swing tackle in 2023 and 2024, usually backing up Andrew Thomas at left tackle. Ezeudu appeared to move up the Giants’ depth chart after the team traded guard Daniel Faalele to the Jacksonville Jaguars for a sixth-round pick after the first preseason game against the Minnesota Vikings. Ezeudu played 30 snaps at right guard against the Miami Dolphins before finishing the game at right tackle. It’s interesting that the Giants have been dealing from their offensive line depth, and moving to recoup lost late-round draft capital. We’ll see if the Giants are done making deals or if more are in the works. The emergence of rookie tackle J.C. Davis, a sixth-round pick, may have influenced this trade. There is also the possibility that the Giants might be looking for a way to keep both Lucas Patrick and Bryan Hudson on the roster. Patrick and Hudson have seemingly been vying for the backup center spot, but both have guard flexibility.
author: Chris Pflum

title: Calvin Austin injury: NY Giants WR carted off with right knee injury
summary: Calvin Austin, who looked like he had earned the starting slot receiver job with the New York Giants, suffered what could be a “serious knee injury” during Tuesday’s practice. Austin went down “without contact” while running a pass route. Reportedly, co-owner John Mara was even part of the group trying to console Austin. Ryan Dunleavy […]
full_text: Calvin Austin vs. the Miami Dolphins in a preseason game. | Getty Images Calvin Austin, who looked like he had earned the starting slot receiver job with the New York Giants, suffered what could be a “ serious knee injury ” during Tuesday’s practice. Austin went down “ without contact ” while running a pass route. Reportedly, co-owner John Mara was even part of the group trying to console Austin . Ryan Dunleavy reported that “ Austin was working a 1-on-1 in-cut route against Deonte Banks when his knee buckled and he groaned in instant pain.” The Giants signed Austin after losing slot receiver Wan’Dale Robinson, who topped 1,000 receiving yards last season, in free agency. He had been one of quarterback Jaxson Dart’s favorite targets throughout training camp, and appeared to be a lock to make the roster and play a significant role on offense. In Saturday’s preseason game against the Miami Dolphins, Austin showed his versatility with a 21-yard rush, two receptions for 24 yards, and two punt returns for 29 yards. On Monday, head coach John Harbaugh had praised the surprising versatility of the 5-foot-9, 162-pound Austin. “It’s pretty clear all the things he does well. And the nice thing about Calvin is that he can play all three spots. You can move him around in any one of those positions,” Harbaugh said. “He’s a quote, unquote, smaller receiver, and yet he can go outside. He’s played outside a lot. You don’t see that that often. So, he gives us a lot of versatility that way, and that – kind of everything you ask him to do, he does it well. He’s very reliable. Runs the right routes, makes catches. He’s been that way kind of his whole career.” Austin spent the first three seasons of his career with the Pittsburgh Steelers. As Baltimore Ravens head coach, Harbaugh competed against him twice a year. If Austin’s injury is as severe as early reports indicate, it could open a spot on the roster for Odell Beckham Jr . Even though Beckham has been a sentimental favorite to earn a roster spot, until now reality has been that there might not have been room for him . That may have now changed.
author: Ed Valentine

title: Film review: J.C. Davis impressed in preseason action
summary: The New York Giants easily handled the Miami Dolphins in a 26-3 preseason Week 2 victory, with their backup offensive line seeing extensive action. Marcus Mbow started at right tackle, while sixth-round rookie J.C. Davis got the nod at left tackle and played all 81 offensive snaps. Davis turned in the Giants’ highest overall offensive […]
full_text: J.C. Davis | Getty Images The New York Giants easily handled the Miami Dolphins in a 26-3 preseason Week 2 victory, with their backup offensive line seeing extensive action. Marcus Mbow started at right tackle, while sixth-round rookie J.C. Davis got the nod at left tackle and played all 81 offensive snaps. Davis turned in the Giants’ highest overall offensive grade, as well as the team’s best run- and pass-blocking grades, according to Pro Football Focus. The depth on the Giants offensive line should not be overstated. There are two day-three picks who are handling swing-tackle snaps, and doing so at an impressive level, albeit it’s against the Dolphins backups. Davis surrendered no pressures and neither did Mbow, but the swing tackle competition remains a topic of conversation, while cross-training for the interior is still a possibility. Davis is 6’5, 335-pounds, and was selected in the sixth-round ( 192nd overall ) out of Illinois. He now has 102 snaps in the preseason with zero pressures allowed. Here’s some tape from his play against the Dolphins. J.C. Davis is No. 74 at left tackle Pass protection via GIPHY Davis quickly locates Max Llewellyn (57) – who is a seventh-round rookie out of Iowa. Davis cuts off the angle with ease on the quick 45-set. Davis uses a forceful outside punch that readjusts to account for Llewellyn’s chop. Davis then attempts to swat the inside hand of Llewellyn downward; it ends up resulting in hand fighting, with Davis mirroring and framing his block perfectly against the rookie. via GIPHY Davis quickly latches onto David Ojabo (50) with a strong outside punch to establish contact, followed closely with inside hand placement on the small of Ojabo’s back. Davis earns upper-body control and his feet shift with Ojabo’s momentum up the arc. Davis is controlled with low-hips and active feet; again, a very impressive, yet quick, rep. via GIPHY Davis uses a quick jump-set to frame and attack Cam Rice (58) while out on an island. Rice stalemates with Davis and tries to find room around Davis’ edge, but the rookie locks him up until Jameis Winston (19) throws the ball. via GIPHY Davis shows patience above on the high-side rush. He doesn’t get too eager and commit too early. His feet dictate his positioning, he stays square to target, and he attacks when appropriate with his hands. via GIPHY Davis showed his anchor on the edge on this quick throw to Odell Beckham Jr. (3). Rice attempted to bull-rush Davis; while some ground was conceded, Davis does a phenomenal job just sitting back on his hips and maintaining great leverage to exhaust rice’s power on the bull-rush. via GIPHY Davis matches Rice’s high-side rush and handles the inside spin well right into the guard. Davis had answers in pass-protection against these back-end Dolphin rushers. via GIPHY I love to see Davis kick out against the wide defender but then effortlessly handle the original 4i-shade on the twist. Positioning and depth are key for a tackle with this assignment, and Davis executes well on both, while taking on the transition and repositioning himself well from a framing and leverage perspective. Again, a very good job by J.C. Davis. Run Blocking via GIPHY Davis and the guard annihilate the Dolphins’ defensive tackle on this double-team block. Davis gets low and he drives through the opponent, causing a massive pile up of players. Davis’ lower-leg drive and how he gets low into contact allows him to land the block effectively. via GIPHY Here’s another double-team where Davis must assume the block once the guard vacates to his secondary assignment. Davis is able to stay low into contact, and does get his hips more to the center of the defensive lineman, allowing him to turn the chest of the defensive lineman. Guard Aaron Stinnie didn’t transition cleanly, leaving Davis to handle two blockers. Still, the control displayed by Davis was impressive. via GIPHY Davis is the point of attack tackle on this under-center, split-zone, run. Davis contacts Seth Coleman (90) and moves him off his spot, while using torque to control. Davis places his hips into the rushing lane, and controls Coleman to disallow access to the 3-Hole. Areas of improvement I’m not saying that J.C. Davis struggles with strength, per se, but there were several plays on tape where he executes his assignment, but the strength doesn’t pop, and that is noteworthy against the Dolphins’ third team. via GIPHY I love how low Davis gets into contact here, and we see him explode low-to-high, but Keith Cooper Jr. (97) sinks down and sets the edge, while conceding little to no space to Davis. Plays like this came up a few times against the Dolphins: via GIPHY Again, not terrible positioning, but little push, which allows Cameron Goode (53) to set the edge and eventually curl around Davis to assist with the tackle. Goode gets low and it doesn’t appear like Davis threatened him much with his power to create any space, despite winning the initial leverage battle. Perhaps Davis’ angle into the wide contact – when attacking – is an area in which he can be more controlled, which can allow him to unlock his power potential. via GIPHY via GIPHY Run game power from an angle wasn’t the only time power came up as a possible concern. Here are two pass protection reps where Davis’ anchor was challenged. While he did handle his business, with some help, there was space conceded and that should be acknowledged if we’re honestly evaluating the young player. Still, I’m not concerned about Davis’ overall power. He is a young player who has put very good tape on film so far. I am encouraged about his ability and hope to see him become an asset for the New York Giants. Final thoughts Davis has handled himself well in preseason. He played all 81 snaps against the Dolphins and he appeared confident, competent, and controlled. His feet, hips, hands, and eyes are all aligned, and he’s flashed power. The question becomes – can he do this against starting NFL talent? That remains to be seen. We’ve witnessed some power questions in the run game; but at the end of the day, these are positive developments for a day three pick who keeps ascending. The Giants’ offensive line is in a much better position now than it was the last decade plus.

title: Survey – How many games will the Giants add to their win total in 2026?
summary: Nobody seems quite sure what to make of the New York Giants as we head into the 2026 season. There was excitement early on when the Giants landed John Harbaugh to be their new head coach. That excitement subsided some when Harbaugh hired Matt Nagy as his offensive coordinator after Todd Monken became the new […]
full_text: New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh on the sideline against the Miami Dolphins | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Nobody seems quite sure what to make of the New York Giants as we head into the 2026 season. There was excitement early on when the Giants landed John Harbaugh to be their new head coach. That excitement subsided some when Harbaugh hired Matt Nagy as his offensive coordinator after Todd Monken became the new head coach of the Cleveland Browns. Likewise, it seems there was disappointment when Harbaugh didn’t immediately use his power blow up the roster and shove Joe Schoen out the door. Instead, the Giants only tinkered with the top of their depth chart in free agency. The Giants were praised for their draft class, particularly adding Arvell Reese , Sisi Mauigoa , and Colton Hood , and it was generally heralded as one of the league’s best draft hauls. Since then, however, the Giants’ rookies haven’t gotten much conversation at the national level. That largely seems to be due to a perception that the Giants’ 4-13 record in 2025 is all there is to the team. This week, Bill Barnwell at ESPN wrote that he believes the Giants will be one of the teams to improve and exceed expectations this year. Barnwell argues that based on their point differential, the Giants should have been a seven-win team last year, and simply regressing to the mean would give them a three-game improvement over last year. Back in May I wrote that last year’s Giants are an extreme statistical outlier to lose as many games they should have won, and they’re better than their record says they are. Furthermore, the Giants are in a much better spot than they would be had they won seven games last year. After all, they might not have fired Brian Daboll, nor would they have been in position to draft Reese, Mauigoa, or Hood. So with that in mind, this week we want to ask you how many more games you think the Giants will win in 2026 than in 2025? Do you think they’ll improve their win total by six or more games, breaking into the double digits with 10+ wins? Do you think they’ll win four or five more games and finish as an eight- or nine-win team? Do you think they’ll only win two or three more games and just finish with the six- or seven-win total they should have in 2025? Do you think they’ll fail to improve at all, adding zero or one win to their 2025 total? Do you think the Giants will regress and win fewer than four games in 2026? Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Giants fans and fans across the country. author: Chris Pflum

title: Are the NY Giants primed for a breakout in 2026?
summary: The New York Giants have won all of 13 games over the last three seasons combined. Even considering their trip to the playoffs in 2022, it’s been a minute since the Giants were a consistently competitive, or exciting, team. The Giants’ pursuit of John Harbaugh generated the kind of free agent excitement that we haven’t […]
full_text: New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart and edge defender Abdul Carter celebrate a victory. | Getty Images The New York Giants have won all of 13 games over the last three seasons combined. Even considering their trip to the playoffs in 2022, it’s been a minute since the Giants were a consistently competitive, or exciting, team. The Giants’ pursuit of John Harbaugh generated the kind of free agent excitement that we haven’t seen since Peyton Manning’s free agency. Since then, however, the excitement surrounding the Giants has mellowed and the a sentiment of “they’re still the same old Giants” prevails. That said, there is some optimism surrounding the Giants in some places, and some analysts believe that they could shock the world and make a real run at the playoffs this year . Bill Barnwell of ESPN may have just given the Giants the loudest vote of confidence in predicting that the Giants are in the company of the Kansas City Chiefs, Baltimore Ravens, and Detroit Lions as one of the teams most likely to improve in 2026 . Barnwell’s argument is that not only should John Harbaugh bring much-needed stability, the Giants’ win total was so far below their level of play last year that they should improve even if nothing changed. New York finished 4-13, but its Pythagorean expectation suggests that Big Blue performed at a 7.1 win rate. Accounting for the 17-game schedule, the Giants are one of only 13 teams since 1990 to finish three-plus wins short of their expected win total by point differential, joining last season’s Chiefs on that list. He continues to point out that the Giants had six different opportunities in which they could — or should — have notched a win against a team with a winning record. Week 2, against the Dallas Cowboys Week 7, against the Denver Broncos Week 10, against the Chicago Bears Week 11, against the Green Bay Packers Week 12, against the Detroit Lions Week 15, against the Minnesota Vikings That’s six losses that could have gone the other way against teams with winning records. The Giants held fourth-quarter leads in five of the six — and final- minute leads in three. They lost four games where they held a win probability of at least 90% in the fourth quarter. The rest of the league lost just 15 such games combined. In other words, the Giants own 21 percent of the entire NFL’s fourth-quarter collapses in which the losing team had at least a 90% chance of winning in the fourth quarter. And while that certainly speaks to the 2025 teams’ struggles with being consistently competent, it also shows that they had the talent to compete against playoff caliber teams. Losing the way the Giants did last year is a pretty massive outlier. I’d argue that being one of 13 teams in the last 35 years to underperform this badly only partly describes the situation when you also consider how frequently the 4-13 Giants were in position to beat winning teams. Interestingly, where we’ve heard nothing but scorn for Matt Nagy and his offense, Barnwell is almost wildly optimistic for the Giants’ upside on that side of the ball. At least as long as Jaxson Dart , Andrew Thomas , Malik Nabers , and Cam Skattebo stay health. The offense is the source of a high ceiling and a low floor. Giants fans are understandably enthused about a core built around Dart, Nabers, running back Cam Skattebo and high-end left tackle Andrew Thomas. The promise of all four on the field at the same time hints at a step forward for an offense that has finished 30th or worse in scoring four times over the past six years. … If they’re all healthy and live up to expectations, the Giants could take a massive leap forward on offense, which ranked 22nd in 2025. The health of their star players is, of course, the the primary concern for the Giants. Of course, that’s also true of pretty much every team in the NFL. Barnwell is less optimistic regarding the Giants’ defense. He has concerns regarding the run defense without Dexter Lawrence and the pass defense without Cor’Dale Flott. Personally, I wonder just how consistently the Giants will be able to keep up with high-powered offenses or put enough pressure on opposing offenses to push them out of a “balanced” game plan — or at least do so without Jaxson Dart playing recklessly. On the flip side, I believe that Dennard Wilson’s take on the “Ravens 2.0” scheme fits the players better from both a schematic and philosophic perspective. This is a hyper-athletic and aggressive defensive roster, and I believe Wilson’s defense will allow them to play as such. At the same time, I think I’ve seen enough to say that Wilson and Harbaugh are far more detail-oriented and hold everyone to a higher level of accountability than Shane Bowen and Brian Daboll. That seems to have energized Abdul Carter , who has been terrorizing offensive linemen all camp. Likewise, we’ve also seen players like Deonte Banks , Tyler Nubin , and Greg Newsome II all raise their games significantly under coaches Donald D’Alesio and Addison Lynch. Ultimately, Barnwell believes the Giants can make a real run at the playoffs this year. I believe they have a legitimate shot at surprising the league and becoming a last-place team that jumps into the playoffs in 2026, but so much will depend on whether the offensive standouts stay healthy for much (or all) of the year. Considering I predicted a 10-win season, I can’t disagree with him. But personal bias aside, the 2025 Giants were a massive outlier which should regress to their predicted win total and win seven games. That alone would be a three-game improvement over the results from last year. From there, is it so hard to believe that adding Harbaugh (and his coaching staff), Nabers, Skattebo, a more mature and committed Carter, resurgent Banks, Newsome, Nubin, Isaiah Likely , Tremaine Edmunds , Jordan Stout , Arvell Reese , Sisi Mauigoa , and Malachi Fields would amount to more than NO additional wins over what the Giants should have won last year? The Giants’ inclusion on Barnwell’s list beside the Ravens, Lions, and Chiefs may be a surprise to some, but it seems like a pretty safe bet to me.
author: Chris Pflum

title: NY Giants’ J.C. Davis took advantage of ‘great opportunity’ vs. Dolphins
summary: New York Giants’ rookie sixth-round pick, J.C. Davis, played all 81 snaps at left tackle for the New York Giants in Saturday’s 26-3 victory over the Miami Dolphins. Davis was the highest-graded Giants’ offensive player, and he has yet to surrender a pressure in 102 offensive snaps (46 pass-blocking snaps). Davis spoke to the New […]
full_text: J.C. Davis in action vs. Miami. | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images New York Giants’ rookie sixth-round pick, J.C. Davis, played all 81 snaps at left tackle for the New York Giants in Saturday’s 26-3 victory over the Miami Dolphins. Davis was the highest-graded Giants’ offensive player, and he has yet to surrender a pressure in 102 offensive snaps (46 pass-blocking snaps). Davis spoke to the New York media on Monday. Davis opened by discussing the heat; he said the last time he played a game this hot was when he played for New Mexico, prior to his two seasons at Illinois. “I think it was a great opportunity for the coaches to see my ability, what I could do at left tackle, and I think it went pretty good,” Davis said. “Of course, I’ve got things to improve on, but overall, it was a good game. We got the win. That was the most important thing.” Davis recently moved from taking reps exclusively with the third team to getting second-team reps. He said the message from the coaching staff has been “just keep working.” Davis is learning from start left tackle Andrew Thomas. “As far as watching them, just seeing how different it is – from being that guy at Illinois almost, but he’s that guy in the NFL,” Davis said. “He does way different stuff than me, but I’m trying to pick up and learn from him and pick off stuff that he does. Some stuff can’t do what he does; that’s him.” The Giants now have two swing-tackles in J.C. Davis and Marcus Mbow, both who could possibly also be considered for guard play. In the case of Davis, though, it would be a first. Davis looked impressive so far through two preseason games, and looks like an emerging depth piece for the Giants.

Let me go out there and do what I do best.” This means increased usage as an aggressive press corner in man coverage. Which NFL Teams Have The Best Skill Position Players? Ranking All 32 Groups | FOX Sports 23. New York Giants. If the Giants are sure that both WR Malik Nabers and RB Cam Skattebo will be ready for the start of the season, this group could be ranked higher. But Nabers is still in the process of returning from a torn ACL and Skattebo is dealing with an ankle injury, so while the early reports are encouraging, the longer-term prospects are at least a little murky. Nabers is the real key because he’s far and away the Giants’ most dangerous weapon. They’ll piece together the rest of the receiving corps with Darius Slayton, Darnell Mooney, Calvin Austin and rookie Malachi Fields, and maybe what’s left of Odell Beckham Jr. New York is also hoping for a leap from TE Isaiah Likely, a John Harbaugh transport from Baltimore who often thrived in limited action behind Mark Andrews. 2026 NFL Preseason Week 2 Winners and Losers | Bleacher Report Loser: Tyrone Tracy Jr., RB, New York Giants. Over the last two weeks, Tyrone Tracy Jr.’s stock has plummeted. In the New York Giants’ preseason opener, he missed a block that allowed Minnesota Vikings safety Jay Ward to crush quarterback Jaxson Dart on a sack. In this week’s game against the Miami Dolphins, Tracy lost a fumble before halftime. He finished with six carries for 26 yards. Devin Singletary outperformed him, logging eight carries for 40 yards and a touchdown. While this may seem like an overreaction, it wouldn’t be a surprise to see the Giants move on from Tracy. Big Blue signed Narris Harris, a 6’1″, 232-pound ball-carrier who can split early-down touches with Cam Skattebo. Singletary may have played his way into the No. 3 spot. Tracy is the most dynamic pass-catcher of the group, but if the Giants believe he’s a liability in pass protection, they may cut or trade him. Feels like Arvell Reese will get a weekly #BaldyBreakdown this year . @Giants @arvxll "Step up; Blow it up". It's his mantra….just follow the red wing tip shoes. Violent and Swift. #BaldysBreakdowns pic.twitter.com/XcAG9tfxp0 — Brian Baldinger (@BaldyNFL) August 23, 2026 Projecting NY Giants’ 53-man roster entering final week of preseason | The Record Defensive line (6). Starters: D.J. Reader, Shelby Harris, Chauncey Golston. Backups: Darius Alexander, Bobby Jamison-Travis, Leki Fotu What we have seen: This is going to be the priority of the personnel department and coaching staff over the next two weeks. We’re including Golston here because he has flashed at 5-technique. Could he legit hold up as a starter in the base run defense? That’s a tough ask. I think the Giants will be looking for depth at this position. There are questions about Alexander against the run that have emerged, so until he firms up there, the Giants have more work to do. The waiver wire and/or trade market should factor here. Giants roster projection: Has Odell Beckham Jr. done enough to secure a spot? | The Athletic In: Malik Nabers, Darius Slayton, Darnell Mooney, Malachi Fields, Calvin Austin III, Braxton Berrios Out: Odell Beckham Jr., Isaiah Hodgins, Beaux Collins, Dalen Cambre, Jalin Hyatt, Xavier Gipson, Ryan Miller, Gunner Olszewski (IR) It may feel wrong to not see Beckham on the 53-man, and I don’t make the choice lightly. The fan favorite has looked sharp in camp and still clearly has something left. He made a couple Dolphins defensive backs look silly in one-on-ones and showed off some wiggle after the catch on his first reception Saturday. However, he also dropped what would have been a touchdown reception. It’s a mistake a player fighting for a spot can’t make. Berrios has made a ton of catches during camp and offers more special teams flexibility, so I ultimately decided to give him the final spot. Predicting NFL teams most likely to improve in 2026 season | ESPN.com That’s six losses that could have gone the other way against teams with winning records. The Giants held fourth-quarter leads in five of the six — and final-minute leads in three. They lost four games where they held a win probability of at least 90% in the fourth quarter. The rest of the league lost just 15 such games combined. The Giants are just the fourth team to lose four of those games in a season, joining the 2013 Buccaneers, 2009 Steelers and … 2015 Giants, who also got their head coach fired (or forced out), with Tom Coughlin’s tenure ending. Dennard Wilson’s defense will be tested to begin the campaign, as the Giants start their season against the Cowboys and Rams before the schedule briefly softens. Over the full season, the Giants project to face the league’s eighth-toughest schedule by the FPI’s algorithm, which could dampen their chances of making it to the postseason. I believe they have a legitimate shot at surprising the league and becoming a last-place team that jumps into the playoffs in 2026, but so much will depend on whether the offensive standouts stay healthy for much (or all) of the year. title: Jets announce Jason Sanders is their kicker
summary: Throughout training camp the Jets have been conducting a competition at kicker to replace Nick Folk. Former Dolphins kicker Jason Sanders has gone against journeyman Cade York. The team has made a decision. York has been waived. This alone would not guarantee that the team has chosen Sanders. It wouldn’t be inconceivable for the Jets […]
full_text: Miami Dolphins place kicker Jason Sanders (7) celebrates a go ahead field goal with seconds left in the game against New York Jets at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, Jan. 8, 2023. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Throughout training camp the Jets have been conducting a competition at kicker to replace Nick Folk. Former Dolphins kicker Jason Sanders has gone against journeyman Cade York. The team has made a decision. York has been waived. The Jets are waiving Cade York, per source. — Zack Rosenblatt (@ZackBlatt) August 25, 2026 This alone would not guarantee that the team has chosen Sanders. It wouldn’t be inconceivable for the Jets to bring in additional competition before the preseason finale Friday night against the Giants. However, special teams coach Chris Banjo explained the decision to the media shortly after the news broke. Banjo indicated that the team is comfortable going into the season with Sanders handling the placekicking duties. STC Chris Banjo says Jason Sanders “has won the job” at placekicker. Cade York has been waived. Banjo says he feels “really, really good about where Jason is.” Cites his experience in the AFC East as a positive. #Jets pic.twitter.com/bfrmIGh9v2 — Rich Cimini (@RichCimini) August 25, 2026 The timing of this decision is interesting from the standpoint that both kickers struggled in practice yesterday. Sanders himself missed three of five field goal attempts. But the Jets have decided the entire body of work is more significant than a single rough practice. There is a logic to this. Sanders was perfect through the first two preseason games. He missed 2025 with an injury but hit more than 90% of his field goal attempts two years ago the last time he played. He also has a First Team All Pro selection to his name, which he earned in 2021. At the kicker spot you are always a few missed attempts from lacking job security, but is sounds like the Jets are comfortable with Jason Sanders as their Week 1 kicker.

title: Eagles Training Camp Practice Notes: Riq Woolen intercepts Jalen Hurts twice at The Linc
summary: Tonight marked the sixteenth Philadelphia Eagles training camp practice ahead of the 2026 NFL season. Here’s what I observed from the team’s one and only public session of the summer at Lincoln Financial Field! EAGLES PRACTICE NOTES PRACTICE ATTENDANCE The Eagles announced “more than 45,000 fans” in attendance. Based on what I saw, I think […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - JULY 30: Philadelphia Eagles cornerback Riq Woolen #2 runs a drill during the Philadelphia Eagles training camp on July 30th, 2026 at Jefferson Health Training Complex in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Tonight marked the sixteenth Philadelphia Eagles training camp practice ahead of the 2026 NFL season. Here’s what I observed from the team’s one and only public session of the summer at Lincoln Financial Field! EAGLES PRACTICE NOTES EAGLES INJURY REPORT: IN-PRACTICE INJURIES: OT Lane Johnson seemed to get banged up early in practice. He went to the sideline and talked to a trainer. He remained on the sideline for the rest of practice with a helmet in his hand. He did seem to be shaking his left leg around at times. Fred Johnson filled in for Lane at right tackle (no practice for Markel Bell). DT Jordan Davis suffered an upper body injury and was looked at by trainers. He put a brace on his arm and returned to team drills. TE E.J. Jenkins suffered an upper body injury and was looked at by trainers. DID NOT PARTICIPATE: OG Landon Dickerson (not injury related/rest) It’s worth noting that Dickerson was carted off the field with an injury at last year’s public practice . TE Eli Stowers (hamstring) OT Markel Bell (thumb/leg) CB Jonathan Jones (shoulder) CB Jakorian Bennett (knee) TE Grant Calcaterra (back) S Cole Wisniewski (concussion) LIMITED PARTICIPATION: CB Mac McWilliams (shoulder) REMOVED FROM THE INJURY REPORT: OG Willie Lampkin Lampkin got banged up on Saturday night and missed Monday’s practice. RB Dameon Pierce Pierce missed a lot of camp before recently returning to practice in a limited capacity. Now he’s full go. DT Byron Young Young was limited on Monday. OT John Ojukwu Ojukwu was limited on Monday. WR Danny Gray Gray was limited on Monday. DT Gabe Hall Hall wasn’t actually on the injury report but he did appear to get banged up on Monday. Apparently he’s OK. JALEN HURTS UPDATE: It was hardly all bad for Hurts but there was ultimately more bad than good. THE GOOD: Hurts rolled right and threw across his body (he continues to do this more often than he has in the past, mostly for better than for worse this summer) to find Dontayvion Wicks for a good gain. Hurts hit Darius Cooper on a curl for first down yardage. Hurts threw a nice ball to Saquon Barkley, who made an over-the-shoulder touchdown grab with Zack Baun trailing (see video below). Saquon with an INSANE TD catch 🔥 pic.twitter.com/1bOiHXbwWJ — The Philly Special (@thePHIspecial) August 25, 2026 JALEN HURTS UPDATE (continued): THE GOOD: Hurts delivered a strike to DeVonta Smith on a comeback. Hurts found DeVonta again, this time in stride on a dig, to beat a trailing Woolen who was not in position to make a tackle after the catch. Lots of YAC for Smitty (see video below). Hurts threw touchdown passes to both Makai Lemon and Hollywood Brown, though I’d give more credit there to scheme/design. Lemon was left wide open by the defense after beginning the play lined up in the backfield. Brown got open after Andrew Mukuba moved up closer to the line of scrimmage and bumped into Woolen. See videos below: Jalen Hurts finds Hollywood Brown for 6 on a late crosser 🙌🏼 pic.twitter.com/AHSq3K6XA7 — The Philly Special (@thePHIspecial) August 25, 2026 An easy TD for Makai Lemon pic.twitter.com/ziDNKask0L — Tom Ignudo (@TomIgnudo) August 25, 2026 JALEN HURTS UPDATE (continued): THE GOOD: Hurts started a two-minute drive with back-to-back chunk gains with completions to Barkley along the left sideline and Dontayvion Wicks over the middle (ball was placed a little behind the receiver). The end of that series, however … THE BAD: Picking up from the last bullet point, Hurts threw a pick six to Riq Woolen on a ball intended for DeVonta along the right sideline. This was Woolen’s second interception of the night; he previously undercut a Lemon route over the middle of the field to come up with a takeaway. See videos below: Riq INT off of Jalen Hurts 🥷 pic.twitter.com/bb15oNzdMh — The Philly Special (@thePHIspecial) August 25, 2026 2nd Woolen INT this open practice. This one a pick 6. Kind of bad by Hurts, but REALLY good by Riq !!! #FlyEaglesFly pic.twitter.com/9iJ9Er1jZs — Big Head Konecny (@BigHeadKonecny) August 25, 2026 JALEN HURTS UPDATE (continued): THE BAD: As I’ve previously noted, Hurts has thrown a lot of interceptions this summer. Certainly much more than he has in previous training camps ( Eliot Shorr-Parks’ charting says 13 INTs … after having 15 in the last four training camps combined ). Is this the end of the world? No. Well, I’m sure the ever-so turnover-averse Nick “End every drive with a kick” Sirianni doesn’t love it. And it’s obviously not ideal. But I don’t think it would be accurate to say he’s had a bad summer just because he’s thrown a lot of picks. After watching the offense go overboard on turnover avoidance at all costs last season, I think it’s good to see Hurts taking some more chances. The offense has had good moments, just as there were some tonight. But there’s obviously a balance to be struck between being aggressive and being reckless. I don’t think Hurts has been the latter. But we’ll see if this trend carries over into the regular season or not. Hurts threw a pass to Lemon on a slant that was knocked down by Quinyon Mitchell. A Hurts deep shot to DeVonta Smith was a bit underthrown. DeVonta still had a chance to make the play, which he didn’t … in part because Mitchell was able to make up ground while DeVonta slowed down. See video below: Quinyon Mitchell breaks up a deep ball from Jalen Hurts (Smith the intended target) #FlyEaglesFly pic.twitter.com/Er6YiHlZKj — Shukri Wrights (@SWrights975) August 25, 2026 JALEN HURTS UPDATE (continued): THE BAD: Hurts threw wide and out of bounds to DeVonta on a play where it looked like the ball kinda slipped out of his hand. Hurts overthrew Wicks deep on a play where he was probably “sacked” anyway. Hurts rolled left and wasn’t able to get the ball within Lemon’s catch radius. Let’s talk Riq Woolen! Well, we’ve already mentioned him. But just wanted to stress that he had a strong night with the two picks. As we said last week, it’s not always going to be pretty with him. He will be frustrating at times. But while there might be some low lows, there will also be pretty high highs. He’s a playmaker and a net positive. Kinda feel like Nolan Smith is being slept on. He beat Lane Johnson (!) to the inside to notch a “sack” on Hurts early in practice. Not sure if this was the rep where Lane got banged up. Smith’s been overshadowed by Jalyx Hunt’s ascent to potential stardom but he’s no chopped liver. Speaking of Jalyx, he was cooking Fred Johnson tonight. There was a rep where he beat Big Fred around the edge for what probably would’ve been a strip-sack by getting to Hurts in his windup. Hunt also had a nice rep in coverage where he was in position to blow up DeVonta Smith in the flat after a short reception from under center play-action. Jalen Carter had an excellent swim move to beat a blocker (think it was either Cam Jurgens or Tyler Steen) and be in position for a TFL on Saquon Barkley. Drew Kendall logged first-team left guard reps tonight with Dickerson resting. Tank Bigsby had a couple nice runs that looked like they would’ve went for big gains. BACKUP QUARTERBACK BATTLE UPDATE: Andy Dalton was first up at QB2 tonight. He overthrew Darius Cooper to the left side, not unlike how the veteran previously missed Cooper and Eli Stowers on Saturday night. Dalton did later hit a crossing Elijah Moore, who was schemed wide open, for a catch-and-run touchdown. Tanner McKee threw a good ball to Hollywood Brown along the right sideline at one point. He also made another connection with Darius Cooper to move the offense into plus territory during a two-minute drill towards the end of practice. McKee also found Moore to get into field goal range…

title: Sean Mannion talks Eagles backup quarterback battle and more
summary: The Eagles are in the final phase of training camp and have just one preseason game left to play. Offensive coordinator Sean Mannion spoke to reporters on Monday about the the offense’s growth from week-to-week as they approach the season. He also gave new OL coach Chris Kuper a lot of credit for the development […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - AUGUST 01: Philadelphia Eagles offensive coordinator Sean Mannion reacts during the Philadelphia Eagles training camp on August 1st, 2026 at Jefferson Health Training Complex in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Eagles are in the final phase of training camp and have just one preseason game left to play. Offensive coordinator Sean Mannion spoke to reporters on Monday about the the offense’s growth from week-to-week as they approach the season. He also gave new OL coach Chris Kuper a lot of credit for the development we’re seeing from the young offensive lineman. Mannion said he isn’t sure yet whether he’ll call Friday’s preseason game against the Bengals from the sideline or up in the booth, but he appreciated the chance to try both options over the past two weeks. He admitted that there are differences in the two approaches, but he feels really comfortable with both. Here’s what the OC had to say: On the QB2 battle When choosing who will be QB2, Mannion said that they evaluate the entire body of work, especially knowing that they’re playing in preseason games with different parts of the depth chart. The OC noted that the games are a really useful tool for evaluation, but the competition started back in April and they’ve got tons of reps on the practice field as well. “Both quarterbacks, really all of our quarterbacks have done a really nice job in the practice setting [and] in the game setting. It’s really about the entire body of the work. Certainly, the preseason’s part of that, but there is a ton of banked reps going all the way back to the spring as well.” Mannion said that they aren’t at a point to name who will be the team’s backup quarterback Week 1, and explained they still have several practices this week and before the season opener to finalize things. The OC was complimentary of Tanner McKee , saying that the QB did a nice job operating and got the ball out fast – something Mannion said Andy Dalton also did well. He went on to talk about how Dalton’s experience is an added benefit to him being around. “He’s a veteran in this league. He’s got well over a hundred starts. That’s unique. We get a chance to be around him, Tanner, Cole [Payton], Jalen [Hurts] every day. That’s part of what he brings to the room. Everyone’s bringing something to the table. Tanner, Cole, Jalen, obviously, they all bring their own experiences. It is something unique to Andy with having so much experience, but ultimately, it’s an evaluation on the field, both in the practice and the games. That’s the driving force.” On Jalen Hurts in joint practices “[Hurts] did a good job. The first day, we had a lot of big plays and just a couple turnovers we need to clean up. That’s always a focus for us, but you could really see the run game come to life, you could see the play passes off of it. We hit a nice pylon route to Elijah [Moore], but you could see the explosives in the past game as well. A couple turnovers, those are obviously things we always want to address. We talk about the ball relentlessly, but he did a really nice job. For the guys who didn’t play in the game, they’ve got a ton of great work in those two practices against the Patriots. I was really happy with how Jalen played throughout.” On Makai Lemon Mannion was emphatic that the rookie WR has been working hard to get back on the field, and they were excited to get him back on the practice field Monday. He noted that Lemon has been really engaged mentally, and he’s done a nice job with the things he’s been able to do. “[Lemon’s] been locked in [for] all the walkthrough settings. Even when he can’t get the rep, he’s kind of shadowing his position on the field and staying super engaged.” The OC later said that he isn’t worried about Lemon having to catch up after missing all the time earlier in training camp, because he’s been super engaged and putting in a lot of work. “He’s been a total pro about his approach to rehab, his approach to the mental side of the game. Like I said, the unfortunate nature of football is sometimes you might miss some time, but he’s done everything in his power despite not having those physical reps to be ready for us to make an impact.” On run game improvements Mannion was asked what stood out about the run game against the Patriots, and he pointed to the execution and play style. “I thought, obviously, the starting unit wasn’t in there, but that second unit [and] third unit, they really did a nice job. We controlled the line of scrimmage early in the game, kind of that first series. I thought the play style was on display. “ The OC went on to say that the three things he wanted to see in their second preseason game was execution, fundamentals, and play style. He admitted that they were a little sloppy in terms of fundamentals and execution at times in their first game against the Ravens, but overall, Mannion thought it was much improved in game two, particularly with the offensive line. He didn’t want to give too much away in terms of their plans to utilize a fullback, as the team has done in the past, but said that position versatility is a priority. On Carson Steele “[Carson Steele] carried a heavy workload late in that game, and he handled it really nicely. There’s so many guys across our roster that put the work in every day. Carson was a great example of getting an opportunity for expanded reps in the preseason and really did a nice job with it. Did a great job with the ball in his hand, run and pass. There could certainly be a role for him. I was excited to see him go out there and really thrive in the reps he got.” On the OL development Mannion talked about the pre-set protection calls and explained that it’s on the offensive line unit initially, and then the QB has a hand in it, as well. He said that the play and protection scheme will dictate how much is on the quarterback’s plate. “It would be dependent on the protection scheme. We have multiple different protection schemes. Some of them it would be the quarterback would have the final say. Some of them it’s communication within the offensive line unit. They’ve both done a nice job — both units I mean. There’s so much communication on the offensive line that, I think, goes unseen. Our centers have done a great job. Jalen’s done a great job with some of our pass protection schemes where he does need to make adjustments. He’s done a nice job of that as well.” The OC said that the OL group has shown physicality and effort every day, and you could see that on the tape. He also noted it wasn’t just the starting unit that’s been doing a good job, and the second and third units are getting better every day. Mannion credited new OL coach Chris Kuper with the development of that group. “[Chris Kuper]’s a great teacher. It’s total focus on the fundamentals. He’s done an outstanding job for us. You can see him every day after practice with those young guys working on all the finer points of offensive line play. He brings a unique perspective having been a player himself. He’s able to lend a lot of context to, ‘Hey, this is where this adjustment to your fundamentals is super useful.’ Like I said, he’s done a great job with the whole room. Talking about those young guys that are just coming up, it’s really stood out in the preseason game with the work he’s put in with those guys.”

title: Eagles News: Makai Lemon talks about being “more professional off the field”
summary: Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Eagles rookie Makai Lemon embraces ‘professional’ mindset in injury return – The AthleticMakai Lemon said he felt a familiar pain. Yes, in his hamstring. Yes, the same hamstring that sidelined him for half of the Philadelphia Eagles’ OTAs. It was a “little tweak,” the rookie […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - JULY 30: Makai Lemon #9 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on during training camp at Jefferson Health Training Complex on July 30, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Eagles rookie Makai Lemon embraces ‘professional’ mindset in injury return – The Athletic Makai Lemon said he felt a familiar pain. Yes, in his hamstring. Yes, the same hamstring that sidelined him for half of the Philadelphia Eagles’ OTAs. It was a “little tweak,” the rookie wide receiver said, which flared when he attempted to burst, just four days into training camp. The injury caused him to miss two weeks of practices, two preseason games and the competitive parts of two joint practices with the New England Patriots. The repeat injury carried all the frustrating elements of a “here we go again” situation. “It was definitely tough,” Lemon said. “I’m real competitive. Ain’t never want to be away from this game. So, me knowing that it’s the hamstring again, I’m just making sure I take the right precautions. (I’m) learning from it so it doesn’t happen again.” Lemon, who returned to full participation in Monday’s practice, further defined his lesson as “making sure I’m more professional off the field.” He works with the team’s trainers. He adheres to the recovery plan they created for him. He makes sure to warm up properly before taking the field. 11 notes from today’s Eagles training camp practice – BGN MAKAI LEMON UPDATE: Lemon was notably working with the starting offense during his first day back. His first target resulted in an incompletion. From my angle, it looked like it may have been a drop. Others thought the throw from Hurts wasn’t on the money and/or timing may have been an issue. Later on, Lemon was utilized on a screen pass. He was also used in pre-snap motion a decent amount. Makai Lemon: “For sure” I’ll be up to speed for Week 1 – PFT Eagles wide receiver Makai Lemon returned to practice last week after an extended absence due to a hamstring injury and the rookie is confident that he’ll have enough practice time to be at full speed for the season opener. Lemon said “for sure” to a question about whether there’s enough time for him to feel like himself for the Eagles’ matchup with the Commanders and said all of the mental reps he took while off the field have served to prepare him for the task at hand. The first-round pick’s process will include as much time with quarterback Jalen Hurts as he can get. “Each and every day I feel like that chemistry and that work never stops,” Lemon said. “Each and every day after practice, just talking to him whenever I can. I feel like anytime I can build that chemistry, it’s good.” Eagles 2026 training camp practice notes, Day 15: DeVonta Smith and Makai Lemon return – PhillyVoice The Eagles finally showed a look with a fullback today, and it was… (drumroll)… Dallas Goedert. He looked less than enthused to be a lead blocker, and gave Zack Baun sort of a “We’re both vets, let’s not be heroes” kind of a block. PS Game Review – NE 24, PHI 21 – Iggles Blitz Gabe Hall had a strong showing. I said last week that he needed to be more physical. Hall did just that. He was able to shed blocks and stuff the RB multiple times. He still showed athleticism, shooting gaps and getting upfield. He drew a holding call. Rookie Zion Wilson started at NT and played a lot. Wilson is at his best when being stout as a run defender. He had a tackle. He also had a good QB pressure when NE forgot to block him. Uar Bernard took a big step forward from last week’s debut. He started slowly and got better as the game went along. He was able to get off blocks and to get to the ball. Bernard made 2 tackles. The light started to come on for him. You can see him figuring things out within the game. Albert Breer Empties His Eagles Notebook From Training Camp – SI The biggest story in Philly’s camp is what the post-A.J. Brown offense looks like and, more specifically, how quarterback Jalen Hurts looks in it. Let’s start with this: It sounds as if Hurts has a good level of self-awareness of the perception around how the past couple years have gone and seems to be subtly working to fix it, given how intentional he has been about helping to build up relationships in the locker room. And I’ve heard that team-wide, too. It’s a huge part of Nick Sirianni’s belief system anyway, but it does seem as if there’s a concerted effort to create a tighter unit, which shows up on trips like this. For example, the Eagles ran the ball effectively against the Patriots on Wednesday. The Patriots responded Thursday with some borderline shots at Saquon Barkley, and a bunch of guys came to his defense in the moment. So that part of it for Hurts and the Eagles seems to be in a good place. As for the football piece, with new OC Sean Mannion aboard, the Eagles will be under center more and will focus on reviving the run game, which should make things easier on Hurts and the skill guys around him. The flip side: It’s a scheme that demands precision, which will challenge Hurts in different ways. Riq Woolen feels like ‘a rookie again’ with the Eagles. His prove-it year is big for him and the Birds. – Inquirer Moments like his plays during Thursday’s joint practice session in New England help the fitting-in part. First, Woolen jumped an A.J. Brown out route near the goal line and picked off Drake Maye for a 100-yard pick-six. Later, he again had tight coverage on Brown and forced the ball free into the air, allowing Jalyx Hunt to make a diving interception. That Woolen’s big day came on the heels of one of his worst days of camp Wednesday was a good sign for him and the Eagles. Woolen may feel like a rookie now, but he is wise enough at 27 to know that a short memory is crucial to playing cornerback in the NFL. The younger version of himself didn’t know how to handle it, he said Monday. “That’s just part of the game and it’s part of being a DB as well,” Woolen said. “One thing may [not] go your way, but you got to be able to rebound and be able to keep playing plays and keep making plays because that’s what the coaches and team expect.” After some dark days, Marcus Epps on verge of becoming a starter again – NBCSP “It would mean everything to me,” Epps said. “I worked real hard to get back to where I’m at. It was a lot of dark days but I still got work to do. I haven’t arrived by any means. It’s a long season and we’re still here just in camp. That’s where my focus is, finishing out camp the right way and continuing to get better.” Epps is 30 now and if he does get named the starter at safety, he’d actually be the Eagles’ oldest starting defensive player this season. It’s clear that Epps brings some stability to the back end of what could be one of the NFL’s best defenses in 2026. After Mukuba got hurt in November last season, Epps filled in admirably next to Reed Blankenship. And after Blankenship left for Houston in free agency, Epps has been getting the first crack at his old job next to Mukuba in the Eagles’ defense. While Fangio has said all summer that there’s a competition for this starting safety job, he clearly became a fan of Epps last year. The Next Generation of NFL Play Callers Is Here – The Ringer One big question for 2026: Can Mannion get Hurts to throw to the middle of the field? Hurts’s aversion to middle-of-the-field throws is well documented, but that isn’t the result of a physical (or mental) inability to throw to that area. We have video evidence that he can do it. But most of those throws come against man coverage, where Hurts can read the leverage his receiver has on a defender and lead his guy to a spot. The no-throws come against zone coverage, where Hurts is forced to make anticipatory throws before his receiver arrives in a certain window. If Mannion is the “evil genius” Eagles lineman Jordan Mailata says he is, the rookie play caller should…

title: Mike McCarthy open to keeping four quarterbacks
summary: Mike McCarthy is not opposed to an unusually crowded quarterback room. In fact, the Pittsburgh Steelers head coach believes keeping four quarterbacks could provide a meaningful benefit once the regular season begins, particularly given the depth and experience Pittsburgh has assembled at the position. “I’d take six QBs in the building if it worked,” McCarthy […]
full_text: Aug 03, 2026; Latrobe, PA, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Drew Allar (16) looks to pass as quarterbacks Aaron Rodgers (8) and Mason Rudolph (2) look on during a practice session at Training camp at Saint Vincent College. Mandatory Credit: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Mike McCarthy is not opposed to an unusually crowded quarterback room. In fact, the Pittsburgh Steelers head coach believes keeping four quarterbacks could provide a meaningful benefit once the regular season begins, particularly given the depth and experience Pittsburgh has assembled at the position. “I’d take six QBs in the building if it worked,” McCarthy said via Mike DeFabo . McCarthy’s comments come as the Steelers evaluate their quarterback situation heading into the final stages of the preseason. Pittsburgh currently has four quarterbacks competing for roster spots: veteran Aaron Rodgers, Mason Rudolph, rookie Drew Allar and second-year quarterback Will Howard. While most NFL teams typically carry three quarterbacks on their active roster, McCarthy indicated that the Steelers could consider keeping all four if the roster construction allows for it. “If you have four quarterbacks in that room, especially given the quality that we have, I think it only enhances what the regular season would look like,” McCarthy said. “I’d keep six QBs in the building if it worked.” Mike McCarthy dismissed the notion that keeping four QBs would take away opportunities to develop the young passers. pic.twitter.com/alWS7XNWhj — Mike DeFabo (@MikeDeFabo) August 25, 2026 The Steelers have invested in developing the position, with Allar selected in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft and Howard entering his second season after being selected in the sixth round last year. Rudolph, meanwhile, provides significant NFL experience behind Rodgers. The potential value of carrying four quarterbacks extends beyond simply having an additional player available on game day. McCarthy believes the competition and preparation within the room can benefit the entire offense throughout the season. That philosophy also applies to Pittsburgh’s quarterback development program. McCarthy said his quarterback school could “kick up some” once the regular season arrives because the quarterbacks will no longer be working under the same time constraints that exist during training camp practices. The additional time could allow the Steelers to devote more attention to the finer details of the position, including preparation, communication, film study and offensive concepts. For a team with a veteran starter in Rodgers and two young quarterbacks in Allar and Howard, that extra developmental work could prove valuable. The Steelers also have Rudolph, who has experience in Pittsburgh’s system and has started games during his NFL career. Keeping all four would give McCarthy a veteran presence behind Rodgers while allowing the organization to continue developing its two younger quarterbacks. Ultimately, the decision will come down to roster mathematics and how the Steelers believe they can best allocate their available spots. Let us know what you think in the comments . title: Asante Samuel Sr critical of Joey Porter Jr’s contract hold in
summary: Pittsburgh Steelers cornerbacks Joey Porter Jr. and Asante Samuel Jr. share some things in common. Both are young and successful NFL corners in the Steelers secondary who are capable of being Pro Bowl players. Their dads both played in the NFL and are vocal supporters of their sons on and off the field. A four-time Pro […]
full_text: Pittsburgh Steelers cornerbacks Joey Porter Jr. and Asante Samuel Jr. share some things in common. Both are young and successful NFL corners in the Steelers secondary who are capable of being Pro Bowl players. Their dads both played in the NFL and are vocal supporters of their sons on and off the field. A four-time Pro Bowl corner and two time Super Bowl champion with the Patriots. Asante Samuel Sr. had harsh words for his son’s teammate when discussing Porter Jr.’s contract extension talks with the Steelers. “I don’t think he’s handling the situation the best way, not going to practice,” Samuel Sr. said on Say What Needs to be Sai d . “You’ve got to know when to read the room and who you’re dealing with.” Porter Jr. remains on the PUP list with a back injury and hasn’t participated in any team drills. Head coach Mike McCarthy said on Monday that he would like to see the defensive coaching staff work with Porter Jr. before the Steelers take the field against Atlanta. “These people seem like they really get offended over there in Pittsburgh,” Samuel Sr. said. “They really are in tune to what’s going on, their players, who their players are and playing their players. They do things a certain way, they don’t like to break bread.” The Steelers have already signed linebacker Nick Herbig, tight end Darnell Washington, and defensive lineman Keeanu Benton to long-term extensions. All are from the 2023 draft class that was led by Broderick Jones and Porter, who was thought to be the priority going into OTAs and minicamp. McCarthy said the talks have reached an “impasse” between the two negotiating parties. #Steelers at an impasse with Joey Porter, Junior per Mike McCarthy pic.twitter.com/VpBzn26npo — 93.7 The Fan (@937theFan) August 24, 2026 Discussions appear to be far apart and could be regarding average annual value, or guaranteed money. Seattle signed star corner Devon Witherspoon to a four-year, $132 million deal to reset the market at the position. The $33 million per year deal includes $101 million guaranteed. Patriots corner Christian Gonzalez is also up for an extension and could require a deal in the same range. It increases the price for Porter Jr. and only complicates the process for the Steelers, dealing with a shifting market rather than locking up Porter Jr. before Witherspoon signed. The two sides have until the season opener against Atlanta on September 13 to work out a deal, or Porter Jr. will play out the final year of his deal and risk being given the franchise tag going into 2027. summary: Episode four of “Hard Knocks” did not pull any emotional punches. It tugged on the heart strings, and made you feel for the team. full_text: Episode four of “Hard Knocks” did not pull any emotional punches. It tugged on the heart strings, and made you feel for the team. While there were some happy moments, there were also some heart breaking ones as well. Let’s get into it. “Hard Knocks” Episode 4 recap Jake Bobo is seen as The Enforcer on the offense. The “Draymond Green” to Jaxon Smith-Njigba’s “Steph Curry” as wide receiver coach Frisman Jackson put it. He does all the things that do not show up on the stat sheet Seahawks WR Coach Frisman Jackson explains to Jake Bobo what it means to be a glue guy 😤 New episode of Hard Knocks: Training Camp with the @Seahawks airs tonight at 9PM ET @hbomax pic.twitter.com/IgcJyThMvo — NFL (@NFL) August 25, 2026 Coach Mike Macdonald held a meeting of the leadership council to try to come up with strategies to keep the energy up in the team and hold everyone accountable. A look inside the Seahawks leadership council reflecting on their preseason opener 🗣️ The new episode of Hard Knocks: Training Camp with the @Seahawks is available now on @hbomax pic.twitter.com/Uxtcz30nb8 — NFL (@NFL) August 26, 2026 Sam Darnold takes his position as a leader on the team seriously and puts a lot of the accountability on his shoulders. Position coaches also hold themselves accountable, and preached toughness, responsibility, consistency, and playing to a high level in each of the position meetings. Interesting to see inside the Seahawks Leadership Council Members appear to be: Darnold JSN Kupp Spoon Ernest Leo JReed Chenna JLove Charbs Barner — SleeperSeahawks (@SleeperSeahawks) August 26, 2026 During an all-team meeting, Mike and the team celebrated Brady Russell becoming a father, and you could tell how proud Brady was. Mike took a moment to celebrate the life of a mentor of his who passed away, O.J. Brigance, who Mike said was the model of what it meant to be a man, and someone who he could go to whenever he needed a word of advice. He stated that Brigance would message him each game day, and was cheering for the Seahawks last season. He passed away from a long battle with ALS, and when Mike was tearing up and getting emotional, the team supported him. RIP OJ Brigance. You can see how much he meant to Mike Macdonald. — Field Gulls (@FieldGulls) August 26, 2026 We have heard tales of it, but we finally got to see John Schneider show off his film knowledge by testing the coaches with a movie quote. The answer: Steve Martin from “Three Amigos”. Classic comedy. Got a peek behind the curtain and got to see John talking to Trevon Diggs, who said he did not feel a 100 percent healthy last season, but now having a full offseason to put in the work with physical training and strength training feels as though he got his twitchiness back. He is ready to prove himself on this team. Hard Knocks provides another view inside John Schneider’s office as the #Seahawks ’ GM talks with CB Trevon Diggs about his health prior to the decision to sign him. New Hard Knocks tonight 9pm ET on @hbomax . pic.twitter.com/lIFX62oS8s — Mike Garafolo (@MikeGarafolo) August 25, 2026 With the heat in Nashville, the coaching staff was emphasizing getting in high carb meals with high protein and drinking plenty of electrolytes. Still, a few players went down in joint practice due to spasms, including Montorie Foster who got a good talking to from his parents after practice. We got to see Bobo go down with the torn ACL, and you could tell how much that loss impacted the team. Teammates and coaches alike were downtrodden after seeing him go down and scream in pain. Hard Knocks showed #Seahawks WR Jake Bobo’s torn ACL from last week. Sam Darnold knew what it was right away. Mike Macdonald: “Oh f***.” pic.twitter.com/bRtx4PO5M3 — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) August 26, 2026 The rookie talent show was a fun watch. Most of the rookies kept to AJ Barner’s instructions and did solo acts, though a couple did duets. Some had rolled up napkins thrown at them. However, Uso Seumalo stole the show with his acoustic rendition of “No Woman, No Cry” by Bob Marley. . @Seahawks rookie DT Uso Seumalo absolutely crushed a rendition of "No Woman, No Cry" at the rookie talent show. 🔥 New episode of Hard Knocks: Training Camp with the @Seahawks airs tonight at 9PM ET @hbomax pic.twitter.com/L8BDyRoq7u — NFL (@NFL) August 25, 2026 The quarterbacks bonding getting custom cowboy hats together was fun to see. Not going to lie, I am a bit disappointed Sam did not get the neon green 14 on his hat as he requested. Regardless, seeing Drew Lock at the end of the episode wearing his cowboy hat on top of his ballcap was pretty amusing. Seeing the emphasis on the small details that mattered during the preseason game was cool to see. Drew was able to take the second team offense down the field against the first team defense of the Tennessee Titan, capping it off with an Elijah Arroyo touchdown, and Foster’s run block that allowed Jacardia Wright’s 69 yard touchdown was fun to see. The Bud Clark injury was rough to watch, however, seeing how his fiancée and child supported him while he was getting the brace on was both tough and heartwarming. “Think about the unicorns” got me chuckling. Bud Clark kept a positive attitude after his injury 🙏 The new episode of Hard Knocks: Training Camp with the @Seahawks is available now on @hbomax pic.twitter.com/BL2vJD2YHk — NFL (@NFL) August 26, 2026 Uso Seumalo being the leading force on that fourth down stop was huge for him. He is fighting for a spot on the 53 man roster, and that was a huge boost for him. Mike’s message at the end of the episode was key. He emphasized how they had improved this week, and that he can see the improvement and was proud of the team and the work they were putting in. Though they lost the game, they won in other ways and improved. What were your favorite moments from the episode? Comment down below and let’s have a discussion! Join the conversation! title: ‘Hard Knocks’ captures moments after Bud Clark broke his ankle
summary: This week’s episode of ‘Hard Knocks’ was the most revealing and simultaneously the most gut-wrenching to watch for Seattle Seahawks fans. The season-ending injuries to Bud Clark and Jake Bobo were both shown on the broadcast, punctuating preceding segments in which we got to see Clark with his fiancee and their young son, as well […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - AUGUST 23: Bud Clark #9 of the Seattle Seahawks is carted off the field injured during the first half of a preseason game against the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium on August 23, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Justin Ford/Getty Images) | Getty Images This week’s episode of ‘Hard Knocks’ was the most revealing and simultaneously the most gut-wrenching to watch for Seattle Seahawks fans. The season-ending injuries to Bud Clark and Jake Bobo were both shown on the broadcast, punctuating preceding segments in which we got to see Clark with his fiancee and their young son, as well as Bobo and his heart-to-heart with receivers coach Frisman Jackson . Bud Clark featured on Hard Knocks the same day he was placed on IR… #Seahawks #budclark #hardknocks https://t.co/DEo0Adb2Qi pic.twitter.com/SF4UfeHqe0 — Tanner Phifer (@TannerPhifer) August 26, 2026 Clark, who broke his ankle on the Seahawks’ first defensive play against the Tennessee Titans, immediately screamed out, “My sh-t just broke!” after an audible snap could be heard as he planted his right ankle. Incredibly, through the intense pain after suffering an injury that would leave him sidelined for months, Clark kept a remarkably positive attitude as he made his way onto the cart. Bud Clark kept a positive attitude after his injury 🙏 The new episode of Hard Knocks: Training Camp with the @Seahawks is available now on @hbomax pic.twitter.com/BL2vJD2YHk — NFL (@NFL) August 26, 2026 “Yeah, we gravy, we gravy,” Clark told the athletic trainers. Clark later said to Coach Mike Macdonald, “Hell yeah, coach, we gravy. It hurts like a motherf—ker, though.” After he’s told they’ll get him on the cart (with an air cast on) and send him into the locker room for x-rays, Clark replied, “Alright. That sounds cool. Cool.” What the above video doesn’t show you is Clark in a video call with his fiancee and son, sounding in great spirits in the immediacy after a traumatic injury. He added, “They snap, crackle, popped my ass.” Clark’s son asked his dad, “Who did that?” To which Bud replied, “I don’t know who did. You gonna kick their butt?” His son gave an approving “mm-hmm” and asked if dad will fix his bike. There is, of course, the part where Bud (with the help of his fiancee) has to gut through the pain as his ankle is wrapped up and placed in a boot. It’s a sequence that is raw, real, heartbreaking, and heartwarming all at once, and it’s a shame that the first time Bud has been featured all series ends that way. He seems like a fun character with a great outlook on life, and he would’ve been a fun player to watch as a rookie in Mike Macdonald’s defense. We can’t wait to see Bud healthy and whole for 2027.

title: Seahawks place Bud Clark and Mason Richman on IR, sign son of ex-Seahawks starter
summary: The Seattle Seahawks returned to practice on Tuesday after Sunday’s preseason loss to the Tennessee Titans. They also made a series of roster transactions, which included three signings and the dreaded decision to place two young players on injured reserve. Bud Clark, Mason Richman are out for the year As expected, the Seahawks placed rookie […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - AUGUST 15: Bud Clark #9 of the Seattle Seahawks looks on during the third quarter during the NFL preseason game against the Dallas Cowboys at Lumen Field on August 15, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Jack Compton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks returned to practice on Tuesday after Sunday’s preseason loss to the Tennessee Titans. They also made a series of roster transactions , which included three signings and the dreaded decision to place two young players on injured reserve. Bud Clark, Mason Richman are out for the year As expected, the Seahawks placed rookie safety Bud Clark on injured reserve after breaking his ankle on the first defensive play of the Titans game. Mike Macdonald confirmed that Clark would miss “multiple months” and this IR placement confirms that the next time we’ll see him is in 2027. The news is also bad for second-year offensive lineman Mason Richman, who was making inroads as one of the primary backup guards. After walking off what looked to be a non-contact right leg injury, Macdonald said on Sunday that Richman was feared to have a “long-term” injury . It doesn’t get much more long-term than out for the whole season. Seahawks sign three free agents, including son of an ex-Seahawk Seattle had an open roster spot prior to placing Clark and Richman on IR, and the team wasted no time in filling those three vacancies. Running back Justin Jones returns after playing in the Dallas Cowboys game. He was waived shortly thereafter but will presumably get some game time versus the Kansas City Chiefs on Friday. Running back Anthony Hankerson going back to college football essentially opened up a spot for someone else at the position. Former Oregon safety Tysheem Johnson was also added to the roster. This comes with both Clark gone for the year and Rodney Thomas II recovering from recent hand surgery . Finally, offensive tackle Derrick Graham was signed following the absence of reserve Seahawks tackle Amari Kight, who did not play any snaps last Sunday. Graham’s father, also named Derrick Graham, played nine NFL seasons from 1990 to 1998. He was Seattle’s starting right guard in the 1996 and 1997 seasons before ending his career with the Oakland Raiders.
