title: Predicting NFL teams most likely to decline in 2026 season
summary: Are the Bears getting too much hype? Did the Panthers and Jaguars overachieve last season? And will the Broncos and Patriots come up short of expectations this season?
full_text:
On Monday, I was an optimist, picking five NFL teams I expect to improve in 2026 . Today, unfortunately, we hit the opposite side of the ledger. I know not to check my mentions on social media for a few days after this annual column, and I take a little longer to answer those texts from people inside the league. "Did you really have to pick us?" ... there's never a good response.

 Don't blame me. I don't have any vested interest or desire to see any team do poorly or struggle. In a zero-sum league, though, five teams improving means that five teams have to decline. And using data that has helped point toward future downswings, I will identify five teams that are likely to win fewer games in 2026.

 Since 2017, the decline column has gone 34-9 at picking teams that will fall short of their win total from the previous season, including an adjustment for the shift from 16 games to 17 per season. The improve/decline columns overall are 69-17 (.802) during that span, with a 50-36 mark (.581) against the preseason over-unders archived on Pro-Football-Reference.com. The average decline amounts to about 3.4 wins per 17 games.

 Last year , the column correctly predicted four of the five teams. The one miss was the Colts, who went 8-9 in 2024 before getting off to a white-hot start in 2025, hitting their bye at 8-2. An offense that looked perfect started to show cracks, lost Daniel Jones to a torn Achilles  and went into free fall. Without Jones or DeForest Buckner for much of the second half, the Colts lost seven straight to finish 8-9 for the second consecutive season.

 
 Subscribe: 'The Bill Barnwell Show' 

 
 But the other four teams suffered substantial steps backward. The Vikings went from 14-3 to 9-8, as J.J. McCarthy couldn't deliver on expectations under center, and Kevin O'Connell's mastery of one-score games slipped in 2025. I'm not sure that one was too surprising.

 The remaining three squads, all favorites to compete for the Super Bowl, each stunningly missed the playoffs.

 Following a 12-5 mark, the Commanders fell to 5-12 last season with one of the league's oldest rosters, a lack of young talent and Jayden Daniels  suffering through an injury-riddled season. The Lions were 15-2 in 2024, but issues with the offensive line and offensive infrastructure, injuries on defense and a tougher schedule knocked them back to 9-8.

 And then there were the Chiefs, who did the unthinkable. Expecting the Chiefs to go 15-2 again probably wasn't realistic even without knowing that Patrick Mahomes would finish the season with a torn ACL . Andy Reid's team somehow fell from 10-0 in one-score games to 1-9, and a 6-11 Chiefs team missed the playoffs for the first time since 2014.

 If you read Monday's improvement column, you know that the Chiefs and Lions are two of the teams I'm (perhaps unsurprisingly) expecting to improve in 2026. I'm going to start this year's decline column with a team that was in last year's improve column.

 Note: Schedule strength is via ESPN's Football Power Index (FPI) . 

 

 
 See more: 
 Five teams set to improve 

 
 
 Jump to: 
 CAR | CHI | DEN | JAX | NE 

 
 

 

 Chicago Bears 
 Record in 2025: 11-6 (7-4 in games decided by seven points or fewer) 
 Point differential in 2025: plus-26 
 Projected strength of schedule: 10th toughest

 I don't typically put these teams in any real order. When Bears head coach Ben Johnson said his team was the No. 1 regression candidate heading into 2026, though, how else could I start the decline column?

 Johnson, who has talked about  the importance of generating passing EPA, isn't naive about what advanced metrics expect to happen to the Bears. And he's not being naive or unrealistic in suggesting that the Bears have a shot at defying those odds. The 2025 Bears are the classic example of a team that should project to decline the following year. And the 2026 Bears have the sort of roster to prevail nonetheless. Let's take a closer look at both sides.

 If you were drawing a blueprint for a team that was likely to appear in this column, you would essentially be describing last season's Bears. An unlucky team in 2023 and 2024, the Bears got far more than their fair share of breaks for most of the 2025 season.

 

 Johnson helped drive a massive offensive improvement in terms of creating explosive plays, but the Bears were also spectacular at holding on to the football. They turned the ball over a league-low 11 times last season. They forced 33 turnovers, which helped keep afloat a defense that otherwise struggled. The Bears were 27th in points allowed per drive on possessions that didn't end with a fumble recovery or an interception. The  Kevin Byard -led secondary picked off 4.3% of opposing passes, the highest rate in the NFL.

 Some of that luck will not occur again. The Bears recovered 66.7% of the fumbles in their games last season, again the highest rate in the league. Twenty-three teams have posted a fumble recovery rate of 65% or more in any given season since 1990. Those teams went 0-for-23 at replicating that the following season, collectively recovering 49.3% of fumbles.

 Forcing fumbles is a skill, to which Charles Tillman-era Bears fans can attest, but what happens once the ball hits the ground is almost entirely random. The defense forced only 17 fumbles last season, which was right around the league average of 16.8. The offense fumbled 16 times but fell on 12 of those balls for a 75% recovery clip. (In the postseason, the Bears forced six fumbles in two games on defense and failed to recover one.)

 Forcing more takeaways than anybody else in football and turning the ball over less often than anybody else is a great way to lead the league in turnover margin. The Bears did, posting a plus-22 mark. The Texans, at plus-17, were the only team within an eight-turnover margin of Chicago.

 And though Johnson is right to put explosive play generation alongside or even ahead of turnover margin in affecting the outcome of games, teams will win a lot when the turnover margin is weighted so heavily in their favor. Turnover margins have shrunk toward zero as offenses have gotten better at protecting the football and shrunken their passing depth in recent years, but 22 teams have posted turnover margins of plus-20 or more since 1990. Their average record was just short of 13-4 after adjusting for the 17-game schedule.

 You know what's coming next. Excluding the 2025 Bears, the other 21 teams posted an average turnover margin of plus-3 the following season, with their margin declining by more than 19 takeaways on average. And 20 of those 21 teams won fewer games the following year, with the 2013 Patriots, who sustained their 12-4 record from the previous season, as the exception.

 The Bears' season started with a frustrating loss to the Vikings , with Chicago leading most of the way before melting down in the fourth quarter. It proved to be an anomaly, as an offense that ranked 18th in EPA per play during the first three quarters of games was also the best in the NFL from the beginning of the fourth quarter onward. That -- and some luck -- led to some dramatic, narrow victories; after a 3-7 record in one-score games in 2024, Chicago went 7-4 in games decided by seven points or fewer in 2025.

 
 In Week 4 against the Raiders , the Bears drove down the field for a touchdown to take a 25-24 lead with 1:39 to go. Their 2-point attempt fell incomplete, giving the Raiders a chance to win the game. Geno Smith drove Las Vegas into position for a 54-yard kick, but veteran kicker Daniel Carlson had his potential winning attempt blocked. 
 
 

 
 After a bye the following week, the Bears were trailing the Commanders by two points and faced a third-and-1 on their 40-yard line with 3:10 left. A first down would have allowed the Commanders to start chewing up the clock and cost the Bears their timeouts. Instead,  Jayden Daniels  fumbled an exchange with Jacory Croskey-Merritt , giving the Bears the…

title: NFL Rivalries uniforms 2026: Designs, debuts and details
summary: The second iteration of the NFL's Rivalries uniform series is unveiled with eight new teams from the AFC South and NFC North sharing their threads.
full_text:
Eight new squads unveiled their threads for the second edition of the NFL's Rivalries uniform series.

 

 The AFC South and NFC North teams will each wear special uniforms for a home game against a division rival. The Indianapolis Colts will be the first team to debut a Rivalries uniform this campaign when they face the Houston Texans in Week 3. The Chicago Bears are the last to do so in Week 16 against the Green Bay Packers . 

 Last season, teams from the AFC East and NFC West rang in the new initiative, which the league says is meant to celebrate rivalries in the NFL. Each design is created in collaboration with the team, Nike and the league. 

 The uniforms will remain in each team's rotation for three years alongside its existing alternate looks. The NFC East and AFC West squads will unveil theirs next season, and the NFC South and AFC North round out the first batch in 2028. NFC West and AFC East teams will continue to wear their designs this season.

 Here's a breakdown of each uniform design, plus the date of its on-field debut, its unique name and quotes from select teams.

 

 Chicago Bears 
 One of the oldest squads in the NFL, Chicago leans into that rich history in a modern way with a look that pays homage to founder George Halas' legacy and the team's "historic resilience." A patch honoring Halas appears on the front of the jersey, similar to what the team wore in 1983 after his death.

 The Bears' burnt orange and deep blue colorway is a classic. The vertical stripe detail on the sleeves is a reinterpretation of a staple design element, and the four stars of the city's flag are referenced on it. Chicago first wore orange pants in the 1930s, and it will return with classic-modern detailing for this design. "Monsters of the Midway" runs on the back of the neckline.

 On-field debut:  Week 16 vs. Green Bay Packers

 

 

 Detroit Lions 
 Detroit is looking forward to the future while highlighting the city's legacy as "a hub for innovation."

 The primary white uniform includes Honolulu blue scattered throughout, a key color in the Lions' palette. Of course, there are elements to the city's car and racing culture -- the sleek carbon-fiber-italicized numerals -- as well as the "Defend the Den" mentality, with a shoulder-pad pattern mimicking a lion's gaze. "Defend the Den" also appears on the back neckline.

 On-field debut: Week 8 vs. Minnesota Vikings 

 

 

 Green Bay Packers 
 The Packers have been a publicly owned, nonprofit corporation since 1923 with just over 530,000 stockholders. It creates a different bond with the fans, one that the new uniform taps into on various levels.

 The design is meant to honor the unique tradition and Vince Lombardi-era legacy in a fresh look for fans. A retro-style "GB" logo appears on the front. Green Bay's uniform includes a "vintage, desaturated green" paired with an "alabaster palette." It pays homage to the Packers' six stock sales over 107 years: 1923, 1935, 1950, 1997, 2011 and 2022. "Making history since 1919" appears on the back of the uniform neck.

 On-field debut:  Week 5 vs. Chicago Bears

 

 

 Houston Texans 
 Houston's look refreshes its H-Town identity inspired by three elements: car culture, street art and local texture.

 It's an all-white design with metallic finishes and chrome details that connect to the city's automobile scene. The blue number set is inspired by Houston's "Be Someone" bridge, which was anonymously painted in 2012 on the city's I-10 and I-45 bridge. "Houston" runs on the back of the uniform with "US" bolded in a blue, similar to the number set.

 On-field debut:  Week 11 vs. Indianapolis Colts

 

 

 Indianapolis Colts 
 Indianapolis' uniform includes classic elements of the team's typical design with twists.

 The team's signature two-stripe design is a key part of it in a dark blue on the shoulder sleeve with black accents. Anthracite, dark gray and glossy black elements run through the uniform adding "depth and intensity." Different references to the Colts' horseshoe (shoulder sleeve), ironwork and pregame anvil ritual nail home the team tradition. On the back neckline is "For the Shoe."

 On-field debut:  Week 3 vs. Houston Texans

 

 

 Jacksonville Jaguars 
 There are various inspirations for the Jaguars' design, but the most prominent is a simple one: the beach.

 Florida's coastal culture and urban influence shape the color, a clean cream that pops. What the team describes as a "historically influenced" custom Jaguars script appears across the chest. There's a distinct drop shadow around the number set plus Jaguar-print pant details. "Bold City" is on the back neckline, and the Jaguars' logo runs on the sleeve near metallic chrome accents.

 On-field debut:   Week 8 vs. Indianapolis Colts

 

 

 Minnesota Vikings 
 It's a different purple than what the team usually wears, described as a "deeper, more intimidating" one. There's an ivory palette with carved number details, and the "Vikings" above the numbers has a unique font. On the sleeve is a refined cap inspired by the Viking Knot for a neat design.

 There are also references to the Gjallarhorn, which according to Norse mythology is used to sound the arrival of the gods. It is blown before the Vikings take the field at home. Similar to the other teams, Minnesota has a message on the back of its uniform. But the Vikings' message is in the runes script.

 On-field debut:  Week 15 vs. Detroit Lions

 

 

 Tennessee Titans 
 Tennessee has a rich history of star musicians, from Dolly Parton to Elvis Presley to Justin Timberlake, among many other greats. And with the Titans playing in Nashville, it's no surprise they leaned into the "Music City" moniker for their design.

 It's a navy uniform with light blue accents around the "Music City" above the similarly colored numbers. Nashville's famous neon signage inspires the light blue number set. On the shoulder of the uniform are six darker blue strings, meant to celebrate the city's music culture. "WE" runs on the back neckline.

 On-field debut:  Week 10 vs. Jacksonville Jaguars

title: Tennessee, Peyton Manning, Dallas Cowboys lead tributes to Dolly Parton
summary: The legendary singer-songwriter from the Volunteer State died Tuesday at the age of 80.
full_text:
Dolly Parton was an icon gone too soon. On Tuesday, Parton's estate announced the superstar singer, songwriter, actress and businesswoman had died at 80. Her death was announced in a video on social media by her nephew Bryan Seaver, who was her head of security. 
 
 

 Parton had an iconic career as an entertainer for more than 60 years. She stepped on the scene in 1959 when she was 13 years old with her first single, "Puppy Love," which eventually led to a career that included the release of 49 studio albums, producing 25 No. 1 hits on Billboard's Hot Country Singles chart.

 She rose to a new peak in 1973 with the release of two of her best-known singles, "Jolene" and "I Will Always Love You," whose legacy was later carried on by Whitney Houston in her 1992 smash hit rendition of the latter.

 A notable philanthropist, Parton contributed millions of dollars toward college scholarships through the Dollywood Foundation and founded the Imagination Library, which provides free books to children.

 She also invested her royalties from "I Will Love You" into an office complex in Nashville, Tennessee.

 "It was mostly just Black families and people that lived around there. It was a whole strip mall. And I thought, 'This is the perfect place for me to be, considering it was Whitney,'" Parton said in 2021 . "I just thought: 'This was great. I'm going to be down here with her people, who are my people as well.' And so I just love the fact that I spent that money on a complex. And I think, 'This is the house that Whitney built.'"

 Outside of the music world, the Dollywood owner's presence was felt across sports, too. Parton, born in Tennessee, was a die-hard fan of teams from her home state. She consistently celebrated Volunteers wins on social media, and in 2020 was named the Tennessee Sports Hall of Fame's Tennessean of the Year.

 In 2023, the "9-to-5" star made an appearance at Neyland Stadium, where she was escorted by Peyton Manning, to perform a rendition of "Rocky Top."

 Her most recent sports appearance was Parton's unforgettable 2023 Thanksgiving halftime show during a game between the Washington Commanders and Dallas Cowboys , where she wore a Cowboys cheerleader uniform and performed "Jolene" and "9 to 5." She concluded the performance with a mashup of "We Are the Champions" and "We Will Rock You."

 Parton's presence will surely be missed in the sports world, and teams are paying their respects to the legendary artist. Here's how the sports world paid tribute to Parton.

title: Dallas Cowboys: Projecting final 53-man roster
summary: Who will back up Dak Prescott, and how will the CB corps and RB room flesh out?
full_text:
OXNARD, Calif. -- The Dallas Cowboys open the 2026 NFL regular season at the New York Giants on Sept. 13 at MetLife Stadium. But first, they play one more preseason game (Friday against the New Orleans Saints ) and then must cut their roster to 53 players by 6 p.m. ET on Sunday.

 Who will make the team? Which positions have tough decisions on deck? And where might the lineup be deepest and thinnest this season?

 Despite a productive training camp, the Cowboys have some questions about depth at cornerback, linebacker and running back. The backup quarterback job between Sam Howell and Joe Milton III remains up for grabs, too, and might push them to keep three quarterbacks.

 Here is our final projection for the 53-man roster for the Cowboys.

 

 

 Quarterbacks (3) 

 Dak Prescott ,  Sam Howell , Joe Milton III 

 Maybe in a perfect world the Cowboys would rather go with two quarterbacks, but Milton and Howell have fared well and if quarterback is the most important spot on the team, then maybe it's wise to keep three.

 

 Running backs (4) 

 Javonte Williams , Malik Davis , Jaydon Blue , Hunter Luepke 

 Davis didn't enter camp as the No. 2 running back despite his work last season, but he earned it this summer. Blue's playmaking gives him the final nod over  Phil Mafah and Israel Abinkanda , both of whom could be on the practice squad.

 

 Wide receivers (6) 

 CeeDee Lamb , George Pickens , Ryan Flournoy , KaVontae Turpin , Jonathan Mingo , Camden Brown 

 The top four have been a given. The last two have been in a state of flux. Brown, undrafted out of Georgia Southern, was able to take to the game what he did in practice. Mingo has earned his way into the mix with a solid summer performance.

 

 Tight ends (3) 

 Jake Ferguson , Brevyn Spann-Ford , Luke Schoonmaker 

 No movement in this group other than Spann-Ford being the backup to Ferguson over Schoonmaker, a 2023 second-round pick. But the Cowboys will use all three in games.

 

 Offensive linemen (9) 

 

 Tyler Guyton , Tyler Smith , Cooper Beebe , Tyler Booker , Terence Steele , T.J. Bass , Nate Thomas , Drew Shelton , Nick Leverett 

 Guyton has locked down the left tackle spot with a good camp. The depth beyond Bass is a question. Thomas looks like the swing tackle for now, but he has lacked consistency. Like a lot of teams, look for the Cowboys to be active in potentially filling their last couple of spots here.

 

 Defensive linemen (5) 

 Quinnen Williams , Kenny Clark , Otito Ogbonnia , Jonathan Bullard , LT Overton 

 This might be the deepest the Cowboys have been at defensive tackle in years. All five can play, but Bullard has been out of practice for a couple of weeks with a soft-tissue injury. Ogbonnia has been a pleasant surprise.

 

 Outside linebackers (6) 

 Rashan Gary , Donovan Ezeiruaku , Von Miller , Malachi Lawrence , Marist Liufau , James Houston 

 The arrival of Miller brought the last spot down to Liufau, Houston and Sam Williams . Liufau is the better special-teamer and has worked a lot with the first group. Houston has a knack for finding the quarterback, so he gets the edge over Williams.

 

 Inside linebackers (4) 

 DeMarvion Overshown , Dee Winters , Jaishawn Barham , Shemar James 

 Overshown won't be able to answer the durability question until he actually plays a lot, but he has seemed like a good fit in Christian Parker's scheme. Winters has come on late in camp. Barham's development was slowed a little by a groin injury, but the Cowboys have a role for him. It was tough to leave Justin Barron off the list.

 

 Cornerbacks (5) 

 DaRon Bland , Cobie Durant , Shavon Revel Jr. , veteran not on roster, Devin Moore 

 Depth is a worry beyond the top three. While Revel has had an excellent camp, he has to show he can do it in the regular season. The fourth corner might not be on the roster at the moment. Adding a veteran free agent or making a small trade for one is not out of the question.

 

 Safeties (5) 

 Jalen Thompson , Caleb Downs , Malik Hooker , P.J. Locke , Markquese Bell 

 Like defensive tackle, the Cowboys like their depth. Maybe a team needing safety help would swing a deal for Bell, but he can be a core special-teamer. Tough calls on Alijah Clark and Julius Wood .

 

 Special teams (3) 

 Brandon Aubrey  (K), Bryan Anger  (P), Trent Sieg  (LS) 

 The Cowboys believe they have one of the NFL's best trios.

title: Broncos QB Bo Nix hopes slowing down leads to improvement
summary: Nix's mobility and sack avoidance have led to success, but the Broncos think slowing him down and getting his footwork right could produce more big plays.
full_text:
ENGLEWOOD, Colo. -- The Denver Broncos believe they can do big things with their passing offense this season -- if quarterback Bo Nix can find a better rhythm from the ground up.

 Nix is coming off his second straight season with at least 25 touchdown passes, and he has brought Denver to the playoffs in both of his pro seasons -- including a 14-3 record and an AFC Championship Game trip in 2025. But coach Sean Payton and offensive coordinator Davis Webb have made it a priority to better sync Nix's footwork with the routes his receivers run on each play. And they think that could smooth out some rough spots in the quarterback's game, allowing him to reach the next level in Year 3. 

 "He's a real good foot athlete ... I think it's one of his gifts," Payton said of Nix, who spent the offseason recovering from two surgeries following a fractured right ankle in the divisional playoffs . But Payton also said there is work to be done "within the framework of each pass play, the definement of a three-[step drop], three no hitch, one big [step], five and a hitch, some of those specifics that put him exactly in time with the depth of the route."

 

 Tucked into Payton's description is the question of the pace at which Nix drops back from center or sets his feet from the shotgun to position himself to throw so it matches the cadence of his receivers' routes. The Broncos want Nix to continue to think fast, but their emphasis is getting his feet right and better timed with his progressions through his receivers' routes.

 "I think it's [about] understanding what we're doing, so we can attack defenses," Nix said.

 Despite the successful 2025 season, the Broncos found they didn't consistently challenge defenses down the field. And when they did, Nix wavered in accuracy more significantly than most of the league's top passers.

 Nix was 28th in the league in yards per attempt last season (6.4). He finished 26th in the league in completion percentage over expectation (minus-2.1 percentage points), per NFL Next Gen Stats, and was 12th in completions of 20 or more yards. Nix completed only 44.1% of his pass attempts of 10 or more air yards, along with 36.1% of attempts of 20 or more air yards.

 Some of those troublesome numbers stem from Nix being one of the NFL's quicker thinkers, which helped Denver get 12 comeback victories a year ago. But they also represent a quarterback who doesn't always have the correct timing when he sets up to throw, sometimes getting to the top of his designed dropback too quickly and making his progressions a bit too rapid.

 "He does a very good job of avoiding [a] sack -- the minus play -- and because of that he's very good with his progression." Payton said. "He's not someone who's slow to progress and slow to process, it's the other way ... but I'd rather deal with that than a slow processor who's getting sacked."

 Chase Daniel, who spent five seasons as the  New Orleans Saints ' backup quarterback when Payton coached there, has studied Nix's play extensively, occasionally attending Broncos quarterback meetings over Nix's first two seasons. He sees what Payton described and said it will require Nix to realize that not all dropbacks are created equal in Payton's playbook.

 

 "Sean's offense is very much timing and rhythm," said Daniel, who now works with ESPN as an analyst. "So, there could be three different five-step drops, for example -- a slow-rhythmic one, a normal one and a really quick one. And [Nix], from what I saw, he hadn't mastered that in terms of timing with the play because there's different routes.

 "At times, Bo sped up his feet so he's already at the top of his drop and no receiver is out of his break, so ... he started to get to the checkdown too quick. 
 
"I don't think that's not him seeing it, I think it's the footwork didn't match up with the routes," he added.

 In those situations, Nix is faced with either trying to squeeze a pass to a receiver who hasn't arrived at the point in the route where the play was designed or just moving to the next progression. And a quarterback who has been drilled not to put the ball in harm's way -- like Nix -- will likely go to the next read.

 This causes a chain effect in which Nix gets to each progression prematurely, forcing him to arrive at his checkdown options or move out of the pocket before it's necessary. As a result, 395 of Nix's league-leading 612 attempts (64.5%) were within 10 yards of the line of scrimmage, with 121 (19.7%) thrown behind the line. Compare that with MVP Matthew Stafford , who threw 59 of his 597 attempts behind the line of scrimmage last season.

 Payton believes that Nix's footwork mechanics are sound and that he has the necessary decision-making ability. Nix's next step is to find the pacing and rhythm of each play yet still know when to use his mobility.

 It was part of an extensive offseason review of Nix and the offense by the coaching staff. And Webb said Nix has shown progress in training camp.

 "It's noticeable the strides he's taken, hanging on [the first read], getting to two, to three, then using his legs," Webb said.

 Webb has also said the Broncos have to be cognizant of how they "marry'' Nix's first reads to the second and third reads, and to how Webb is sequencing playcalls.

 Payton has been steadfast that Nix has the arm strength to punish defenses down the field if everything else is right. The arrival of wide receiver Jaylen Waddle -- who Nix called an "explosive playmaker" -- changes the dynamic, and Courtland Sutton said he has already seen the effects of the work his QB has put in.

 

 "He's in this spot where he's understanding the game at such a different level," Sutton said. 
 
"He's seen what defenses do, seeing what leverages are getting thrown at him ... and [the big plays] are in there, we've seen them out here more already, and our defense is hard to get."

 Nix said he believes it's all linked to simply understanding the position and the team's playbook.

 "When you have a second-nature thought process and you know the play and you're not thinking about operation, or emotion or a route concept or a handoff point, you can attack the defense in a little bit more of a strategic way," Nix said. "So my eyes are up a little bit more. I just feel comfortable.

 "I'm excited about the growth and know that there's plenty left, but also I feel strongly where I'm at."

title: How Colts' Anthony Richardson is fighting back from adversity
summary: He was benched, injured and asked to be traded, but Richardson remains in Indy, and he's persevering.
full_text:
INDIANAPOLIS -- The last meaningful NFL snaps Indianapolis Colts quarterback Anthony Richardson Sr . played came in Week 16 of the 2024 season.

 And the 19 months since that Dec. 22 win over the Tennessee Titans have felt like a lifetime.

 First, severe back spasms kept Richardson out of the final two games of the 2024 season. The next spring, the Colts signed Richardson's eventual replacement, Daniel Jones , who recently signed an $88 million contract extension to remain the team's quarterback.

 Richardson also sustained a scary eye injury in a freak pregame accident last October, leaving his vision temporarily impaired and sidelining him for the rest of the season. And, most recently, Richardson -- sensing his time in Indianapolis was nearing its end -- requested a trade from the Colts after a February meeting with the club.

 The series of setbacks and sideshows seemed to never stop. Maybe that's why Richardson was so enthusiastic about his opportunities to play in the preseason the past two weeks, something that might once have appeared trivial for a former No. 4 draft pick.

 "Just getting back out there after sitting down for a while with the eye injury, going to see a lot of different doctors, getting back in the groove of practice, putting pads back on, just being back out there on the field and just doing it," he said, the noticeable scar under his eye providing an ever-present reminder. "I definitely needed that."

 Others also have sensed it.

 "He's had real joy, at least I've seen," offensive coordinator Jim Bob Cooter said. "Going out and playing ball, playing real football. And it is really beneficial for him."

 Richardson's career is still somewhat in a state of limbo and many questions remain. Most immediate is whether Richardson or second-year player Riley Leonard will be the team's primary backup behind Jones this season.

 It was long thought that Richardson might wind up elsewhere given the team's growing affinity for Leonard and the decision to move on from Richardson as a starter. But Richardson has arguably outplayed Leonard in exhibition games, with Richardson completing 60.9% of his attempts over Leonard's 48.6%. Richardson has also run nine times for 68 yards and a touchdown.

 

 Given Jones' injury history, it's beginning to look as if Richardson might have a role for the Colts even after all that has happened -- including his infamous tapout of a 2024 game , his injuries and his past struggles.

 "I'm just looking forward to helping the team," Richardson said. "They truly believe that I still have a chance to be on this squad, and I love that.

 "I just want to be able to contribute."

 That, it seems, was a reference by Richardson to recent statements made by team officials such as general manager Chris Ballard and assistant general manager Ed Dodds, throwing water on the idea of trading Richardson and strongly suggesting he will remain a key part of the roster.

 It might not be the situation Richardson envisioned when he was drafted with the intention of becoming the team's franchise quarterback. But it's a long way from where he was late last year after a bar holding a thick elastic stretching band popped, with the bar hitting him in the face and breaking his orbital bone. Richardson spent weeks at home just waiting for the substantial swelling to subside.

 Everything that has happened has brought important perspective. So, Richardson said he has decided to live in the moment.

 

 "Regardless of what's happened in my life, I always dreamed about being in the NFL," he said. "I never knew how my career was going to go. There's been adversity, but I feel like that's what helps people grow. I've been going through a lot of adversity, but that just keeps me pushing forward. I just keep my faith and just work and keep my head down."

 Richardson is entering his fourth season, but he's still only 24, making him just a few months older than Leonard. For that reason, Richardson says he believes he can still have the career he expected.

 "I'm looking to be the best one day," he said.

 But, for now, Richardson gets to play football again. It has helped renew his passion for the game.

 "I love football," he said. "Football has done so much for my family. It's brought me here, the best of the best, the NFL. I still love football regardless of what's going on.

 "As long as I get to go out there, grab a football, put my pads on, and run around, I thank God for it and I'm excited for it."

title: 2026 New England Patriots training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our daily updates from Patriots training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Patriots reporter Mike Reiss has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Patriots camp. Will Drake Maye  start another MVP-like campaign in Year 3? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Patriots camp 
 
 Gonzalez focused on season, but irked by talks with Patriots 
 Patriots trade Kayshon Boutte to Texans for Jaylen Reed, pick 
 Patriots' Will Campbell leaning into offseason advice from top linemen 
 Vrabel says starters sitting in order to develop depth 
 Patriots TE Hunter Henry signs extension worth up to $20M 
 Has Patriots CB Christian Gonzalez found his voice? 
 Patriots' Brown knows Vrabel's rip comes from 'great place' 
 Kraft: Patriots' Gonzalez has offer to be 'highest-paid' CB ever 
 
 

 Tuesday, Aug. 25 
 Cornerback Marcus Jones was presented the Ron Burton Community Service Award during the Patriots' annual charitable gala inside Gillette Stadium, with owner Robert Kraft introducing him by saying his actions represent "the very best of our family's feeling of what it means to be a New England Patriot."

 Jones accepted the award, which Kraft calls the highest individual award a player can win as it recognizes outstanding commitment in giving back to the community, shortly after 9 p.m. ET. He turned to humor in his initial remarks.

 "You got up me up here with no haircut," he cracked, adding that his mother, Viola, would let him hear about that.

 As Jones spoke, he was joined on the stage by the Burton family and past recipients of the award in attendance, which included teammates Brenden Schooler and Hunter Henry , as well as former center David Andrews.

 Jones spoke of how his passion for producing music is part of his identity.

 "I'm a creative person, I love music so much, and [football] gives us a platform to let younger people know that if there's things they want to do in a creative role, they can do it," he said, adding that being part of Special Olympics this offseason in Minnesota was also meaningful to him.

 Jones, who is from Enterprise, Alabama, played at the University of Houston and joined the Patriots as a third-round draft pick in 2022, shared with the crowd of 1,000-plus that he's become an adopted New Englander.

 "Being drafted here was a dream come true. I wasn't crazy about the cold, but now I'm loving that part," he said.

 

 More observations: 

 
 The team held an afternoon practice, which was its 22nd and final session of training camp. Newly-acquired safety Jaylen Reed , wearing No. 26, joined his teammates for the early parts of the practice, but went to the fieldhouse more individual work once team drills began. 
 RB TreVeyon Henderson , who had slipped during Monday's practice and had his right ankle/foot examined by the athletic training staff, did not practice. But Henderson was walking Tuesday with no noticeable limp. 
 Kicker Andy Borregales was 6-of-6 kicking at the skinny goal posts, with his final attempt right down the middle from 54 yards. That was also notable because it was his first practice with new holder Matt Haack . 
 Starting safety Craig Woodson has been out of practice since last Thursday, so Dell Pettus stepped into his spot alongside  Kevin Byard . 
 Veteran Greg Van Roten worked at both guard spots and center as the top interior backup. 
 WR Pop Douglas had one of the catches of the day, reaching his right hand up to corral a crossing route, while WR Efton Chism III had a diving grab and long TD. 
 Byard and CB Kindle Vildor registered interceptions of backup QB Tommy DeVito . 
 

 

 
 
 
 Monday, Aug. 24 
 Cornerback Christian Gonzalez , who had been sidelined since landing hard at the end of practice Aug. 10, returned to the field Monday and his presence was noted by teammates.

 Gonzalez's agent remains engaged in contract extension negotiations with the team.

 "He's a ballplayer, first and foremost. He loves football. He loves being around the team. He loves lining up and playing against the best," linebacker Christian Elliss said. "It doesn't matter what he has going on, he's going to line up and play and he locks people down."

 Gonzalez was a full participant in his return to practice.

 "It's always special to have one of the better corners in this league, and have him out there with us. Obviously as we start to ramp up getting into the season, for him to be able to go out there and start practice fully, it was pretty cool," starting safety  Kevin Byard  said.

 Earlier in the day, coach Mike Vrabel was asked about the status of contract talks with Gonzalez.

 "We're working hard to try to get him; we want him [to be] a part of our team for as long as certainly I'm here, for as long as he can possibly here," he said on sports radio WEEI.

 

 More observations: 

 
 RB TreVeyon Henderson slipped while making a cut, had his right ankle/foot area looked at, and left practice about midway through. The team practiced on its lower field and multiple players noted the slippery natural-grass surface when asked by reporters. 
 Safety John Saunders Jr . stepped in front of a Tommy DeVito sideline pass for an interception, which was his team-leading fifth of training camp. 
 RB Rhamondre Stevenson had a beautiful touchdown catch in the end zone from QB Drake Maye , beating LB Robert Spillane on a longer-developing pass route from the high red zone. 
 After punter Bryce Baringer sustained an undisclosed injury in Saturday's preseason game, the team signed veteran Matt Haack , who showed up midway through practice and donned No. 19. 
 Patriots signed former Boston College OL Jack Conley , who spent time with the team in 2025. He wore No. 67 and practiced at right guard with the third unit. 
 

 

 

 Thursday, Aug. 20 
 Quarterback Drake Maye has said that wide receiver A.J. Brown is "open even when he's covered," and Thursday's practice with the Eagles highlighted the fine line Maye walks with that thought.

 Maye was intercepted twice when targeting Brown, the first of which came in front of the right pylon in red zone work as cornerback Riq Woolen stepped in front of the pass and returned it for a would-be pick-six.

 "I was just late with the football. You can't be late in the red zone," Maye explained. "It's tight, and it's a concept that we probably need to get some more work on and just find some timing."

 The second pick came closer to midfield, with Maye firing a pass to Brown on an in-breaking route. It was unclear in real-time if Brown caught the ball and had it jarred loose from his grasp by Woolen, or if the ball simply popped up in the air. Nonetheless, outside linebacker Jalyx Hunt showed impressive awareness and quickness to dive and haul it in.

 Overall, Maye was pleased with the two days of practices with the Eagles. The teams play Saturday night but it's possible Maye won't see any action based on the extensive reps he received in practice.

 "I think we had a lot of great work," he said. "You got to string some plays together in a row, and I felt like we did that more [Wednesday] than we did today."

 More observations: 

 
 CB Marcus Jones had two interceptions. That gave the Patriots a total of seven INTs over the two days of practice with the Eagles. 
 With starting right tackle Morgan Moses having his reps managed, first-round pick Caleb Lomu elevated to the top unit in his place. 
 In one-on-one red zone work, Brown had what looked like a highlight-reel catch in the back left corner of the end zone on CB Quinyon Mitchell , but…

title: Ann Michael Maye grants Patriots fan's baking Make-a-Wish
summary: Ann Michael granted a Make-A-Wish on Friday at Gillette Stadium for Skylar, a 16-year-old from Massachusetts diagnosed with a brain tumor.
full_text:
FOXBOROUGH, Mass. -- New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye has said often how much pride he has taken in watching his wife, Ann Michael, go viral on social media with her popular Bakemas theme.

 In a poignant reminder of her impact, Ann Michael granted a Make-A-Wish on Friday at Gillette Stadium for Skylar, a 16-year-old from Massachusetts diagnosed with a brain tumor.

 

 "When the idea was brought to me, I was in shock someone would choose that," Ann Michael said. "It's such an honor."

 The two baked gluten-free chocolate chip cookies together. Ann Michael presented Skylar a custom Patriots jersey and then surprised her with tickets and sideline passes to the team's preseason game against the Philadelphia Eagles the following night.

 Drake Maye met Skylar on the field before the game and autographed the jersey that Skylar wore.

 

 In a story posted to the Patriots' official website , Skylar said: "I've always loved to cook and bake, and I've always loved the Patriots. I knew Ann Michael as someone who liked baking and cooking, too, especially during her Bakemas era. I thought it was so cool. Choosing to bake with her was the wish I knew I wanted to do."

 As they baked, Ann Michael shared one of her tips.

 "There can never be too may chocolate chips," she said.

 Drake Maye has shared that his favorite recipe in Bakemas was peppermint chocolate chip cookies. In January, he said of Ann Michael: "It's been awesome to follow her journey. She's just being herself, and that's the best thing about her, and that's what I love her for."

title: 2026 New York Giants training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our updates from Giants training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Giants reporter Jordan Raanan has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Giants camp. How will the Giants handle increased expectations and a new coach? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, including the Giants' top camp performer and biggest lingering question.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Giants camp 
 
 New York Giants WR Calvin Austin carted off practice field 
 Players pulled from fight-filled Giants-Dolphins practice 
 Giants trade Daniel Faalele to Jaguars for 6th-round draft pick 
 Giants' Malik Nabers 'felt good' in 1st full-speed live drills 
 Giants QB Jaxson Dart 'puzzled' by latest concussion test request 
 A Harbaugh team meeting during training camp -- an inside look 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 25 

 The afternoon began for Odell Beckham Jr.  with one of his patented one-handed catches. It concluded with four receptions in live drills to complete one of his best practice performances of the summer.

 It comes at just the right time, with final cuts looming Sunday. Beckham has been presumed to be on the roster bubble after running mostly with the second team this summer. He also dropped a potential touchdown in Saturday's preseason game. But the injury to fellow wide receiver  Calvin Austin III could ultimately open the door for Beckham.

 "I know he's superfrustrated about that drop he had in the game the other day. We all know nine out of 10 times he's going to catch that," offensive coordinator Matt Nagy said of Beckham. "But I like where he's at."

 It wasn't just Beckham who had a strong practice Tuesday. Wideout  Darnell Mooney made a handful of big plays, including catching a deep touchdown from Jaxson Dart behind the defense.

 Other observations: 

 
 Coach John Harbaugh said over the weekend it's "an ongoing pecking order" at running back. The Giants listed Cam Skattebo as the starter on their weekly unofficial depth chart, with Tyrone Tracy Jr.  or Najee Harris or Devin Singletary next on an equal line. 
 TE Theo Johnson missed practice one day after colliding with outside linebacker Kayvon Thibodeaux . 
 G Francis Mauigoa (stinger) and RT Jermaine Eluemunor took part in individual drills after sitting out Monday. 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 24 

 John Harbaugh huddled a group of veterans after practice. They went over schedules, practice details and other team-related items.

 This is how Harbaugh operates. He assembles a leadership group and consults with them on decisions.

 For the Giants, that consists of quarterback Jaxson Dart , left tackle Andrew Thomas , outside linebacker Brian Burns , middle linebacker Tremaine Edmunds , safety Jevon Holland , punter Jordan Stout , backup quarterback Jameis Winston and tight end Chris Manhertz . They were voted as leaders by their teammates.

 "We've been doing it for a long time. It's good," Harbaugh said of the leadership group. "I do kind of try to emphasize to the team that everybody's a leader and everybody has every opportunity to speak their mind. Talk to anybody.

 "But sometimes, it just kind of helps because guys don't always want to do that."

 They talk about everything. Harbaugh went on to say the Giants players asked Monday for a pool table in the locker room. He told them if they won enough games, they might even get a golf simulator.

 Other observations: 

 
 The Giants ran only a couple of periods of full-speed live drills. TE Isaiah Likely remains Dart's favorite target. The team keeps finding different ways to use WR Calvin Austin III ; the former Steelers wideout is going to have a significant role in this offense. 
 Tight end Theo Johnson left practice after a collision with Kayvon Thibodeaux . Harbaugh initially didn't think it was serious. 
 The Giants' offensive line was without RT Jermaine Eluemunor , G Francis Mauigoa (stinger) and G/OT Joshua Ezeudu (leg) at Monday's practice. All three should be back soon, possibly as early as Tuesday, when the Giants will be in full pads. 
 WR Jalin Hyatt (knee), TE Tanner Connor and DT Shelby Harris also didn't practice. 
 

 
 Thursday, Aug. 20 
 MIAMI GARDENS, Fla. -- This was the kind of practice you wanted to see from the Giants' offense -- and from quarterback Jaxson Dart .

 Dart had perhaps his best performances of the summer, going 17-of-23 passing in a joint practice against the Miami Dolphins that included several deep and intermediate gains. Six went to his favorite target, tight end Isaiah Likely .

 "I felt like I played clean," Dart said.

 This was an important day for Dart and the Giants' offense, which has been up and down most of the summer while learning a new system. They hadn't been able to hit many plays downfield.

 This was sort of a validation that this new offense can work.

 "We had a number of chunk gains off play-action, which was good to see," Giants coach John Harbaugh said. "It's one thing in theory, it's another thing in practice. You want to see it work. At the end of the day, did the play work? It could be a great play, but if it doesn't work, then there's a lot of things that go into making it work, including executing it well, then it's not a good play. I agree [it's validating]."

 

 More observations: 

 
 The Giants' offense probably wasn't even the team's best unit in the joint practice against the Dolphins. Outside linebacker Brian Burns said the defense was "dominant." When asked by a reporter if they had six sacks, Burns said no. In his estimation, they got to Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis even more than that. 
 How about this for a quick integration? Running back Najee Harris participated in live drills after just three days with the team. He even got a couple carries, including one on the goal line where he made an impressive cut and reached the end zone. Harris looked good for a player that supposedly wasn't going to be in football shape for a "couple weeks." 
 Another perfect practice for undrafted rookie kicker Dominic Zvada , who went 6-for-6, including one to end practice after the Giants drove the field on a two-minute drill. 
 Rookie guard Francis Mauigoa left practice with what Harbaugh called a "stinger." He didn't expect it to be serious. Josh Ezeudu was next in line at guard. 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 18 

 Malik Nabers participated in full live-speed team drills for the second straight day in a red jersey. And he looked even better than he did on Monday.

 Nabers saw a slightly increased workload. He ran eight routes and caught four passes from quarterback Jaxson Dart in 11-on-11 and 7-on-7 drills. Of course, it helped that the defense couldn't touch him.

 On one deep pass, safeties Jevon Holland and Tyler Nubin had to pull up on the play to avoid any contact.

 Coach John Harbaugh said that Nabers "handled it well" bouncing back after his first day of live drills. The next step is adding reps, getting bumped around, shedding the red jersey and feeling contact. That could come as early as next week.

 In the meantime, Nabers' workload will be light during Thursday's joint practice with the Dolphins. Barring a setback, the expectation seems to be that Nabers will be ready for Week 1 against the Dallas Cowboys .

 

 More observations: 

 
 Running back Tyrone Tracy Jr . was first up at running back on Tuesday. He's still squarely in the Giants plans even with the signing of Najee Harris . Tracy and Cam Skattebo have both been the first running back up throughout training camp. 
 Harbaugh seemed to indicate he expects it to take a "couple weeks" before Harris gets into football shape. The veteran running back did only…

title: 2026 New York Jets training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our updates from Jets training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Jets reporter Rich Cimini has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Jets camp. Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football, and which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, concluding with the Jets' top camp performer and biggest lingering question as preseason games begin.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Jets camp 
 
 RB Breece Hall strains groin, Glenn says its not serious 
 Jets CB Stiggers taken to hospital after collapsing at practice 
 No. 2 pick Bailey living up to hype, bringing 'juice' to Jets 
 Rookie TE Kenyon Sadiq to miss time after hernia setback 
 Jets' Smith rues being 'distraction' after dispute with girlfriend 
 2026 Jets training camp preview 
 
 

 Thursday, Aug. 25 

 Rookie TE Kenyon Sadiq , expected to bring a big-play dimension to the offense, will have a reduced role at the outset of the season as he works his way back from injury.

 "There's no doubt we'll have to scale back," offensive coordinator Frank Reich said. "We have to work him in slowly. We can't rush it, as much as we'd like to. The good thing is he's very smart ... and he'll be as ready as you can be, but there's nothing like practice."

 Sadiq hasn't practiced much. The first-round pick from Oregon missed OTAs because of hernia surgery and returned for the first three practices of training camp before a setback put him on the shelf again. He missed the final 12 practices of training camp, which concluded Tuesday.

 The Jets still have about six practices before they open the season against the Tennessee Titans .

 Other observations: 

 
 The not-so-heated kicking battle between Jason Sanders and Cade York came to a conclusion -- one day after a practice in which they combined for several misses. The Jets waived York, with special teams coordinator Chris Banjo announcing, "[Sanders] has won the job. Yes, sir." 
 In the preseason games, Sanders was 2-for-2, with a long of 47. York was 2-for-3, with a long of 38 and a miss from 59. Sanders was a solid kicker for the Miami Dolphins (2018-2024), but he missed last season because of a hip injury and was released by the New York Giants before training camp. 
 Coach Aaron Glenn ended camp with one of the longer practices of the summer, much of it a live "move-the-ball" period with offense versus defense. QB Geno Smith finished on a high note, completing 15 of 18 passes. He spread the ball around evenly to Garrett Wilson , Adonai Mitchell and rookie Omar Cooper Jr ., who came on strong toward the end of camp. 
 The roster must be pared to 53 by 6 p.m. on Sunday, and one of the areas to watch is the offensive line (depth), as the second-team line allowed several sacks. It wouldn't be a surprise if GM Darren Mougey looks to the waiver wire for veteran help. Starting LG Dylan Parham sat out the last two series for an undisclosed reason. 
 Reich said rookie QB Cade Klubnik is "extremely poised," noting there was a play against the Steelers in which he got to his third read while backed up in the end zone. "He did it like he's been doing it for years," Reich said. "That was probably for him my favorite play. He's made good progress." Klubnik is the odds-on favorite to be the No. 2 QB. 
 Reich has been calling plays on game day from the coaches' booth -- a career first for him. He said he likes the vantage point and will continue to call plays from upstairs. 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 19 

 Upset that Cade Klubnik played only two series last week in the preseason opener? Want to see the rookie quarterback in a longer stint?

 Well, you probably will get your wish this week, and don't be surprised if he starts again. The Jets face the Pittsburgh Steelers on Friday night at Acrisure Stadium.

 With Geno Smith still dealing with an ankle injury -- it was heavily taped for practice -- coach Aaron Glenn remained noncommittal on his QB choice. Out of caution, he could sit Smith for the second straight game even though he hasn't missed a full practice.

 "I've never been a coach that was afraid of injuries because it's part of the game, but I also want to be a coach that's smart and make sure I get our guys ready for Week 1," Glenn said.

 Klubnik, who led the offense to 10 points in his two-series debut, appears to be in line for a bigger role this week.

 Rebounding from an uneven practice Tuesday, the former Clemson star was sharp, especially during the red zone period. He went 3-for-3, with passes to Garrett Wilson , Jelani Woods (TD) and Kene Nwangwu (TD). In previous practices, he had experienced some hiccups in the red area.

 "I think every time he practices, he's getting better and better and better," said Glenn, adding that Klubnik has the aptitude to learn from his mistakes.

 Barring something unforeseen, Klubnik appears to have locked up the No. 2 job.

 Other observations: 

 
 The defense controlled the early part of an abbreviated practice. DE  Will McDonald IV  (sack), DT Jowon Briggs (tackle for loss) and S Dane Belton (pass breakup) made splash plays while the entire unit stymied Smith (0-for-3) and the passing attack. 
 The kicking competition between Jason Sanders and Cade York is difficult to call, but it's clear that York has the stronger leg. 
 The defense is putting an emphasis on takeaways. Makes sense, considering the ignominy of 2025 -- first team in history to go an entire season without intercepting a pass. The goal is three picks a day in practice, according to nickelback Jarvis Brownlee Jr ., who said the defense faces "consequences" if it comes up short. The consequences are post-practice gassers. 
 Good news: CB Qwan'tez Stiggers , who was diagnosed with a concussion last week after passing out on the sideline, returned to practice on a limited basis (red concussion jersey). 
 An extreme example of load management -- backup MLB Kiko Mauigoa received a veterans' rest day. Mind you, he's a second-year player, only 23 years old. Explaining the decision, Glenn noted that Mauigoa had logged more practice reps in camp than perhaps any player on defense. 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 18 

 Quarterback Geno Smith , learning a new system, said it's "very important" for him to play in the preseason. But he wouldn't take it further, saying the decision belongs to coach Aaron Glenn.

 Smith is dealing with a sore left ankle. He hasn't missed any practice time, but he was scratched from the preseason opener last Friday. On Tuesday, Glenn was noncommittal on whether Smith would play Friday night against the Pittsburgh Steelers .

 Every other offensive starter played last week. Ideally, Smith would get a couple of series against the Steelers for the sake of timing and chemistry.

 Smith is accustomed to playing in the preseason. He played 28 snaps last summer for the Las Vegas Raiders . In his final two preseasons with the Seattle Seahawks , 2023 and 2024, he played a combined total of only 17 snaps.

 "I'll leave it up to coach, but my job is to get ready and help this team get ready to be ready to play Week 1," Smith said. "Whenever I get the chance to play, I look forward to it. I'll also leave that up to coach."

 Smith, commenting for the first time on his ankle injury, was tightlipped. He wouldn't say how it happened, except to say, "I just had some swelling, swelling in my ankle." It developed during last week's joint practices with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers .

 For what it's worth, the sleeve on his lower left leg was gone for practice.

 Other observations:  

 
 Rookie QB Cade Klubnik threw a couple of interceptions in practice, one on a pass that was tipped by Will McDonald IV and picked off by Azareye'h Thomas and…

title: Did Aaron Glenn, Geno Smith change? 10 notes from Jets camp
summary: As New York heads toward the regular season, we look back at training camp, including the high-end promise of rookie linebacker David Bailey﻿.
full_text:
FLORHAM PARK, N.J. -- The New York Jets were 0-2, on their way to 0-7 and eventually 3-14, when Aaron Glenn delivered a line that still resonates. "Big ships turn slow," the coach said last September.

 Translation: Don't expect an overnight miracle after more than a decade of losing and dysfunction.

 Glenn inherited a team that seemed lost at sea -- a league-low .311 winning percentage from 2016 to 2024 -- but now he's had more than a year to implement his program, and there's no reason why it shouldn't look better in 2026.

 "We're still turning that ship -- we're still turning it -- but I like exactly where we are," Glenn said last week.

 Training camp ends Tuesday, the preseason culminates Friday against the New York Giants  (7:30 p.m. ET) and soon Season 2 of the Glenn era will be underway.

 Here's a look at 10 things we learned in training camp:

 

 1. Glenn has changed 

 He seems more at ease than last year, not as edgy. Maybe it's because he's back in his comfort zone, calling the defense -- his "super power," as he noted in the offseason. Maybe it's because his revamped coaching staff is more experienced than last year, particularly with offensive coordinator Frank Reich on board -- a departure from first-timer Tanner Engstrand.

 Maybe it's simply his natural evolution as a head coach. It's probably all of the above.

 Glenn said his rookie year taught him the importance of being able to "pivot" -- changing on the fly if something (or someone) isn't working.

 

 2. Speaking of a pivot ... 

 Subscribing to load management, Glenn dialed back training camp in the interest of preserving players for the regular season. An extreme example: Linebacker Kiko Mauigoa received a veterans' rest day because his practice rep count was soaring, according to Glenn. Mind you, Mauigoa is only 23 years old. Typically, the rest days are reserved for the guys in the 30-and-older club.

 Glenn, who last year made such a big deal out of having live tackling in practice, eliminated the drills from this year's script while claiming, "I want to be the best tackling team in the NFL." He believes "thud" tackling (hitting and wrapping up but not going to the ground) promotes better technique.

 In his soul, Glenn is an old-school coach, but he is embracing new-school concepts such as sports science and artificial intelligence.

 

 

 3. Geno Smith hasn't changed 

 At 35, Smith still throws a gorgeous ball -- his upper-body mechanics are pristine, Reich said -- but he's still prone to interceptions, based on what he showed in camp. He threw a league-high 17 interceptions last season for the Las Vegas Raiders , and it'll be up to Reich and quarterbacks coach Bill Musgrave to coach that out of him. He was sharp in his preseason debut Friday night against the Steelers, illustrating how good he can be when he's on.

 In practice, Smith displayed a penchant for pushing the ball downfield, a tendency that played well with his receivers. They loved his aggressiveness, his willingness to take chances.

 

 4. The organization believes in Cade Klubnik  -- more than we thought 

 You knew there was an affinity for the former Clemson star when they traded up 18 spots to draft him in the fourth round, but they doubled down by not bringing in a seasoned quarterback for the No. 2 job. They made it Klubnik's job to lose ... and he hasn't. Not in emphatic fashion, though.

 Klubnik was up and down in camp, and his performance against the Steelers wasn't as crisp as the previous week, but the organization apparently has seen enough maturity and intelligence to make him the backup.

 "He's kind of got a little bit of a swagger to him," guard Joe Tippmann said.

 The decision to go with a middle-round rookie for such an important job carries a lot of risk, especially for a head coach who needs to win games in a potential make-or-break season.

 

 

 5. David Bailey will be the Jets' most compelling defensive rookie since Sauce Gardner (2022) 

 You can't take your eyes off him when he lines up on the edge, usually over the right tackle, because his speed creates possibilities.

 "I see him in the backfield all the time, my gosh," defensive tackle Harrison Phillips said.

 The No. 2 draft pick still is polishing his craft, but the raw tools -- notably, an elite get-off -- were evident on most days in camp. So was his confidence. During a joint practice with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , he did some trash talking, telling veteran tackle Luke Goedeke that he was eager to beat him in a one-on-one drill. And he did, sparking a melee. Against the Steelers, he used a power rush to beat veteran tackle Broderick Jones for a sack.

 

 6. Beyond Bailey, the most impactful rookie was -- surprise! 

 It wasn't a great camp for the draft class, as tight end Kenyon Sadiq , cornerback D'Angelo Ponds and safety VJ Payne missed significant time because of injuries. Wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr . was OK, nothing spectacular.

 The unsung standout was fourth-round defensive lineman Darrell Jackson Jr ., a 6-foot-5, 315-pounder with knock-back ability and surprisingly quick feet. With T'Vondre Sweat nursing a hamstring for the first three weeks, Jackson capitalized on his extra reps. Because he can play multiple spots, including 5-technique end, he could crack the early-season rotation.

 

 7. Minkah Fitzpatrick will be everywhere 

 On the first play of the first preseason game, the former All-Pro safety set up on the line of scrimmage and blitzed from the front side. Get used to it. The plan is to deploy Fitzpatrick in a Kyle Hamilton -like role, which means multiple positions.

 

 Publicly and privately, Fitzpatrick has expressed a desire to be a chess piece in Glenn's defense. He doesn't want to be a traditional safety. His wish will be granted.

 

 8. The competition fell short 

 One of the objectives in camp was to increase the competition on both sides of the ball, but it didn't materialize, in part, because of injuries. Cornerback got hit the hardest, as Ponds and Nahshon Wright missed time. The only true positional battle is safety ( Andre Cisco versus Dane Belton ), along with kicker ( Jason Sanders versus Cade York ).

 

 9. Glenn's defense will be aggressive 

 He outlined a four-point plan for his defense: Disrupt the quarterback. Disrupt the receivers. Attack the ball. Limit explosive plays.

 In other words, look for pressure schemes and a lot of man-to-man coverage. When he called plays for the Detroit Lions , his "man" percentage in 2024 was the highest in the league, per NFL Next Gen Stats. His blitz rate was No. 2.

 

 10. And, finally: Most Improved Player 

 It is wide receiver Isaiah Williams . Can the team MVP be the most improved? In this case, yes, because he was voted the MVP last season by his teammates because of his success as a kick returner. This summer, he made his impact as a receiver, improving in all areas and impressing with his leadership.

 Receivers coach Shawn Jefferson said Williams is so reliable that, "If I was in a burning building -- Jefferson pretended to dial a phone -- 'Hey, you need to come get me.' And he's on the way.

 "Just to put it bluntly, he's a heartbeat on offense."

title: 2026 Pittsburgh Steelers: Projecting final 53-man roster
summary: The toughest decision facing Pittsburgh comes behind QB Aaron Rodgers and the deliberation between keeping two or three backups.
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Steelers open the 2026 NFL regular season against the Atlanta Falcons on Sept. 13 ( 1 p.m. ET, Fox ) at Acrisure Stadium. But first they play one more preseason game Thursday at the Buffalo Bills  ( 7 p.m. ET, NFL Network ) and then must cut their roster to 53 players by 6 p.m. ET on Sunday.

 Who will make the team? Which positions have tough decisions on deck? And where might the lineup be deepest and thinnest this season?

 The toughest decision facing the Steelers comes behind Aaron Rodgers and the deliberation between keeping two or three backup quarterbacks. Will Howard and Drew Allar are young and unproven, but their preseason performances show they're progressing well under coach Mike McCarthy and could handle filling in for Rodgers in case of emergency. Beyond quarterback, the depth on the defensive line made that position a difficult one to reduce.

 Here is our projection for the 53-man roster for the Steelers.

 

 Quarterbacks (4) 
 

 Aaron Rodgers , Mason Rudolph ,  Will Howard , Drew Allar 

 McCarthy has never had four quarterbacks on his Week 1 roster, but that changes this season. While keeping four signal-callers takes away another roster spot, the decision is necessary because the gulf between Rudolph and the pair of young quarterbacks is sizable.

 That much was noticeable in the second preseason game when Howard threw a pair of interceptions and couldn't replicate the success he had in his first outing. Allar's arm talent is evident, but he is still too green to be a legitimate safety net for a 42-year-old quarterback. Keeping Rudolph along with Allar and Howard gives the Steelers an insurance policy for Rodgers and McCarthy more time to evaluate and develop potential future options.

 
 Running backs (3) 
 Jaylen Warren , Rico Dowdle , Travis Homer 

 Lew Nichols turned heads in training camp, but ultimately, Homer's special teams prowess gives him the edge over the undrafted free agent. Nichols, though, is a good practice squad candidate. Kaleb Johnson , a 2025 third-round pick, was buried in the running back rotation throughout training camp and struggled to stand out in a crowded backfield.

 
 Wide receivers (6) 
 DK Metcalf , Michael Pittman Jr ., Germie Bernard , Roman Wilson , Ben Skowronek , Kaden Wetjen 

 No change here from the pre-training camp prediction. This group has been solidified throughout camp.

 
 Tight ends (3) 
 Pat Freiermuth , Darnell Washington , Robert Tonyan 

 Tonyan emerged as Howard's go-to target in the first preseason game, and he's a savvy veteran with a good rapport with Rodgers from their Green Bay days. He rounds out a solid tight end group.

 
 Fullbacks (1) 
 Riley Nowakowski 

 The rookie is a true fullback, something the Steelers haven't had since Roosevelt Nix in 2019.

 

 

 Offensive linemen (9) 

 Troy Fautanu , Zach Frazier , Mason McCormick , Spencer Anderson , Dylan Cook , Max Iheanachor , Gennings Dunker , Brock Hoffman , Broderick Jones 

 Jones' health to start training camp was a pleasant surprise after a long recovery from season-ending neck surgery . He still hasn't regained his strength or technique, but Iheanachor's early camp injury means that the Steelers need as much veteran depth as they can get at tackle.

 
 Defensive linemen (6) 
 Cameron Heyward , Keeanu Benton , Derrick Harmon , Yahya Black , Sebastian Joseph-Day , Gabriel Rubio 

 One of the biggest surprises of training camp is sixth-round rookie Rubio, who even missed the last six games of his final season at Notre Dame with an elbow injury. Rubio performed well in his preseason debut, and because of that, he edges out veterans Dean Lowry and Esezi Otomewo .

 
 Linebackers (9) 
 T.J. Watt , Alex Highsmith , Nick Herbig , Jack Sawyer , Patrick Queen , Payton Wilson , Cole Holcomb , Carson Bruener , Elandon Roberts 

 Roberts' late addition infused a shot of energy into training camp, and he'll be a key player in the Steelers' run defense. Veteran Malik Harrison was unnoticeable during camp, leading to Roberts taking his spot.

 
 Cornerbacks (6) 
 Jalen Ramsey , Joey Porter Jr , Jamel Dean , Asante Samuel Jr ., Daylen Everette , Brandin Echols 

 Half of this group missed significant parts of training camp either on PUP (Ramsey and Porter) or with an injury (Echols). But the Steelers unearthed quality depth in their absence thanks to a standout camp from Samuel. Everette, a rookie, had some growing pains in camp but largely held up against tough competition.

 
 Safeties (3) 
 DeShon Elliott , Jaquan Brisker , Rayshawn Jenkins 

 Keeping the fourth quarterback means making cuts somewhere else on the roster, and with the position flexibility of Ramsey, that spot is safety. Seventh-round pick  Robert Spears-Jennings  benefited from extra snaps in training camp with Elliott slowly working back from last season's knee injury, but the numbers just don't work in his favor. He's a great candidate for the practice squad and could get some game-day elevations to prove his value.

 
 Special teams (3) 
 Chris Boswell  (K), Cameron Johnston  (P), Christian Kuntz  (LS) 

 No changes here. The standard is the standard.
