title: 2026 San Francisco 49ers training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our daily updates from 49ers training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. 49ers reporter Nick Wagoner has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at 49ers camp. What does  Mike Evans  look like as a top receiver on the 49ers? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, including the 49ers' top camp performer and biggest lingering question as preseason games begin.

 
 Camp previews for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from 49ers' camp 
 
 49ers owner Jed York arrested on suspicion of engaging in prostitution 
 Kittle activated from PUP list; McCaffrey returns to practice 
 Shanahan dismisses idea RB McCaffrey sitting out for new deal 
 Can the 49ers depend on rookie WR De'Zhaun Stribling? 
 49ers' Ricky Pearsall has knee surgery, targets 9-month recovery 
 How the 49ers' defense looks different under Raheem Morris 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 25 
 With only a walkthrough and a preseason game left, the 49ers are, for all intents and purposes, done with this year's training camp. They wrapped things up with their final practice on Tuesday and now turn their attention to forming an initial 53-man roster based on how healthy (or not) they are.

 Tuesday's practice offered a good reminder of how much the 49ers have to sort out. They were without 23 players during the session, including new additions to the list such as WR Mike Evans (groin), CB Upton Stout (hip flexor), G Dominick Puni (concussion protocol) and WR Jacob Cowing (groin). And they're still without DE Nick Bosa , though coach Kyle Shanahan said the hope is to have Bosa back at practice next week.

 Making matter more difficult? The Niners need to button things up quickly since they have to have a roster and practice squad in place before leaving for Australia a week from tomorrow.

 "It's one of their bigger challenges, just having to get everyone, get our practice squad ready, all that stuff a lot sooner than other teams are going to have to," Shanahan said.

 More observation: 

 
 TE George Kittle again went through individual drills on the side but did not participate in team periods. They are hoping to get Kittle more involved in practices before leaving for Australia next week to make a better determination on his availability for Week 1. 
 One name that might be worth watching ahead of roster cut-down to 53: LB Larry Worth III . He's been getting a longer look of late, including Tuesday and he had a nice pass breakup against TE Jake Tonges as well. 
 WR De'Zhaun Stribling is still in a no-contact jersey because of a sore shoulder, but it didn't stop him from having another big day in practice. He caught a tough contested deep ball from QB Brock Purdy and held on despite CB Jack Jones and S Marques Sigle ignoring the no contact jersey designation. 
 With the trip down under coming so soon, Shanahan indicated the starters won't play much on Thursday night against the Raiders. Shanahan said the players participating that night will be similar to the first preseason game in which only a handful of projected starters played. 
 

 

 Sunday, Aug. 23 
 The 49ers welcomed tight end George Kittle (Achilles) and running back Christian McCaffrey (tightness) back to practice on Sunday. First, the team activated Kittle from the physically unable to perform list, clearing his path to practice again. About 20 minutes later, McCaffrey trotted on to the field in pads for his first session in a couple of weeks.

 The Niners eased both back in, with Kittle only doing individual drills and McCaffrey taking about seven reps in team drills, including a handful of carries. Regardless, it was a positive step for both in the mission to have them ready for Week 1.

 "It definitely just gives us energy," offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak said. "It just changes things. You have two Hall of Fame caliber players out there who are back out there and getting their work in and they practice at a high standard and they lift everybody up. ... It's good to see them back out there." 

 More observations :

 
 The only new name on the non-participant list was rookie DE Romello Height . He was seen Saturday moving slowly after practice, but it's unclear what he is dealing with at the moment. 
 Practice got a bit animated late in the session when QB Brock Purdy dropped a perfect pass beyond the reach of LB Fred Warner and into the hands of WR  Deebo Samuel Sr . for a big gain over the middle. Purdy apparently took issue with Warner's trash talk after an earlier pass breakup and let him know about it after the completion to Samuel. No hard feelings, though, as Warner and Purdy were seen talking and laughing a few moments later. 
 WR De'Zhaun Stribling and CB Deommodore Lenoir were both back in practice after missing Saturday with a shoulder issue. Lenoir (blue) and Stribling (black) were in no-contact jerseys. 
 CB Upton Stout had an interception against Purdy on what seemed to be a miscommunication with Stribling. The pass went right to Stout, who would have had a long return on it in a real game. 
 Among the kick return combinations they worked on Sunday: RBs Kaelon Black and Jordan James . Both have fresh legs after recently returning from injury and both have stood out in recent practices. 
 Another good day in one-on-one pass rush drills for undrafted DT James Thompson Jr . Thompson might be hard to keep off the initial 53-man roster, both because of his strong camp and because of uncertainty in front of him at the position. 
 

 

 
 Saturday, Aug. 22 
 Wide receiver Mike Evans was back at practice Saturday after leaving Tuesday's session early with quad tightness. The Niners weren't concerned about it at the time and suggested Evans would be back soon, so his presence wasn't a total surprise.

 Evans went on to have a nice practice, connecting with QB Brock Purdy a few times for big gains and catching a short touchdown pass from Purdy in the red zone. RB Christian McCaffrey , meanwhile, did not return to practice from his own bout with tightness -- but he was seen in the weight room going through a workout.

 More observations: 

 
 Coach Kyle Shanahan is basically all the way back to full duties from his car accident, but he took another step Saturday when he was seen calling in plays on the walkie-talkie. It's the first time I've noticed it in this camp (doesn't mean it hasn't happened before), and he didn't do it the whole time, but it is also a sign that the regular season is fast approaching. 
 WR De'Zhaun Stribling and CB Deommodore Lenoir did not practice because of shoulder issues. They're considered day-to-day, according to the team. 
 The Niners welcomed back three potential important contributors from injury Saturday: RB Jordan James (rib), G Dominick Puni (concussion) and DT C.J. West (concussion). WR Malik Turner was also back in the mix, though he did some work on the side after individual. 
 Among the others not practicing after suffering injuries in Thursday's preseason game: LB Nick Martin (hamstring), CB Renardo Green (hamstring) and OL Austen Pleasants (knee). 
 James and rookie RB Kaelon Black have fresh legs and it shows after their returns from injury. Black, in particular, showed off some sure hands in the pass game, one of the questions surrounding him coming out of the draft. 
 Other 49ers I did not see participating today who haven't had any injuries disclosed: LB Jalen Graham , WR Wesley Grimes (was seen with a wrap on his hand), RB Zamir White and DL Xavier Thomas .
